For an Al (70 nm)/Si structure, Fourier fits of synthetic TDTR phase signals give $κ_{\rm app}$ of Si from about 93 to 360 W/(m K) for different interfacial transmission spectra, and $κ_{\rm app}$ correlates with the heat-flux-weighted $Λ_ω$ of the transmitted phonons. Thus, $κ_{\rm app}$ from thermoreflectance reflects not only the substrate thermal properties but also the phonon spectrum injected across the transducer interface.

items.title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
items.summary: Stabilizer-based subspace methods can substantially reduce the quantum resources required for electronic structure calculations, but the resulting projection neglects Hamiltonian couplings to configurations outside the retained subspace. In this work, we introduce Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) to recover the associated correlation contributions, using the Contextual Subspace Variational Quantum Eigensolver (CS-VQE) as a representative application. The central idea is to exploit the Pauli terms eliminated by stabilizer projection as perturbative operators that generate an external manifold from the optimized reference state. Their energetic contributions are evaluated using an Epstein-Nesbet-type second-order correction or a resolvent-based formulation that retains couplings within the external space. By exploiting the factorized structure of the stabilizer-constrained reference state, the required matrix elements can be evaluated through Pauli expectation values on the reduced contextual register without explicitly reconstructing the full-space wave function. Molecular benchmarks demonstrate substantial reductions in projection-induced energy errors, allowing chemical precision to be achieved with fewer contextual qubits in several cases. These results establish stabilizer-guided perturbation theory as a promising strategy for improving the accuracy of resource-efficient quantum chemistry calculations.

items.title: Computation in flight through precision-processed optical fiber
items.summary: In distributed sensing and computing systems, optoelectronic conversion, buffering, and scheduling can make data movement a bottleneck. We propose FBG-CA, a passive computing module fabricated by automated through-coating inscription of weak fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs). The spatially distributed FBGs reflect, delay, and accumulate temporal samples to produce a convolution output in the backward direction, while the forward signal carries the original data stream to a remote receiver. This enables transmission and convolution within the same optical propagation event. To mitigate finite reflectivity resolution and fabrication deviations, we combine quantization-aware training with sharpness-aware minimization. Over 1440 m of computing fiber, the single-wavelength implementation achieves a convolution correlation coefficient of 0.987, classification accuracies of 87.90% on MNIST and 79.07% on MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, and an estimated throughput of 288 GOPS. With approximately 20% forward-power reduction (0.97 dB) across the FBG sections, the recovered MNIST images achieve a mean structural similarity index of 0.9930, and the recovered MIT-BIH heartbeat waveforms have a mean squared error of 0.005826. Using four wavelength-division-multiplexed channels over 144 m of computing fiber, FBG-CA achieves 92.25% accuracy on four-class Fashion-MNIST and an estimated throughput of 115.2 GOPS. An architecture-level projection indicates an intrinsic throughput density of 1.6 POPS/m for eight wavelengths at 100 GBaud per wavelength. These results demonstrate passive, wavelength-scalable computation-in-flight in optical fiber.

items.title: A response-based self-energy from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory and its reduction to GW, GW+SOSEX, and GF2
items.summary: We construct a frequency-dependent one-particle correlation self-energy by coupling a reference Green's function to the neutral excitation response obtained from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory with singles and doubles (EOM-CCSD). Direct, mixed direct-antisymmetrized, and fully antisymmetrized choices of the external interaction vertices define three approximations, all admitting an explicit spectral representation without numerical frequency integration. In the bare-state limit, the mixed and fully antisymmetrized forms recover second-order Green's-function theory (GF2), whereas the direct form retains only its ring contribution. With a direct random-phase approximation (RPA) response, the direct and mixed forms reduce to $G_0W_0$ and $G_0W_0$ plus second-order screened exchange (SOSEX), respectively. For molecular ionization potentials, replacing the RPA response by EOM-CCSD generally lowers the ionization energies, whereas introducing exchange at one external vertex raises them. These substantial opposing effects partially compensate, although the mixed approximation does not systematically improve upon conventional $G_0W_0$, either against IP-EOM-CCSD or QUESTDB reference energies (aug-cc-pVDZ mean absolute errors relative to the QUESTDB theoretical best estimates: 0.45 vs 0.36~eV). A third-order perturbative analysis reveals that the three approximations retain different contributions and weights of particle-hole diagrams while omitting explicit particle-particle and hole-hole ladder contributions and the static self-energy. In particular, the fully antisymmetrized form recovers GF2 at second order but assigns incorrect weights to its retained third-order diagrams. These findings highlight the importance of a balanced treatment of screening and vertex corrections in constructing accurate self-energy approximations.

items.title: Stellar Temporal Intensity Interferometry with Adaptive Optics at the Palomar Observatory
items.summary: Spatial intensity interferometry has seen a major resurgence in astronomy due to its immunity to atmospheric phase turbulence, but its temporal counterpart - a cornerstone of quantum optics - has remained largely unexplored for astronomical sources. Here, we demonstrate that high-visibility temporal photon bunching signatures from stellar sources are now accessible by combining ultra-narrowband spectral filtering with high-speed single-photon counting detectors. Leveraging the adaptive optics architecture at the Palomar Observatory, we report the first observation of resolved stellar temporal photon bunching, with a peak of $g^{(2)}(τ=0) = 1.3 \pm 0.1$, from the red supergiant $α$ Her. This advance establishes stellar temporal intensity interferometry as a viable observational modality, bridging quantum optics with high-resolution stellar astrophysics.

items.title: Growing Knot Embeddings into Spherical Graphs
items.summary: Knotted structures occur throughout soft matter and biology, where topological constraints can shape relaxation and spatial organization. Here, we introduce a computational construction that maps a specific 3D knot embedding to a graph embedded on the sphere through growth and interfacial-energy relaxation. For standard 3D embeddings of prime knots with at most seven crossings, we obtain a family of growth-based graphs that generally differ from the corresponding Tait graphs. We further identify an empirical growth-graph reconstruction rule based on polygonal regions with alternating crossing structure in a knot diagram. Non-minimal diagrams demonstrate that these graphs are not knot invariants, while selected connected sums suggest that graph features associated with their prime factors can remain recognizable. Determining how these graphs transform under isotopy may reveal invariant features, which we leave for future study.

items.title: Efficient Spectra and Dynamics with Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks
items.summary: We present a tangent-space Chebyshev method (TaChe), which combines tree tensor network states with Chebyshev recursion and maximum entropy spectral analysis in a tree tensor network tangent space, for quantum many-body spectra and dynamics. Implemented tensor network state calculations in the tangent space of the ground state, the core advantage of TaChe is that it can substantially reduce the computational complexity, memory usage, and numerical instability associated with tensor network state compression. Implemented on the GPU platform, it produces accurate spectra with speedups of up to $46.8$ over the previous Chebyshev tensor network method and $13.7$ over one-site time-dependent variational principle propagation in the reported benchmarks. Applications to acetonitrile, thermal aggregate emission, finite-temperature charge transport on a \(6\times6\) lattice, and internal conversion in aggregates of up to 100 molecules demonstrate the efficiency and versatility of TaChe in simulating complex molecular systems.

items.title: High-rate accumulation of ${8.9\times10^9}$ positrons using a linac-driven buffer-gas trap combined with a SiC remoderator
items.summary: We report the accumulation of $(8.9 \pm 0.9)\times10^9$ positrons in less than 35 minutes in a Penning--Malmberg trap connected to the GBAR electron-linac-based positron source. To our knowledge, this exceeds the largest previously reported trapped-positron population by more than a factor of two and was achieved at an 18-fold higher average accumulation rate of $4.5\times10^6$~e$^+$/s. The accumulated positron clouds are intended for the creation of dense positronium targets to produce keV-antihydrogen beams by charge exchange with antiprotons delivered by the CERN AD/ELENA facility. The system combines a low-energy electron linac, a modified Surko-type buffer-gas trap enhanced by a silicon carbide remoderator, and a high-field Penning--Malmberg trap operated as a positron accumulator. Time-resolved annihilation measurements provide insight into the capture and cooling dynamics, while comparisons of CO$_2$ and SF$_6$ show that the trapping signal reaches saturation at lower gas pressures with SF$_6$. Measurements show that the SiC-remoderator-based trapping scheme more than doubles the trapping efficiency, contributing to a more than threefold increase in the positron accumulation rate compared with the original configuration.

items.title: Accelerating interatomic potential development through student-driven exploration and reliability-aware distillation
items.summary: Conventional two-stage distillation first establishes a teacher through teacher-driven configuration exploration, a costly first stage for complex materials, and then uses its predictions to supervise students, potentially propagating teacher-label errors. Here, we propose distillation-driven teacher-student co-evolution (DICE), which uses a fast student to accelerate configuration exploration and replaces the fixed teacher-to-student sequence with alternating student and teacher updates. A representation-based support-assessment algorithm routes high-support configurations to teacher labelling and selects low-support configurations for density functional theory (DFT) calculations to update the teacher, thereby reducing the risk of teacher-label error propagation to students. Across Al2O3 (structural ceramics), yttria-stabilised zirconia (solid electrolytes) and MIL-120(Al) (a metal-organic framework), DICE develops reliable compact potentials using only 140-494 target DFT reference configurations per system; total recorded student exploration times per system are just 2.6-5.1% of the corresponding teacher-driven estimates. Combining computational efficiency with broad applicability across diverse material systems, DICE provides a practical route to developing reliable compact interatomic potentials.

items.title: Polarization switching of double azimuthal backflow in two transverse orbital angular momentum superpositions
items.summary: Optical backflow in the azimuthal direction can be generated by the interference of two rotating-wave structured light beams with distinct transverse topological charges and equal intensity. Here we show that the interference reverses both azimuthal components of the Poynting and the canonical momenta. Although these two momenta are not generally tied, they reverse jointly here: both acquire azimuthal backflow in a common angular sector, while their radial intervals can differ. The double backflow is switched solely by the polarizations of the two beams, without amplitude tuning. A single polarization overlap enters the interference terms of both momenta but not the single-beam terms of either, so that matched polarizations switch the double backflow on whereas mismatched ones switch it off. The double backflow is periodic in the azimuthal direction, with its angular period locked to the topological charge difference and independent of the individual charges. Our results establish a vectorial mechanism for polarization-gated azimuthal backflow, with potential applications in polarization-switchable optical manipulation.

items.title: Geospatial foundation models and deep learning for climate resilience: a review of transfer, uncertainty and decision readiness
items.summary: Geospatial foundation models can reuse information learned from large Earth-observation archives, but their value for climate resilience depends on whether that information transfers to unfamiliar events, regions and observing conditions. This review connects advances in deep learning with the evidence needed for hazard monitoring and early warning. A descriptive audit of 137 full-text hazard-application studies is interpreted alongside a separate corpus of 37 model and benchmark records. Ninety-eight application studies reported an out-of-distribution experiment, whereas headline evaluations included held-out events in 31 studies, regions in 25 and sensors in only two. None of the ten studies coded for geospatial foundation-model fine-tuning used sensor holdout as a headline test. Uncertainty-related methods were recorded in 16 studies, including two with explicitly calibrated probabilistic output. These overlapping counts describe evaluation practice within the coded corpus, not a ranking of model families. We distinguish Earth-observation representation learning from atmospheric forecasting and examine how labels, observability, forecast lead time and decision requirements constrain their contribution across flood, wildfire, drought, heat, cryosphere and cascading-hazard applications. We then develop a decision-backward evaluation framework: define the action and information available when it must be taken, reproduce the relevant shift, retain a matched task-specific baseline, and report misses, false alarms, reliability and end-to-end latency. The framework turns transferability from a broad model claim into a testable requirement for climate adaptation and risk management.

items.title: Strain-driven terahertz phase modulation in piezoelectric and nonlinear optical crystals: mechanisms, material developments, and modulation strategies
items.summary: Terahertz (THz) technology has witnessed notable developments in sensing, spectroscopy, imaging, and wireless communication which have increased the demand for high-performance THz modulators. Among the various approaches for controlling the THz waves, the application of external stimuli such as optical pumping and thermal or electric fields is widely employed as a promising strategy for modulation. This review focuses on recent advances in THz modulation based on different materials including 2D semiconductors and metamaterials with attention to their response under external stimuli. In addition, strain-driven THz modulation in non-centrosymmetric piezoelectric materials including organic and semi-organic crystals is examined with an emphasis on their ability to establish strong coupling between propagating THz waves and lattice vibrations under piezoelectric resonance conditions. We further highlight earlier reports on strain-driven THz modulation in lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and critically assess the potential of several other nonlinear optical crystals exhibiting piezoelectric resonance peaks suitable for strain-driven THz modulation. An overview of THz modulators integrated with tunable materials is presented highlighting their operating principles and key performance metrics comprising modulation speed, bandwidth, modulation depth and insertion loss.

items.title: COSIMA Cookbook: a community-driven resource for ocean and sea-ice modelling science
items.summary: The COSIMA Cookbook is an open educational resource for analysing ocean and sea-ice model output in Jupyter notebooks. It has been developed by the Consortium for Ocean--Sea Ice Modelling in Australia (COSIMA) as a community resource for researchers, students, and practitioners working with large gridded datasets, especially output from the ACCESS ocean--sea ice model configurations. The Cookbook is organised around a gastronomy theme: ``Cooking Tutorials'' teach generic, transferable techniques for handling model output, while "Easy Recipes", "Advanced Recipes" and "Regional Specialties" are self-contained notebooks that show how to perform concrete diagnostics and analyses. Along the way, the notebooks demonstrate open-source tools for the scientific analysis of large data, including Intake catalogues, Xarray, Dask, xgcm, xESMF, eofs, Parcels, matplotlib and Cartopy. The Cookbook addresses the steep entry cost of analysing climate model output: it packages expert, often tacit, knowledge into complete, well-documented and reusable workflows, in the same medium in which researchers actually work. It is developed openly on GitHub, is published as a documentation website, and is continuously reviewed and extended by its community through pull requests and regular hackathons. The easy access to data and analysis it provides has contributed to the international adoption of ACCESS ocean and sea-ice model configurations, and has facilitated well over 100 peer-reviewed papers and more than 20 PhD projects.

items.title: A Unified Energy-Density Framework for Moiré Interface Energetics and Mechanics
items.summary: The mechanical response of moiré interfaces depends on how atomic registry combines with contact size and boundary geometry. An analytical description must retain this discrete lattice information while connecting microscopic interactions to the energetics of finite contacts. Here, we develop a unified energy-density framework for rigid van der Waals interfaces by expressing registry-dependent pair potentials and atomic densities in reciprocal space. The resulting formulation accommodates different lattice bases and atomic species, linking single-atom and molecular adsorption to infinite bilayers and finite crystalline contacts. Explicit expressions for circular and regular polygonal flakes separate the area contribution from boundary-dependent terms and connect microscopic corrugation coefficients to energy barriers, rotational torques, and interlayer shear stiffnesses. The boundary analysis recovers the quarter-power area scaling of the barrier envelope for circular flakes and distinguishes bounded oscillations from square-root area scaling for polygonal contacts according to edge orientation. A dimensionless criterion characterizes the polygon-to-circle crossover in terms of moiré wavelength, flake size, and side number. Direct-summation benchmarks support the finite-domain expressions, while calculations for two-dimensional ice on graphene demonstrate the corresponding boundary-scaling trends in a molecular lattice. Applications to interlayer shear and graphite compression connect the same microscopic interaction description to tangential and normal mechanical responses. The framework establishes an analytical connection between microscopic registry, moiré periodicity, and finite-domain geometry, providing a basis for understanding and tailoring the energetics and mechanics of van der Waals contacts.

items.title: Plasma-enabled magnet-free LSW search for eV-scale axions with laser-stimulated regeneration
items.summary: In conventional light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) experiments, strong magnetic fields mediate the conversion of photons into axions and their subsequent reconversion into photons. At eV-scale axion masses, however, photon--axion phase mismatch causes these conversions to lose coherence, substantially reducing the experimental sensitivity. We propose a magnet-free LSW scheme that addresses this limitation via plasma-based axion generation and laser-stimulated regeneration. At low laser intensity, a two-color dispersion-matched source generates axions in a narrow mass range set by the plasma dispersion. At relativistic laser intensity, a single-pulse plasma-broadened source generates axions over a broad mass range, as shown by particle-in-cell simulations. The Fourier spectrum of the source term $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ broadens around the laser branch, consistent with mixing between the laser and low-frequency plasma waves. For axion detection behind the wall, a counter-propagating laser stimulates axion decay into a detectable signal photon and a second photon emitted into the laser mode, with the laser frequency chosen to satisfy phase matching. For representative parameters, the requirement of at least one regenerated photon yields projected upper limits on the axion-photon coupling on the order $10^{-7}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ over $m_a=0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{eV}$.

items.title: Flow-induced vibration of an array of circular cylinders in a square enclosure due to thermal buoyancy
items.summary: Flow-induced oscillations of heated cylinder arrays in a square enclosure driven solely by natural convection are investigated in the current study at Prandtl number of 7 and Raleigh number of $10^7$ (based on side of square enclosure). This is accomplished by a coupled thermal-fluid-structure-interaction formulation based on body-fitted arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework, implemented using variational finite element methodology. Study on stationary array shows asymmetry in the $3\times 3$ configuration, along with a non-dimensional wall-gap plume oscillation frequency of 0.183 on the left column cylinders. When elastically mounted, these cylinders synchronize and lock-in with the frequency at reduced velocity of 15.7. The remaining cylinders undergo broadband buffeting that grows monotonically with reduced velocity and exceeds the synchronized response. The $4\times 4$ array shows symmetric behavior with no synchronization. The response is observed to be forced buffeting for all the cylinders, and dominated by the slow plume forcing for the inner column cylinders. The motion of the cylinders also influence the heat transfer characteristics. The $3\times 3$ array shows negligible change in heat transfer for the whole array, while measurable enhancement is observed for $4\times 4$ array.

items.title: A Novel Multi-Target Approach for simultaneous enhancement of brightness, intensity, and bi-spectral performance of cold neutron sources
items.summary: Increasing the brightness of cold neutron beams is a central objective in modern cold neutron source development, since it largely governs the sample intensity for high-resolution neutron instruments. Raising accelerator beam power is constrained by the target heat-removal limit of 0.5-1 kW/cm2, and increasing the moderator length beyond about 20-30 cm becomes inefficient owing to the finite mean free path of cold neutrons. We propose reversing the conventional design logic: rather than tailoring the cryogenic moderator to a fixed target-premoderator source, we tailor the thermal-neutron source geometry to a high-performance moderator configuration. The concept is realized as a staircase moderator assembly of several shorter compressed moderators, each with its own target-premoderator unit, which distributes neutron production among multiple units and thus enables higher accelerator powers while preserving the brightness advantages of compressed moderators. This approach can provide additional brightness and intensity gains relative to a single low-dimensional or conventional voluminous moderator at the desired transverse beam size and may naturally generate bi-spectral neutron beams, thereby extending the dynamic range of neutron instruments.

items.title: Relativistic Harmonic Generation in Spatiotemporal Plasma Photonic Crystals
items.summary: Spatiotemporal photonic crystals offer a route to controlling the frequency, momentum, and energy of light. Extending this capability to relativistic laser intensities calls for a plasma-based platform. Here we propose a spatiotemporal plasma photonic crystal (SPPC) formed at a solid surface driven by intense pump pulses, with a separate probe interacting with the resulting modulation. The spatial and temporal periodicity of the SPPC determines the allowed harmonic frequencies and emission angles, while its complex Floquet bands explain how the probe draws energy from the modulation. Beyond harmonic generation, this picture predicts wavelength-dependent probe amplification as the probe accesses amplifying modes of the SPPC, providing an experimentally testable connection between the band structure and energy transfer. Agreement with particle-in-cell simulations supports this interpretation.

items.title: Integrable discretization of the Maxwell-Bloch equations
items.summary: Numerical schemes for the Maxwell-Bloch equations keep the length of the Bloch vector but not the integrable structure, so that solitons are only approximate solutions. We write an integrable discretization, in both time and space, of these equations for a complex field in a resonant two-level medium in the physical variables and use it as a numerical scheme. The lattice follows from a discrete Lax pair with the analytic structure of the continuous one; an auxiliary field variable is fixed by an isospectral normalization, and the resulting scheme is explicit, a $2\times2$ similarity transformation of the density matrix per grid node. It conserves the length of every Bloch vector and satisfies an exact energy balance between field and medium. The lattice coincides with a known fully discrete integrable system, which we use to obtain closed-form solitons and breathers; they are reflectionless potentials with energy $16\sum_j\mathrm{Im}\,λ_j$ and converge to the McCall-Hahn soliton and Lamb's breather. Inhomogeneous broadening is included through ordered sublayers that keep integrability. On a finite time window the scattering data evolve by a closed map, with the final state of the medium given by the data at one point of the spectral plane. On the infinite line, if the medium returns to its ground state behind the pulse (which we show on the first row and observe numerically on later rows), the transmission coefficient is conserved and the reflection coefficient evolves linearly, with the multiplier of the linearized lattice. As a numerical method the lattice is explicit and second order, with a cost per accuracy comparable to that of Cayley and exponential-midpoint schemes, and an area-preserving input map with a calibrated medium coupling makes it exact for a chosen soliton.

items.title: Designing Incoherent Multispectral Diffractive Optical Networks for Satellite Image Classification
items.summary: Optical neural networks and diffractive optical computing provide a promising route for performing task-specific inference with high parallelism and lightweight electronic post-processing. These advantages are especially attractive for multispectral satellite imaging, where conventional workflows rely on transmitting high-dimensional image cubes to the ground for downstream electronic analysis. Here, we introduce a computationally efficient surrogate model-guided framework for designing incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks that directly output class probabilities onboard, eliminating the need to capture and transfer the full multispectral data cube for ground-side inference. We first train a physically compatible surrogate model, represented by a non-negative fully connected model that accommodates a generalized detector readout, yielding a task-specific non-negative multispectral intensity transformation that can be transferred to an optical processor. We then synthesize its diffractive counterpart through data-free point-spread-function-based optimization under spatially incoherent illumination. Using this approach, we numerically demonstrate a six-spectral-channel diffractive classifier for tri-class satellite-scene recognition, achieving a blind-testing accuracy of 79.8% for artificial surface, water body, and vegetated land images, closely approaching the 81.8% accuracy of its surrogate. We further demonstrate a more compact three-spectral-channel design that numerically achieves 72.7% blind-testing accuracy, compared with 75.1% for its corresponding surrogate model. This surrogate model-guided strategy provides a practical pathway for designing compact, task-specific incoherent multispectral optical processors for resource-constrained remote-sensing inference.

items.title: Jordan-Frame Dynamics of Curvature Inflation: A Derivative Expansion of the Friedmann Constraint
items.summary: We derive a slow-roll approximation for the Jordan-frame Hubble rate $H_J$ in metric $f(R)$ gravity. A derivative expansion of the vacuum Friedmann constraint to third order gives $\dot H_J$ as a function of $H_J$. In the Starobinsky model we also show that the difference in $\dot H_J$ between two expanding solutions decreases as they pass through successively lower values of $H_J$, and that a signed square root of $H_J$ evolves smoothly through the zeros that follow inflation. We test the approximation in a regularized inverse-logarithmic $R^2$ model and in $R+α^{p-1}R^p$, taking the pivot from the exact background 60 Einstein-frame e-folds before the end of inflation. For the inverse-logarithmic coupling $δ=3$, the third-order approximation reproduces $\dot H_J$ at the pivot with a relative error of $3\times10^{-8}$. Integrating the approximate branch between the pivot and exit values of $H_J$ taken from the exact background gives 59.98 e-folds, compared with 60 on the exact trajectory. At the six couplings $δ=0,1,\ldots,5$, the absolute difference from the numerical mode result is below $1.1\times10^{-5}$ in the scalar tilt $n_s$, and the relative difference is below $0.0052\%$ in the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. Here the second-order spectral formulas account for nearly all of this difference. For $p=1.8$ the approximation itself adds to the error, which becomes $3.9\times10^{-5}$ in $n_s$ and $0.047\%$ in $r$. For $δ=3$, perturbative scalaron decay into a minimally coupled Higgs doublet places the pivot 51.59 e-folds before the end of inflation and gives $n_s=0.9690$ and $r=0.0067$. At fixed $αμ_0^2=0.006065$ and with the same decay rate prescription, $δ\simeq8.7$ gives the central $n_s$ value inferred from ACT DR6, Planck, CMB lensing and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. This comparison uses the published one-dimensional constraint.

items.title: Thin-Film AlN Microbolometer for Very-Long-Wave Infrared Detection
items.summary: We demonstrate a suspended thin-film aluminum nitride (AlN) microbolometer for narrowband very-long-wave infrared detection. The device uses a 100 nm-thick AlN membrane suspended above a Pt back reflector by a 1 $μ$m air gap. Resonant absorption near 15.4 $μ$m is set by the AlN transverse optical phonon and is strengthened by suspension above the reflector. A periodic perforation pattern reduces membrane thermal mass, facilitates release, and tunes the effective optical thickness without requiring a thinner deposited film. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) reflection measurements on the released bolometer show approximately 95% peak cavity absorptance near 15.4 $μ$m with a 0.772 $μ$m FWHM. DC resistance measurements under tunable infrared illumination verify bolometric operation, with a peak normalized resistive responsivity of 252 ppm/mW at 15.48 $μ$m. This platform can enable compact wavelength-selective thermal detectors for multispectral imaging, on-chip infrared spectroscopy, and chemical sensing.

items.title: A Steady Theory for Highly Unsteady Thin Airfoil Motions
items.summary: A generalized steady thin airfoil theory is built not from steady flow, but from flows in which there exists a frame of reference where the absolute vorticity field is steady. We specialize this general idea to construct a foliation of a domain of phase space for thin airfoil motions in which staying on a leaf of the foliation maintains zero absolute vorticity in the fluid indefinitely. The phase space is described by the airfoil's total rotation rate, speed, and angle of attack. It is found using this definition that one of the preeminent unsteady stall conditions is equivalent to the traditional steady stall condition for this class of flows, various other classical results can be re-interpreted as steady in the absolute vorticity field, and insight is also provided into the surprising experimental results of McGowan et al. (AIAA J. 49, 2011). We show parts of existing quasi-steady flow and Theodorsen unsteady flow theory can be built from a planar approximation of our foliation, making the quasi-steady extension of our theory trivial, and suggesting how an unsteady extension can be created as well. Furthermore, pure unsteady effects in the new theory amount to a transversal of the leaves, occupying just one dimension, inviting interesting prospects for future experimental and theoretical work.

items.title: Magnetic Lifting of BIC Symmetry Protection Enables Nonreciprocal Beam Steering and Angular Information Encoding
items.summary: Symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum (SP-BICs) offer exceptional optical confinement but remain nonradiative. Here, we demonstrate that magnetically lifting their protecting symmetry enables nonreciprocal beam steering with intrinsic angular information encoding. In a magneto-optical photonic crystal slab, an in-plane magnetic field converts an SP-BIC into a radiative quasi-BIC and, together with vertical dielectric asymmetry, continuously displaces the associated band extremum away from the Gamma point. The steered beam exhibits two independent locking relations: its wavelength is locked to the elevation angle, while its polarization orientation is locked to the azimuthal angle. These relations embed complementary spectral and polarization information into the scanning beam, providing additional sensing channels for multidimensional LiDAR. Moreover, the nonreciprocal dispersion gives different resonance frequencies at opposite wave vectors, supporting resonant emission at +k while back-reflected light at the same frequency is off resonance at -k, opening a route to intrinsic self-isolation and reduced optical feedback. These findings establish a unified framework connecting magnetic beam steering, angular information encoding, and nonreciprocal feedback suppression, with prospects for compact reconfigurable light sources and integrated optical engines.

items.title: What Do Co-Folding Models Learn? Insights from Enhanced Transition Path Sampling
items.summary: Co-folding models are diffusion-based generative models that sample biomolecular complexes from distributions learned on a large corpus of experimental data. Although these models are powerful for structure prediction, it remains unclear whether the conformational ensembles they learn resemble physically meaningful statistical ensembles. To understand what these models learn, we introduce transition path sampling (TPS), which uses Markov chain Monte Carlo over denoising trajectories to sample the learned distribution. Because its Monte Carlo trajectories resemble biomolecular dynamics, TPS couples directly with enhanced-sampling techniques to recover the full conformational ensemble. Applied to Boltz-2, enhanced TPS reveals physical conformational changes biased toward crystal-like states near the training data, indicating both learned physics and memorization. These results suggest new ways to evaluate and improve co-folding models by jointly assessing structural recovery, proximity to training data, and conformational ensembles.

items.title: Solar System and Atomic Clock Bounds on Locally Coupled Swampland Scalars
items.summary: We study how local measurements constrain light scalar fields that are relevant in late time cosmic acceleration and are often discussed in connection with swampland criteria. Starting from a scalar-tensor framework, we define the swampland slope and curvature variables in the canonically normalized Einstein frame and relate them to Solar System tracking, Lunar Laser Ranging, equivalence principle tests and atomic clock comparisons. These measurements do not constrain the scalar velocity by itself, but products of that velocity with microscopic couplings to matter, gravity and atomic parameters. For coupling directions visible to local experiments, the scalar is driven into an ultra slow present regime. This severely restricts the possibility of realizing an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ de Sitter gradient through unscreened visible sector couplings alone. The refined de Sitter alternative remains possible, but in the single field hilltop realization it requires proximity to the maximum or a tuned suppression of the growing mode.

items.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
items.summary: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on single-family, fixed-domain datasets that cannot test the minimum bar for an aerodynamic foundation model: predicting CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (URANS) solutions with a transition model across seven geometry families, eight enclosures, and Reynolds numbers from $10^3$ to $10^8$. Each sample poses a well-posed PDE problem as a solver receives it: boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values, and fluid properties. The 2,816 time-mean-stable samples form the canonical benchmark: two tasks, mean engineering metrics with an overall flow score $S_{\mathrm{flow}}$ (1.000 for uniform inlet flow), and 22 frozen geometry-disjoint splits holding out shapes, enclosures, boundary-condition layouts, and Reynolds ranges. On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's mean velocity error from 89.8% to 15.2% of inlet speed (uniform flow: 44.0%; $S_{\mathrm{flow}} = 0.290$). ISLA, a boundary-driven transformer, reaches 8.2% ($S_{\mathrm{flow}} = 0.153$; 0.123 with boundary targets), about 6 times mesh-refinement sensitivity. On shared test samples, holding out a geometry family barely changes ISLA's mean velocity error, whereas holding out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts raises it 3.8 to 8.4 times. The dataset is public; the scoring code will be released.

items.title: Comparative qualification of advanced plasma-facing materials for fusion pilot plants through public- and private-sector experiments in DIII-D
items.summary: A coordinated DIII-D campaign involving four private fusion developers and 12 participating institutions comparatively assessed 44 advanced plasma-facing materials, including the first DIII-D divertor exposure of neutron-irradiated W, to support fusion pilot plant wall and divertor material qualification. Samples were exposed using the Divertor Materials Evaluation System (DiMES) under Ohmic, L-mode, and H-mode conditions with edge-localized modes, at 0.2-2.5 MW m$^{-2}$ on flush geometries and 10-15 MW m$^{-2}$ on 10$^\circ$ angled geometries. Engineered tungsten architectures retained integrity; long-fiber Wf/W showed the clearest crack-arrest behavior. W-Re and K-doped W showed near-ITER-W-like responses, while additively manufactured W-Ta showed heat-flux-sensitive mass losses of 0.64 mg for the flat sample and 2.19-2.87 mg for angled samples. After irradiation to 0.3 dpa at 550$^\circ$C, neutron-irradiated ITER-grade W retained 2.8 times more deuterium than pristine W, while TiB$2$ showed the lowest D$2$ release in the Ohmic set. VTaHfMo was the most stable refractory multi-principal-element alloy. NbC and (Nb${0.5}$Ta${0.5}$)C retained integrity with 0.02-0.03 mg mass loss, whereas ZrC lost 7 mg. CVD SiC retained macroscopic integrity but exhibited an effective Si erosion yield of 0.5, about 5-10 times above prior DIII-D trends. Renewable boron pebble rods underwent plasma-driven recession; 13% of released boron was ionized near the outer strike point and up to 50% was recovered locally. Initial in-situ Cr gross-erosion measurements yielded effective erosion yields of order $10^{-2}$. Together, these results provide cross-material benchmarks for fusion pilot plant down-selection and future AI/ML-assisted plasma-facing-material development.

items.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
items.summary: Symmetry is a foundational principle of physics: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the coordinate frame, unit system, or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet today's leading neural surrogates lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation), rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs. Because the boundary determines the interior solution, ISLA encodes the posed boundary once into learned slices and evaluates arbitrary interior points independently through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel. Inputs are nondimensionalized in scales computed from the boundary, sums over boundary cells are area-weighted quadratures that converge under mesh refinement, and geometry enters only as distances and relative angles to equivariant slice anchors, making the model equivariant to rigid motions and reflections up to optional token subsampling and tree clustering. On AeroZoo, 2,816 3D flows spanning diverse geometries, poses, physical scales, and boundary conditions, ISLA's mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are 1.9 and 2.2 times lower than the best baseline's. On full AirfRANS, ISLA is second only to an explicit boundary-integral network (GLOBE), with errors 1.6 to 2.6 times lower than the better of Transolver's and GeoTransolver's in every field.

items.title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
items.summary: The aerodynamic performance of motorsport vehicles relies on understanding the unsteady flow dynamics around complex geometries at high Reynolds numbers. Extracting the dominant 3D coherent structures from high-fidelity simulations is often intractable due to the high dimensionality of the state-space, and standard modal decompositions, such as proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), do not give interpretable meaning to the temporal dynamics of the modes. This study demonstrates a scalable POD and Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) method, implemented in the open-source pyLOM framework, that can identify coherent structures and their temporal dynamics in high-fidelity simulations of Formula 1 aerodynamics, specifically the Imperial Front Wing (IFW), a publicly available benchmark based on the McLaren MP4-17D, at Reynolds number $Re = 2.2 \times 10^5$. DMD is applied to large eddy simulation (LES) results of the flow field that is resolved using spectral/hp element method via Nektar++, producing $49.72 \times 10^6$ degrees of freedom at polynomial order p=4. The simulation captures four dominant vortical structures (endplate, canard, main, and footplate), with time-averaged force coefficients showing 2.24% and 2.87% differences in $C_L$ and $C_D$ compared to the reference data. DMD extracts the frequencies, amplitudes and damping ratios of the coherent structures, and modes at chord-based Strouhal numbers of 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 are associated, through point-probe spectra, with the main-element laminar separation bubble, canard vortex core pulsation and endplate vortex meander, respectively. The DMD allows for both a model reduction technique and a compression scheme, here reducing approximately 6 TB of snapshots to 200 GB of modal data.

items.title: Pseudo-Altermagnetism in Non-Hermitian Systems
items.summary: Altermagnetism has attracted growing attention, and its analogs have been actively explored across classical platforms. Here, we introduce pseudo-altermagnetism in non-Hermitian systems, where balanced gain and loss plays the role of the altermagnetic spin, and the opposite gain and loss sublattices are related by an antiunitary symmetry $O$ with $O\bm k\neq \bm k$ for generic momentum $\bm k$. Using a two-dimensional non-Hermitian system with $O=C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$ symmetry as a representative example, we find that pseudo-altermagnetism not only leads to a momentum-dependent gain and loss distribution analogous to the momentum-dependent spin splitting of altermagnets, but also exhibits intrinsic non-Hermitian properties. The bands of $C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$-invariant non-Hermitian systems are either isolated or paired by $C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$, and both cases are guaranteed to host movable but unremovable nodal structures, characterized by the zeros of two distinct quantities. An isolated band exhibits two movable but unremovable Hermitian spectral lines, whose generic points are not invariant under $C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$, in sharp contrast to the conventional Hermitian spectra enforced only at the fixed points of an antiunitary symmetry. The paired bands, in turn, feature a movable but unremovable nodal network formed by the union of real-part and imaginary-part degeneracy lines, whose intersections are generally exceptional points. We further demonstrate these findings in a non-Hermitian photonic crystal. Our results establish a symmetry-based bridge between non-Hermitian physics and altermagnetism, and provide novel mechanisms of Hermitian spectra beyond $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry.

items.title: A Constrained Coupled Cluster Approach for Strongly Correlated Electrons
items.summary: We introduce constrained coupled cluster (cCC), a general framework for imposing arbitrary physical constraints on conventional single-reference coupled cluster amplitudes without rederiving or replacing the underlying coupled cluster residual equations. As a first application, we derive a constraint from the spin-symmetry requirement for an exact wavefunction and demonstrate the resulting approach on strongly correlated problems. Across benchmark Hubbard models, nitrogen and chromium bond breaking, and iron--sulfur cluster spin gaps, the constraint strongly suppresses spin contamination, repairs qualitative failures of conventional coupled cluster, and often brings CCSDT, and in several cases CCSD, into quantitative agreement with exact diagonalization or high-accuracy density matrix renormalization group calculations. The derived constraint adds only a mean-field cost contraction to the coupled cluster calculation and is compatible with any cluster truncation. These results identify numerical constraints as a promising route for extending single-reference coupled cluster machinery into strongly correlated regimes conventionally associated with more complicated electronic structure methods.

items.title: Global Patterns and Drivers of Terrestrial Surface Albedo Dynamics from 2001 to 2025
items.summary: Terrestrial surface albedo is a fundamental determinant of the global radiative balance, yet a spatially integrated understanding of its long-term trajectories and multi-sphere environmental drivers remains lacking. Utilizing MODIS observations (2001-2025), this study integrates Theil-Sen trend analysis, standardized anomaly diagnostics, and a pixel-wise multiple linear regression framework to quantify global albedo dynamics and attribute them to biophysical drivers. Our results reveal that global albedo change is characterized by profound spatial heterogeneity rather than a uniform trend, with 23.3% of the land surface exhibiting significant brightening, while 18.9% showed significant darkening. Multi-driver attribution demonstrates a clear zonal organization of controls: snow cover dominates albedo variability in northern high latitudes (46.9% of classified area), while NDVI (41.0%) and soil moisture (12.1%) govern tropical vegetated regions and moisture-limited transitional zones, respectively. These findings underscore that while terrestrial albedo is a robust indicator of Earth system change, its interpretation depends strongly on regional cryospheric, biophysical, and hydrological contexts.

items.title: Direct, Collision-Operator-Free Simulation of Electron-Ion Transport in Magnetized and Unmagnetized Plasmas
items.summary: Accurate electron-ion collision models are central to predicting transport in fusion and space plasmas, yet collision operators and Monte Carlo collision models assume that a charged particle meets one partner at a time and that its successive encounters are independent. However, an electron that turns back along the magnetic field passes the same ions again. We solve the Newton-Lorentz equations for test electrons among static ions with a prescribed Debye-screened potential. The method combines force summation within an interaction radius, a time-symmetric particle pusher, and adaptive time stepping, enabling stable and scalable simulations in unmagnetized and magnetized plasmas. Using simulation-based measures of momentum relaxation and cross-field diffusion, we compare the simulations with a reference in the same model that treats every encounter as independent. Without a magnetic field the scattering rate reproduces the binary-collision rate for the same potential to within 2%. When the gyroradius is smaller than the Debye length, the scattering rate stays within 10% of the reference, but the cross-field diffusion coefficient exceeds it by a factor that grows with the field, up to 17. The excess comes from repeated passes of the same ions, whose guiding-center displacements add up: when the ions are replaced by new random ones many times per scattering time, so that a returning electron meets different ions, most of the excess disappears. The framework therefore provides a computational benchmark for testing and improving reduced collision operators and transport models.

items.title: The Sustainability Paradox of Biodegradable Packaging Through a Life Cycle Perspective on Chitosan Based Food Packaging
items.summary: Chitosan-based packaging systems are being studied as alternatives to traditional food packaging made from petroleum sources. The research that has been carried out so far has mostly focused on analyzing their material properties, formulation strategies, or biodegradable behavior. However, as a result, there is a gap left in understanding how the upstream impacts affect the functional advantages of food packaging and the end-of-life results of the formulation process. This review evaluates what trade-offs exist as well as what factors affect the sustainability of chitosan-based packages. Beginning with chitin extraction from crustacean waste, key processing steps, including demineralization, deproteinization, and nanoparticle synthesis, are assessed in terms of chemical intensity, energy demand, and associated emissions. Manufacturing routes, including solvent-based and green synthesis approaches, are compared with those of conventional plastics to identify relative environmental burdens. The use phase is analyzed with respect to antimicrobial functionality, shelf life extension, and potential reductions in food waste. End-of-life pathways, including biodegradation and composting, are evaluated alongside uncertainties related to degradation behavior and nanoparticle fate. The review takes into account life-cycle issues and offers a scientifically based viewpoint on how to differentiate between packaging applications whose environmental benefits can be determined and those whose ecological footprint, lack of functionality, and uncertainty regarding disposal make it impossible to assess sustainability.

items.title: Friendship paradoxes in networks
items.summary: Since Scott L. Feld's seminal paper entitled ``Why your friends have more friends than you do'' [Am.~J.~Sociol.~\textbf{96}, 1464 (1991)], the friendship paradox (FP) has been extensively studied in network science and related fields over the last decades. In this paper we survey the literature on the FP and its generalizations. We first introduce definitions and general results of the FPs defined in networks, and then overview their results on model networks. Empirical results using various social network data as well as applications to real-world problems, such as early detection of outbreaks and network sampling, are also summarized. Finally, we conclude by discussing several directions of possible future works.

items.title: Classical diamagnetism: How adiabatic change of field makes it work
items.summary: Many textbooks discuss the diamagnetic response of a ``classical atom'' to a small and slowly (adiabatically) applied magnetic field. Here we show that the small-field assumption is not essential, whereas the slow rate of field change is crucial: it preserves the circular nature of the orbit regardless of the applied field magnitude. The latter property follows from the existence of an adiabatic invariant of electron's motion. Orbit circularity allows us to solve the problem for arbitrarily large fields. Resulting diamagnetic response exhibits symmetries that unexpectedly persist beyond the small-field limit, and provides a nice illustration of the range of applicability of Larmor's theorem.

items.title: Rare Event Analysis via Stochastic Optimal Control
items.summary: Rare events, from biomolecular conformational changes and phase transitions to chemical reactions, are central to many physical systems, yet extremely difficult to study computationally because unbiased simulations seldom produce them. Transition Path Theory provides a rigorous statistical framework for analyzing such events: it characterizes the ensemble of reactive trajectories between two metastable states (reactant and product), and its central object, the committor function (the probability that the system next reaches the product rather than the reactant), encodes essential kinetic and thermodynamic information. We introduce a framework for committor estimation that builds on stochastic optimal control, with a principled formulation that grounds committor learning on capped hitting-time trajectories. In this framework the committor defines a feedback control, proportional to the gradient of its logarithm, that steers trajectories toward the reactive region, enabling sampling of reactive paths. As practical algorithms, we develop two training losses: a heuristic on-policy direct backpropagation loss and a principled off-policy Value Matching loss, for which we establish first-order optimality guarantees. Being off-policy, Value Matching can leverage simulated trajectories from alternative sampling processes and reuse them from a replay buffer, which enables efficient learning. In particular, we derive a reactive current-preserving sampling process that can accelerate exploration. On reversible and non-reversible dynamics, the framework yields more accurate committor estimates, reaction rates, and transition path samples than existing methods.

items.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
items.summary: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

items.title: Quantum frequency comb with pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading in a lithium niobate microresonator
items.summary: Integrated quantum photonics requires bright, high-fidelity photon-pair sources capable of spectral multiplexing, correlation control, and circuit-compatible extraction. Cavity-enhanced spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) increases pair generation, but triply resonant operation imposes stringent pump-signal-idler spectral-alignment constraints. Moreover, the trade-off between intrinsic generation and coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) does not capture the usable output flux, which depends on photon extraction. Here, we demonstrate a single-pass-pumped, resonator-enhanced quantum frequency comb (QFC) source based on a periodically poled lithium niobate photonic-crystal Fabry-P$é$rot microresonator. The device yields intrinsic and loaded brightnesses of 69.9 and 1.88 MHz/$μ$W, respectively, and a maximum CAR of 16,000. Frequency-resolved measurements reveal 461 cavity-defined bins spanning 1495-1570 nm, and loaded spectral brightness approaching $2.22\times10^9$ pairs/(s$\cdot$mW$\cdot$nm). Heralded autocorrelation measurements yield a second-order autocorrelation $g_H^{(2)}(0)$ as low as $4.0\times10^{-4}$ for a selected high-CAR cavity-defined bin pair. In particular, tuning the single-pass pump deterministically selects correlated frequency-bin pairings within the fixed QFC grid while preserving brightness and pairwise coincidence rates. We further separate intrinsic generation from output photon-pair flux, revealing the loaded-brightness-CAR relation. Together, pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading point to tailored SPDC QFCs as chip-integrated nonclassical light resources for multichannel quantum-state transport and information processing.

items.title: China daily CO2 emission estimates 2019-2025
items.summary: Near-real-time CO2 estimates enable timely tracking of emission changes, but broad sectoral classifications limit their ability to resolve industrial dynamics across China's provinces. Here, we update Carbon Monitor to estimate daily CO2 emissions across five sectors in 31 mainland Chinese provinces during 2019-2025 and monthly emissions from 40 industrial and construction subsectors in 30 provinces, combining historical inventories with industrial production indicators. National emissions increased from 10.83 Gt CO2 in 2019 to 12.15 Gt CO2 in 2023, before declining slightly to 12.08 Gt CO2 in 2025. The 2024-2025 national reduction of 0.23% reflected opposing sectoral trends, with industrial emissions increasing by 48.8 Mt CO2 while power generation and ground transport emissions decreased by 46.6 Mt CO2 and 27.7 Mt CO2, respectively. Provincial trajectories also diverged, with emissions rising in 16 provinces and falling in 15. Industrial disaggregation revealed increases of 102.3 Mt CO2 in nonferrous-metal smelting and pressing and decreases of 108.1 Mt CO2 in nonmetal mineral products during 2019-2024. Comparison with a historical provincial inventory yielded a median absolute relative difference of 9.4%. These findings demonstrate that national emission stabilization masks divergent regional and industrial changes, highlighting the need for temporally updated, sector-specific evidence to assess progress toward sustained reductions and identify mitigation priorities.

items.title: Pyroelectric Harvesting from Steady Heat Sources via Active Piezoelectric Thermal Switching
items.summary: This study demonstrates pyroelectric energy harvesting from a steady heat source using active piezoelectric thermal switching in a PZT/Si bimorph cantilever. The same PZT layer serves as both the mechanical actuator and the pyroelectric energy-conversion element. Dual output electrodes enable separation of the pyroelectric and piezoelectric signals. Pyroelectric energy harvesting is experimentally demonstrated at frequencies up to 110 Hz and temperature differences as small as 5 K. Comparison with the response predicted from the independently measured pyroelectric coefficient, together with transient thermal simulations, identifies dynamic interfacial heat transfer as a key limitation to high-frequency operation. This work demonstrates a compact MEMS approach for higher-frequency pyroelectric energy harvesting from low-grade steady heat sources.

items.title: Beyond PINNs: Boundary-Enriched Holomorphic Networks for Laplace Problems
items.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations by penalizing their residual, but this formulation can be difficult to optimize for solutions with singular behaviour. We focus specifically on the two-dimensional Laplace equation, whose strong analytical structure allows the governing equation to be enforced directly in the neural representation. We compare a hybrid harmonic-neural model with a holomorphic neural network whose output is harmonic by construction and therefore requires only boundary training. We further enrich the holomorphic model with singular functions chosen according to the interior angle and boundary conditions at each junction of boundary segments. On six singular benchmarks, the enriched model is the most accurate of the neural models we compare. On the four with a closed-form solution, however, that solution lies in the span of the enrichment terms, and a least-squares fit of these terms alone is exact to rounding error. On Motz's problem and the cracked beam, the neural core reduces the relative error of the recovered leading singular coefficient from about $10^{-2}$, for a least-squares fit with the same four terms, to about $10^{-6}$, and on four variants whose solution has a smooth part outside the span, the network is $4\times10^{4}$ to $2\times10^{7}$ times more accurate than a fit of its singular terms alone; classical least-squares fits with more singular terms, or with harmonic polynomials and rational poles, are more accurate still. Our results demonstrate how exploiting problem-specific analytical structure can provide an alternative to base and residual PINNs for challenging scientific computing problems.

items.title: Mathematical basis, phase transitions and singularities of (3+1)-dimensional phi4 scalar field model
items.summary: The lambda phi4 scalar field model can be applied to interpret pion-pion scattering and properties of hadrons. In this work, the mathematical basis, phase transitions and singularities of a (3+1)-dimensional (i.e., (3+1)D) phi4 scalar field model are investigated. It is found that as a specific example of topological quantum field theories, the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model must be set up on the Jordan-von Neumann-Wigner framework and dealt with the parameter space of complex time (or complex temperature). The use of the time average and the topologic Lorentz transformation representing Reidemeister moves ensure the integrability, which takes into account for the contributions of nontrivial topological structures to physical properties of the many-body interacting system. The ergodic hypothesis is violated at finite temperatures in the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model. Because the quantum field theories with ultraviolet cutoff can be mapped to the models in statistical mechanics, the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model with ultraviolet cutoff is studied by inspecting its relation with the three-dimensional (3D) Ising model. Furthermore, the direct relation between the coupling K in the 3D Ising model and the bare coupling lambda0 in the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model is determined in the strong coupling limit. The results obtained in the present work can be utilized to investigate thermodynamic physical properties and critical phenomena of quantum (scalar) field theories.

items.title: XTCP: an open-source FPGA TCP endpoint for readout over 10 and 25 Gigabit Ethernet
items.summary: XTCP is an open-source implementation of the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for high-rate detector readout. It targets sustained single-connection throughput near the TCP payload limit. In separate 10 Gigabit Ethernet transfers on the same Kintex UltraScale+ KU5P card and Linux host, XTCP and SiTCP-XG each delivered a median application-level throughput of 9.49 Gbit/s towards the host. Towards the FPGA, the medians were 9.49 Gbit/s for XTCP and 5.76 Gbit/s for the tested SiTCP-XG configuration. The XTCP prototype used more lookup tables and on-chip memory. In a 96 GiB echo test spanning repeated sequence-number wraps, recording when an acknowledgement first crossed the recovery boundary allowed four fast recoveries that the earlier signed comparison would have blocked. On one 25 Gigabit Ethernet bitstream, increasing the IP maximum transmission unit from 1500 to 9000 bytes raised median one-way throughput from 23.30 to 24.70 Gbit/s towards the host and from 22.09 to 24.08 Gbit/s towards the FPGA. At 9000 bytes these rates reached 99.7% and 97.1% of the TCP payload limit, respectively. In a separate echo test, the host verified all 8.77 TB returned by a jumbo-frame prototype over one connection in 3595 s, averaging 19.51 Gbit/s per direction.

items.title: Scaling Density Functional Theory with Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: Density functional theory (DFT) strikes a practical balance between accuracy and computational cost in many problems of computational chemistry and materials science. However, many DFT calculations are limited by fixed atom-centered basis sets, which dictate how accuracy and cost scale with system size. We propose Gaussian Splatting for Density Functional Theory (GS-DFT), which represents molecular orbitals as a cloud of Gaussians whose positions, shapes, and mixing coefficients are optimized jointly by gradient descent to minimize the energy without training data. Conceptually, GS-DFT is 3D Gaussian splatting with the renderer replaced by quantum mechanics. We introduce two key solver components: adaptive density fitting with screening for efficient evaluation of two-electron integrals, and a regularized differentiable orthogonalization of the molecular orbitals. Empirically, the optimized basis reaches the accuracy of the largest conventional basis sets with a fraction of the parameters, converging systematically in energy, density, and nuclear forces. At equal parameter count, it captures the stretched-bond and anion physics that fixed bases only recover with specialized basis augmentation. The resulting solver exhibits quadratic peak memory scaling in the cloud size, allowing us to simulate systems of up to 2,742 atoms (10,406 electrons) without any modifications at triple-zeta scale using a single four-GPU node.

items.title: Autonomous Multireference Quantum Chemistry with Artificial Intelligence Agents
items.summary: Accurately describing chemical reactions that involve strongly correlated electrons remains a major challenge in computational chemistry. Multireference electronic structure methods can address this challenge, but their application requires expert decisions that are di!cult to automate, particularly when the electronic structure changes as chemical bonds form and break. Here we introduce CASPER, an autonomously agentic workflow that performs multireference calculations along chemical reaction pathways. CASPER combines chemical knowledge, electronic structure calculations, and iterative assessment to identify chemically meaningful active spaces and maintain their consistency as bonds form and break. We demonstrate its capabilities on five transition-metal reactions, for which CASPER generates consistent multireference potential energy profiles with minimal human intervention. Importantly, in two reactions, CASPER identifies critical electronic-structure problems that an independent Claude session fails to recognize without the structured workflow. These include an electronic-state crossing and the exclusion of an orbital involved in bond breaking. Our results show the importance of combining language models with chemical knowledge and independent assessment of computational results. Beyond automating calculations, such agents have the potential to help researchers better understand the underlying physics and chemistry and open new opportunities for investigating complex chemical reactivity and generating high-quality quantum chemical data at scale.

items.title: QuakeConsensus: Reducing false detections in automatic earthquake catalogs through consensus phase association
items.summary: Automatic earthquake catalogs rely on phase associators to group the picks of a phase picker into events. Associators also produce false events that inflate the catalog. We measure the false events of five associators, PyOcto, GaMMA, REAL, GENIE, and backprojection, on two benchmarks built from observed phase picks in Taiwan. The first benchmark isolates 28,129 cataloged earthquakes in 20-minute windows, adding noise by shifting unassociated picks independently. The second evaluates 11,917 earthquakes from the 2024 $M_w$ 7.4 Hualien aftershock sequence, shifting unassociated P and S pairs together. We also propose a consensus association strategy that keeps an event found by at least two associators. With noise picks, single associators produce 5.3% to 10.2% false positives on the regional benchmark and 11.8% to 46.8% on the Hualien benchmark, whereas the consensus catalog reduces these false positive percentages to 4.2% and 11.5%, respectively. The consensus has the highest F1 score and the smallest percentage of false positives on both benchmarks.

items.title: Can Satellite Mega-Constellations Justify Their Impact on Astronomy?
items.summary: Private space companies are increasingly commercializing near-earth space. Some estimates show that more than 100,000 satellites may orbit the Earth by 2030. This increase in the number of satellites has many consequences for science, particularly astronomy. Satellite mega-constellations for satellite Internet connectivity are one of the main drivers behind the explosion in the number of satellites. Here, we briefly note whether such satellite mega-constellations can justify their impact on astronomy.

items.title: An eight-channel RFSoC waveform digitizer with AC- and DC-coupled front ends and transparent dual-DDR event memory
items.summary: We present Transparent Dual-DDR Event Memory (TDEM) for the triggered readout of an eight-channel radio-frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) digitizer. With either an AC- or a DC-coupled front end, each accepted trigger records 4096 samples per channel at 5 GSa/s. Two pulses 100 ns apart produced separate, overlapping records. On one DC-coupled input, interleaving calibration reduced an eight-sample periodic residual by a factor of 29 at +100 mV, but not at zero input. After a power cycle, the digitizer restored the coefficients for all eight DC-coupled inputs without a training tone. TDEM assigns complete events to 64- and 32-bit DDR4 memory interfaces in a 2:1 ratio. With this allocation alone, host page requests still determined which memory served each read. In two runs of approximately 6 s at 160 kHz, the peak receiver backlog fell from 20 140 events with the earlier readout to 1457 with event-level prefetch. Prefetch raised the sustained rate of the DC-coupled system from 150 to 170 kHz under repeated host readout pauses. With the same receiver design and a revised host buffer allocation, the AC-coupled system passed three 30 min tests at 175 kHz, each with 48 readout pauses and no rejected triggers. Without imposed pauses or background load, the host verified all 323 452 631 events in 30 min at 179.7 kHz. At 180 kHz, triggers were first rejected at the digitizer, consistent with a modelled transmitter capacity of 179.730 kHz for this event format.

items.title: Infrared Relaxation Modes and the Emergence of Collective Order in Neural Dynamics
items.summary: We develop a microscopic field theory of collective order formation in interacting nonlinear neural systems. Integrating out microscopic neural degrees of freedom yields an effective action whose quadratic kernel determines the ordering threshold, while higher-order connected responses govern nonlinear stabilization. Spectral decomposition reveals that relaxation rates and collective-mode overlaps control collective instability and memory dynamics. Enhanced infrared spectral weight lowers the critical coupling and generates long-time memory, revealing a common spectral origin of collective ordering and persistent dynamics. Controlled numerical constructions verify the spectral dependence of collective instability and response, while nonlinear mean-field scaling follows from the microscopic Landau expansion. Transformer Jacobian spectra further reveal learning-induced infrared organization and transient memory enhancement consistent with critical-like response. Our results establish a microscopic framework linking neural interactions, collective order, and long-time memory.

items.title: Electric polarizabilities with phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
items.summary: While projector quantum Monte Carlo methods are known for producing accurate ground-state energies, the prediction of other properties that encode the electronic response to applied electric and magnetic fields has historically been challenging. In this work we demonstrate that the electric (static) polarizability tensor, which is formally a second-derivative of the energy with respect to electric fields, can be efficiently computed with phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo using a correlated sampling finite-difference strategy. With simple Hartree-Fock trial wave functions, we investigate a series of small molecules (some of which are difficult for approximate density functionals), polyacenes of increasing size, and ferrocene as a representative organometallic complex. The methodology is scalable to relatively large molecules involving thousands of basis functions, and with appropriate trial wave functions remains robust for strongly correlated electronic states, as we show for the stretched dinitrogen molecule. This work opens the door to the computation of a host of other second-order molecular properties with auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, which will inform the ongoing search for optimal trial wave functions and extend benchmark-quality training data sets for the refinement of semi-empirical and machine learning models for quantum chemistry and molecular simulation.

items.title: Investigating planar Proca metamaterials in nonlinear (2+1)-Electrodynamics
items.summary: The present work pursues the investigation of the physics of a planar electromagnetic system incorporating nonlinear effects, as well as de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass terms in vacuum, which can be tuned to describe new planar metamaterials (MTMs) potentially suitable for technological applications. As a result, we observe interesting effects generated by a spatially dispersive profile that emerges from non-linearity. This characterizes the three-dimensional QED vacuum as a nonlocal metamaterial. The constitutive relations are derived, and the dielectric function of the metamaterial (MTM) exhibits spatial dispersion due to the Chern-Simons mass. The dispersion relations are analyzed in terms of applied external electromagnetic fields and both the de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass parameters. We also notice that, in the special case in which only a background magnetic field is present, this field gives no contribution neither to the dielectric function nor to the spatial dispersion profile, as is the case when both the electric and magnetic fields are present.

items.title: The replication-energy limit of PQG reduced-density-matrix theory from a single-fragment semidefinite program
items.summary: Variational two-electron reduced-density-matrix calculations are not size extensive: the energy per fragment can decrease when identical, strictly noninteracting fragments are replicated [M. Nakata and K. Yasuda, Phys. Rev. A 80, 042109 (2009)]. For the $P$, $Q$, and $G$ conditions (PQG) we prove the following. (i) The energy per fragment converges to the minimum of a semidefinite program (SDP) on one fragment. The limit is reached through negative interfragment covariances of order $1/(k-1)$ for $k$ replicas, which cancel the local electron number and spin fluctuations consistently with a global singlet. (ii) The energy per fragment is nonincreasing in the replica count. (iii) It reaches the limit exactly at a finite replica count. (iv) The defect is tied to the local electron-number variance: a sharp local electron number restores additivity without a spin constraint. (v) In chains of identical units the energy per unit has a limit that tends to the same minimum as the coupling vanishes. The key tool is that the $G$ condition [C. Garrod and J. K. Percus, J. Math. Phys. 5, 1756 (1964)] keeps the variances and covariances of one-body operators positive semidefinite without a representing state, so that the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applies. PQG therefore admits explicitly constructed replicated points whose compensated local fluctuations lower the energy per fragment below the isolated value. Be, CH$_4$, N$_2$, and H$_2$O (STO-6G) and a four-site Hubbard fragment illustrate the results; in these examples the gap to the isolated value persists with three-index conditions $T_1$ and $T_2$.

items.title: Newton's Second Law: A Structural Necessity of Mechanics Constrained by Excluded Perpetual Motion and Universal Free Fall
items.summary: For over three centuries, Newton's second law (F = ma) has governed mechanics with extraordinary success, while its epistemic warrant has remained empirical. That merely empirical contingency vanishes once mechanics is constrained by two principles: the principle of excluded perpetual motion (PEPM) with its pre-Newtonian phenomenological content and the weak equivalence principle (WEP) with universal free fall as its primitive content. The PEPM secures the applicability of Suppes' measurement-theoretic framework to gravitational mass and force, exposing the formal structure latent in their empirical manifestations and establishing both as independent primitives. Gravity bridges statics and kinematics in Stevin's and Galileo's inclined-plane arguments, where the common sine factor in force and acceleration cancels in F/a.
