This occurs without the need for external forcing or the presence of an energetic plasma population. This finding suggests that the time-asymptotic regime of the plasma is rather akin to a non-linear superposition of multiple BGK-like modes associated with nearly constant phase-speed waves. The electric field and the space-averaged particle distribution function exhibit a power-law broad spectrum, which is consistent with an energy cascade towards smaller scales in both position and velocity spaces.

items.title: Tunable Microresonator Arrays Induced by Geometric Phase
items.summary: Unlike periodic field-intensity patterns, which can be generated by interference of coherent beams of uniform intensity, periodic structures in a material are usually created by periodic modification of its properties or geometry. In contrast, we show here that a millimeter-long bundle of four conventional side-coupled optical fibers with a slowly varying transverse arrangement can support a nearly periodic array of whispering-gallery-mode microresonators, whose period can be tuned mechanically down to about $100\,μ\mathrm{m}$.

items.title: Data handling, production, and simulation in the Muon g-2 Experiment at Fermilab
items.summary: This paper details the computing strategies of the Muon g-2 Experiment at Fermilab, which measured the muon's anomalous magnetic moment with a precision of 127 ppb by processing over 10 petabytes of detector and simulation data. This paper discusses the computational and operational challenges of data production, data handling, and data analysis of such large datasets. These challenges were overcome by using Fermilab-developed software infrastructure and production tools, making efficient use of resources, and improving the collaboration-developed reconstruction workflow. By overcoming these challenges, the experiment improved the data throughput capacity and reduced the analysis turnaround time by an order of magnitude over the course of its lifetime.

items.title: Degenerate symmetric formulation and principal subsystems for chemically reacting multi-temperature fluid mixtures
items.summary: We construct a degenerate symmetric first-order formulation and principal subsystems for chemically reacting multi-temperature fluid mixtures with independent constituent velocities and temperatures, viscosity, and heat conduction. Starting from the entropy-admissible Class-III theory of arXiv:2610.37637, we characterize when its prescribed constituent Euler fluxes are generated by scalar potentials in the conservative entropy variables. Under the stated hypotheses the necessary and sufficient condition is that the separate Gibbs--Duhem one-forms $ω_i$ vanish. This implies locally additive entropy, but it is not required by the general parent theory. In this subclass, the complete main field contains multipliers for both conservative balances and zero-storage constitutive equations. The spatial Hessians are symmetric, and the temporal Hessian is positive semidefinite and singular. For separated transport laws, eliminating auxiliary variables factorizes the positive-semidefinite dissipative principal symbol. We extend the algebraic Boillat--Ruggeri principal-subsystem construction to degenerate systems. Commuting restrictions yield a dissipative common-temperature system and a nested hierarchy of grouped-temperature Euler subsystems. Classical characteristic interlacing applies within the nested Euler hierarchy, whose temporal Hessians are positive definite. Separately, constrained entropy maximization defines an energy-equivalent common temperature and provides a thermodynamic Class-III-to-Class-II reduction for additive and nonadditive parent entropies. For a thermally reconstructed reference state, the full relative entropy splits exactly into the thermal projection deficit and the relative entropy of the retained variables. We derive the Class-II entropy-production identity and distinguish the thermodynamic projection from principal restrictions and dynamical relaxation limits.

items.title: High-Power Laser Drives Motion in Ultra-thin Photonic Crystal Lightsails
items.summary: Laser-driven lightsails require reflectors that are ultralight, highly reflective and robust under intense illumination. These demands point to the thinnest reflectors that dielectric optics allows, photonic crystals, in which a perforated membrane thinner than the wavelength of light acts as a mirror. Such mirrors reflect by confining light inside the membrane, but this confinement also amplifies absorption, making ultralow-loss, tension-bearing materials essential. Stoichiometric high-stress silicon nitride uniquely meets both requirements, yet its ~1 GPa stress makes large, compliant structures difficult to release intact, and such sails have never been pushed by high-power lasers. Here we demonstrate millimeter-wide, 200-nm-thick photonic-crystal trampolines in this material, with 99% design reflectivity at 1070 nm and a static stiffness of 0.53 N/m. Radiation pressure displaces them by more than a micrometer within 50 microseconds. In air, they withstand several times the irradiance found at the Sun's surface, delivered as a coherent beam. Light reshapes the sail more than it pushes it, since modest temperature differences buckle the membrane and collapse its stiffness, so thermal deformation outpaces radiation pressure within milliseconds. The interaction and compliance that make lightsails movable also let light deform them. These results establish a testbed for high-power nanophotonics, directed-energy systems and light-driven propulsion.

items.title: Large Deviations and Critical Scaling in the Finite-Population Granovetter Threshold Model
items.summary: We develop a systematic asymptotic analysis of the exact finite-population solution of Granovetter's threshold model, in which a single initial instigator triggers a cascade among agents with independently distributed adoption thresholds. By expressing the propagation probability as an order-statistic boundary-crossing event, we formulate its macroscopic large-deviation rate as a constrained relative-entropy minimization problem. For Beta-distributed thresholds, we obtain explicit solutions for all shape parameters $α$ and $β$, identifying four possible optimal empirical threshold profiles: fully free, fully pinned, pinned--free, and free--pinned. These profiles determine both the exponential probability of macroscopic cascades and the threshold configurations responsible for their occurrence. Importance-sampling estimates confirm the analytical rate functions, while sequential Monte Carlo simulations independently reproduce the predicted optimal profiles. We also revisit the critical scaling near $α_c=1$ and confirm the principal finite-size scaling laws: the mean active fraction decays as $N^{-1/2}$ for uniform thresholds and as $N^{-1}$ for $α=1$ and $0<β<1$. In the latter regime, we further derive an explicit scaling function for the logarithmic critical window from the microscopic branching-process limit. Our results provide a general framework for determining the probabilities and characteristic configurations of rare collective events in threshold-driven cascade processes

items.title: Learning free energy across a differentiable temperature range by deep generative modeling
items.summary: Free energy governs the directionality, stability, and temperature sensitivity of physical, chemical, and biological transformations. Conventional free energy calculations, such as thermodynamic integration and free energy perturbation, often have to be performed at individual temperatures and are limited by the high cost of sampling an extensive set of thermodynamic states. Here, we introduce learned temperature-differentiable free energy perturbation (TD-FEP), a deep generative framework that learns a temperature-conditioned, invertible mapping between reference and target systems through data-free, energy-based optimization. TD-FEP thereby unifies one-shot state generation and free energy calculation across a continuous temperature range. We validated TD-FEP across a broad range of applications, including isolated molecules, periodic materials, and chemical reactions.

items.title: Ion Backflow Suppression and Absorption Dynamics in Cascaded GEM Structures
items.summary: Ion backflow (IBF) is a persistent challenge in Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) detectors: positive ions drifting back into the sensitive volume distort the drift field and degrade both spatial and energy resolution. We investigate the ion-absorption characteristics of single- to quintuple-GEM detectors using ANSYS and Garfield$^{++}$ for an Ar/CO$_2$ (70:30) gas mixture. A layer-resolved formalism is developed that distinguishes conditional foil-level absorption from a detector-level absorption metric that correctly weights ion production at every amplification stage. For the conventional biconical geometry, cascading foils improves the overall ion-absorption fraction only moderately, from 47.83\% for a single GEM to 59.06\% for a quintuple GEM. Replacing the biconical holes with a single-conical profile raises the absorption fraction to 75\%-87\% across the same range of multiplicities and reduces the IBF/Gain ratio by a factor of two to three an improvement that exceeds what is gained by adding four additional biconical foils. As a secondary test under more realistic conditions, the second transfer-gap length of a triple-GEM detector is varied from 1.2 to 3.5~mm. The gain shows a non-monotonic dependence with a maximum near 2.0-2.5~mm, while the IBF/Gain ratio decreases monotonically with increasing gap length; the single-conical geometry retains its factor-of-two advantage throughout. These findings establish that ion suppression in cascaded GEM structures is governed not only by the number of foils but primarily by the local ion-collection properties of each foil, and that single-conical holes represent a promising route to improved performance in high-rate detector applications.

items.title: Lagrangian particle simulations of an idealized deep convective squall line: Aggregation, fragmentation, and their polarimetric signatures
items.summary: We investigate secondary ice production (SIP) in an idealized deep convective squall line using the Lagrangian particle model McSnow coupled to ICON. The model represents ice particle properties, including habit, riming degree, and mass composition. We introduce a parameterization of collision-induced ice--ice fragmentation linked to apparent density as a measure of particle fragility. We compare rime splintering (RS), freezing fragmentation (FF), and collision-induced fragmentation (CF), including turbulence-enhanced collision rates. Collision-induced fragmentation is the dominant SIP mechanism, strongly increasing ice number concentrations in the dendritic growth zone. Freezing fragmentation contributes little because sufficiently large raindrops are scarce. Rime splintering produces secondary ice at lower altitudes and indirectly promotes large aggregates. Turbulence has little effect on fragmentation but enhances the aggregation of fragments. Fragmentation shifts the particle size distribution toward smaller sizes and reduces precipitation, while turbulence-enhanced aggregation partly restores large particles and precipitation. McRadar forward simulations show that SIP affects radar moments and Doppler spectra. Specific differential phase KDP provides the clearest conventional radar signature of fragmentation. Spectral differential reflectivity identifies secondary ice source regions through enhanced signals at the slow edge of the Doppler spectrum. Our results identify collision-induced fragmentation as a key source of secondary ice in deep convection and show that its impact depends on interactions with aggregation and turbulence. Spectral polarimetric radar observations may help constrain SIP in nature.

items.title: Probing Extended Recognition Sites in Zn-Metalloproteins via Quantum Chemistry and Polarizable Molecular Dynamics
items.summary: Zn-metalloproteins play vital roles in numerous metabolic processes, making them high-value targets for structure-based drug design. To advance these efforts, it is useful to unravel the individual components of the intermolecular interaction energies ($ΔE$) that stabilize the Zn-binding cavity, both in the absence and presence of bound protein ligands. Here, we utilize quantum chemistry (QC) to decompose $ΔE$ into distinct physical contributions. The relative magnitudes of these components vary significantly depending on the coordination number (four to six) and the chemical nature ('hard' vs. 'soft') of the Zn-coordinating ligands. These high-level QC analyses serve to calibrate and validate polarizable molecular mechanics potentials, effectively extending the accurate description of electronic effects beyond the immediate Zn-binding cavity to enlarged recognition sites and, ultimately, entire protein systems over long molecular dynamics (MD) simulation timescales. We focus here on a QC-grounded molecular mechanics procedure, denoted as SIBFA. Following a concise overview of our QC methodology used for its calibration, we present validation studies on complexes containing up to 300 atoms and discuss the prospects of applying this framework to large-scale simulations of Zn-metalloprotein-ligand complexes. Finally, the structural and energetic roles of discrete, highly polarizable water molecules are highlighted.

items.title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Balancing Causation, Correlation, and User Intent
items.summary: Turbulence states vary widely in modeling difficulty, requiring distinct paradigms; thus, no single AI or data-driven approach suits all flows. We propose an operational framework classifying data-driven turbulence modeling by balancing physical causation and statistical correlation via non-equilibrium flow memory and user intent. Using the Mori--Zwanzig projection formalism, we decompose unclosed turbulent stress into a local response ($τ_{ij}^L$) and a spatio-temporally non-local memory integral ($τ_{ij}^{NL}$). Near statistical equilibrium, rapid relaxation suppresses advective memory, letting local correlations capture physical causation via intrusive $τ_{ij}^L$ constitutive relations in Reynolds-Averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations. Because the elliptic Poisson equation for fluctuating pressure couples stress evolution to eddy dimensionality beyond single-point velocity-gradient componentiality, local closures are not strictly valid even at equilibrium, yet remain acceptable engineering approximations. In non-equilibrium turbulence, modeling bifurcates by user intent. For predicting unseen geometries, large coherent structures sustain non-local memory ($τ_{ij}^{NL}$), invalidating local total-stress closures and requiring first-principles causal scale resolution guided by Rules-Augmented AI (RAAI), with resolution set by a recent non-equilibrium theory. Conversely, for rapid design in a known, parameterized coherent flow class, a purely correlational strategy suffices: combining Non-Intrusive Reduced-Order Modeling (NIROM) with uncentered Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) across multi-realization ensembles yields zero-solver synthesis of stationary statistics and unsteady coherent evolution from governing dimensionless parameters. This framework aligns physical causation, statistical correlation, and user intent across flow regimes.

items.title: Transient coupling of Marangoni spreading and interfacial waves
items.summary: How does an initially non-uniform distribution of surfactant generate waves on a de- formable interface, and how do those waves then govern the redistribution of the surfactant? We answer this question for the linear Cauchy-Poisson problem of an axisymmetric interface between two viscous fluids, released from rest with independently prescribed distributions of surfactant and of interface displacement, by Hankel and Laplace transforms. In Stokes flow the pressure and the viscous normal stress of the Marangoni flow cancel in the nor- mal traction on the interface, for any viscosity ratio, so that the surfactant relaxes without displacing the interface: the coupling between surfactant redistribution and interface de- formation is inertial. With inertia, the Marangoni flow initiates a capillary-gravity wave whose polarity, at leading order for thin boundary layers, is set by the sign of $ρ_l μ_l - ρ_u μ_u $, and the surfactant is then carried by the wave, so that its concentration performs weakly damped oscillations at the wave frequency after the Marangoni relaxation of a flat surface has ended. The amplitude of these oscillations is given in closed form at small viscosity; its maximum does not coincide with that of the familiar resonant damping, and the surfactant and the interface shape decouple exactly only when the two fluids have equal densities and viscosities. A localized displacement radiates a wave packet that the surfactant damps, and a localized surfactant redistribution initiates a wave on an initially flat interface. Direct numerical simulations with sharp geometric surfactant transport verify these predictions.

items.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
items.summary: An improved camera-based 3D-velocity map imaging (VMI) system was demonstrated with a neuromorphic camera. We show a machine vision event-driven camera can achieve an unprecedented latency of 2 microseconds when detecting single ion/electron with a microchannel plate imaging detector, which boosts the speed of the momentum imaging system to more than 100 kHz, while the system with a conventional frame camera is limited to a few kHz. The high spatial resolution of the camera offers additional performance boost while maintaining excellent multi-hit capability and a high time resolution.

items.title: How Brine Pockets Evolve and Release in Ice
items.summary: Liquid inclusions migrate through solids by melting at one end and freezing at the other, but how a macroscopic phase boundary regulates their deformation and release remains poorly understood. Here, we track individual brine pockets in saline ice through bulk migration, elongation, and release at the ice-water interface, resolving the motion of both ends. In the bulk, temperature-dependent thermomigration gradually elongates the pockets. Near the ice-water interface, the front slows, whereas liquid connection is followed by accelerated rear freezing and rapid shortening. These opposing responses arise from distinct changes in thermal-solutal transport: proximity to the boundary suppresses the local thermal-gradient enhancement and slows front-end melting, while liquid connection enables salt exchange with the surrounding liquid and accelerates rear-end freezing. A quasi-steady diffusion-resistance model captures the dependence of the half-length release time on the pocket length at connection and identifies an effective external exchange length consistent with a salt-balance estimate. Our results identify thermal proximity and liquid connectivity as distinct controls on inclusion evolution and release, providing a framework for understanding liquid redistribution in multicomponent solids.

items.title: A Polarization Hall Effect in Hydrated DNA
items.summary: We report magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent transverse-voltage phenomena in hydrated genomic DNA. The sample is confined beneath a glass coverslip in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry and subjected to perpendicular magnetic fields, revealing sharp thresholds, staircase-like voltage plateaus, and oscillatory structures approximately periodic in inverse magnetic field. Fixed-field cooling reveals longitudinal reorganizations near 20.6 and 12.0 $^\circ$C, while a separate experiment shows large-amplitude transverse oscillations below approximately 12 $^\circ$C. Water controls and buffer-free DNA measurements support an association between the structured response and the hydrated DNA system. We propose a polarization-based interpretation of the transverse response, termed a ``polarization Hall effect,'' and discuss the observed regimes within a phenomenological framework of nonlinear dynamics and metastable configurations. These findings identify hydrated DNA as a soft-matter system exhibiting structured electrical responses jointly regulated by magnetic field and temperature.

items.title: A Semi-Lagrangian Adaptive Rank (SLAR) Method for High-Dimensional Vlasov Dynamics
items.summary: We extend our previous work on a semi-Lagrangian adaptive rank (SLAR) integrator, in the finite difference framework for nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson systems, to the general high-order tensor setting. The proposed scheme retains the high-order accuracy of semi-Lagrangian methods, ensuring stability for large time steps and avoiding dimensional splitting errors. The primary contribution of this paper is the novel extension of the algorithm from the matrix to the high-dimensional tensor setting, which enables the simulation of Vlasov models in up to six dimensions. The key technical components include (1) a third-order high-dimensional polynomial reconstruction that scales as $O(d^2)$, providing a point-wise approximation of the solution at the foot of characteristics in a semi-Lagrangian scheme; (2) a recursive hierarchical adaptive cross approximation of high-order tensors in a hierarchical Tucker format, characterized by a tensor tree; (3) a low-complexity Poisson solver in the hierarchical Tucker format that leverages the FFT for efficiency. The computed adaptive rank kinetic solutions exhibit low-rank structures within branches of the tensor tree resulting in substantial computational savings in both storage and time. The resulting algorithm achieves a computational complexity of $O(d^4 N r^{3+\lceil\log_2d\rceil})$, where $N$ is the number of grid points per dimension, $d$ is the problem dimension, and $r$ is the maximum rank in the tensor tree, overcoming the curse of dimensionality. Through extensive numerical tests, we demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm and highlight its ability to capture complex solution structures while maintaining a computational complexity that scales linearly with $N$.

items.title: Conceptual Design of a 5 MV High-Voltage System for a Compact Orbitron Fusion Device
items.summary: The high-voltage system is a key part of the puzzle toward achieving net-positive fusion power in a compact Orbitron device. This paper presents a conceptual engineering design for a 5 MV, 20 mA, 100 kW HV system for a next-generation Orbitron, serving as an upper-bound design point for the HV system. The MC-TRANS++ 0-D code is used to set the load requirements: a 1 m long, 0.45 m first-wall-radius central cell, 2.5 T on-axis and 10 T mirror-throat fields, and a 5 MV radial potential drop sustaining supersonic rotation ($M = 4.8$). This delivers a triple product of $5.8 \times 10^{21}$ keV s /m3 and $Q_{sci}$ = 8.5. The HV power supply integrates an AC-DC converter, a SiC full-bridge inverter, a CLLC resonant network with an air-core step-up transformer, and feeds a 120-stage parallel-fed series-cascaded rectifier operating at 250 kHz. At full load, this architecture yields an end-to-end efficiency of 85%, much higher than the 60% typical of triode-driven MV-class power supplies. The 5 MV voltage is delivered to a radially nested 50-gap bushing system that interfaces pressurized insulating gas to high vacuum, using brazed alumina spacers with a corrugated profile. The design draws directly on the measured behavior of a previously demonstrated 300 kV prototype, from which six quantitative lessons are extracted and mapped onto the 5 MV design. Electrostatic simulations of the complete assembly at rated voltage show maximum surface fields of 30.3 MV/m on the corona rings, 7.7 MV/m at the cathode triple junction, and average vacuum-gap fields ranging from 5.5 to 40 MV/m. These field strengths remain below breakdown thresholds due to the implementation of triple-junction shielding, insulation corrugation, and axial magnetic insulation at 2.5-10 T. The conceptual system has a form factor of 2.7 meters in diameter and 6.5 meters in length, projected to deliver a net power output of 86-171 kWe.

items.title: LayerCake v1.0: a framework for low- to intermediate-order automated models development
items.summary: A new model development framework called LayerCake is presented. It is written in the Python language and relies on the Sympy symbolic computation package to compute the Galerkin projection of two-dimensional spatially extended geophysical models. These projections provide their time evolution operator in the spectral space on a restricted set of modes. The resulting tendencies of the models can be evaluated either numerically (for time integration) or symbolically (for parameters sensitivity analysis and bifurcation analysis). We provide several simple examples of geophysical models to showcase the capabilities of the framework, and we hint at how more complex systems can be designed.

items.title: Breit interaction in elastic scattering of vortex electron on Hydrogen atomic target
items.summary: The interaction of electron vortex beams with atoms is fundamental to their applications, yet existing studies of elastic scattering have considered only the Coulomb interaction. The role of the Breit interaction, which represents the leading relativistic correction to the Coulomb potential between two electrons, has not been systematically examined. In this paper, we study the elastic scattering of a vortex electron by a hydrogen atomic target, with emphasis on the role of the Breit interaction. Comparisons are made between two situations: the pure Coulomb contribution and the pure Breit contribution. Our results show that the Breit interaction dominates the scattering process when the total angular momentum of the vortex electron is larger than a certain threshold, which challenges the conventional notion that the Breit interaction makes little contribution to electron scattering for low-$Z$ atoms. This phenomenon arises primarily because a vortex electron with large angular momentum possesses a substantial magnetic moment, and the Breit interaction precisely describes the interaction between magnetic moments. The threshold can be adjusted by changing the parameters of the initial vortex electron. Moreover, we further compare the single-atom, mesoscopic, and macroscopic target cases, and show that the target size significantly influences the observability of the Breit-induced effects, with a smaller target size being favorable for observing this phenomenon. Vortex electrons add a new tool to the well-established electron-atom scattering tool box. Our results are important for applications of vortex electrons: they show that, when large total angular momentum is involved, the Breit interaction must be taken into account in calculations.

items.title: The state of nuclear data for fusion activation simulations
items.summary: This report compares decay-heat calculations made with four nuclear data libraries, TENDL-2025, ENDF/B-VIII.1, JEFF-4.0 and JENDL-5, against the JAEA FNS decay-heat benchmark. The main comparison uses the 2000 campaign, in which 73 foils were irradiated for five minutes in a mostly 14 MeV neutron field and their decay heat was measured for about an hour. The 1996 seven-hour campaign, with 29 foils and cooling times of up to 400 days, is compared separately and is not included in the rankings. Over the 69 elemental foils solved by all four libraries, the median deviation from the measurement (the mean absolute C/E deviation of each foil) is JENDL-5 17 percent, TENDL-2025 19 percent, JEFF-4.0 22 percent and ENDF/B-VIII.1 44 percent. No library is best everywhere: JENDL-5 on 24, JEFF-4.0 on 18, TENDL-2025 on 17 and ENDF/B-VIII.1 on 10 of the foils. For each element the report breaks the heat down by product and lists the nuclear data on which the libraries differ, and the final sections propose measurements, including enriched-isotope irradiations, that would resolve the largest differences.

items.title: Wavelet-domain flow-matching posterior estimation for LISA signals with data gaps
items.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) data stream will contain scheduled and unscheduled gaps, which break the stationarity of the instrumental noise and invalidate the standard frequency-domain likelihood. Amortized simulation-based inference (SBI) avoids explicit likelihood evaluations, but its application to months-long observations requires compressing high-dimensional, gapped time series while preserving information about source parameters. We develop an end-to-end amortized posterior estimation pipeline: the gapped data are mapped to noise-scaled Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) wavelet coefficients and summarized by a convolutional-Transformer network, trained jointly with a flow-matching (FM) posterior estimator, with optional importance-sampling correction. For a LISA-like signal observed for 3 months, the amortized FM posteriors are well calibrated on simulated observations whose waveforms and gaps were not seen in training. The FM posteriors agree closely with the benchmark, the posteriors from parallel-tempered Markov chain Monte Carlo (PTMCMC), although they exhibit moderately greater dispersion. Importance sampling efficiently reweights the FM posterior, achieving close agreement with the benchmark at modest additional cost.

items.title: A Viscosity-Decoupled Uzawa Lattice Boltzmann Method for Incompressible Flows Across Reynolds Numbers
items.summary: Conventional lattice Boltzmann methods (LBMs) tie viscosity to collision relaxation, which induces diffusive stiffness at low Reynolds numbers, non-hydrodynamic instabilities at high Reynolds numbers, and passband breakdown in variable-relaxation dual-time schemes, whereas continuum incompressible solvers require global pressure-Poisson solves every step. We propose a Viscosity-Decoupled Uzawa Lattice Boltzmann Method (VDU-LBM) in D2Q9 and D3Q19 that permanently fixes collision at unit relaxation under smooth harmonic scaling and clears pre-collision non-conserved kinetic memory in one sweep. Constant, heterogeneous, and Smagorinsky eddy viscosities enter through a parameter-free post-streaming bond-symmetric momentum-flux lift that conserves discrete momentum pairwise without perturbing continuity. Variable-step BDF1/BDF2 marching is accelerated by a matrix-free local polynomial Uzawa smoother on the $(d+1)$ conserved moments, paired with link-wise Bouzidi curved walls and shifted ghost open boundaries. Across $\mathrm{Re}\in[10^{-4},10^6]$, VDU-LBM achieves smooth low-Mach second-order space--time accuracy, accelerates unsteady DFG 2D-2 shedding per cycle by $14.27\times\text{--}15.85\times$ over matched 20-core OpenFOAM-v2412, and lowers $256^3$ $\mathrm{Re}=1600$ resolved enstrophy error by $2.25\times$ versus hybrid recursive regularized LBM. On an NVIDIA A100 GPU, the fused D3Q19 solver attains $80.9\%\text{--}85.5\%$ of measured copy bandwidth in multi-pass port traffic and cuts bounded-relaxation diffusive step cost at high viscosity contrasts.

items.title: Condensation-related expansion work of water vapor as a major pathway for kinetic energy generation in the lower atmosphere
items.summary: Earth's atmosphere operates a steam cycle: water evaporates from the surface, expands as vapor, condenses in colder air, and returns as precipitation. Yet its power and relationship to atmospheric mechanical power remain poorly quantified. Applying the Clausius--Clapeyron relation between saturated vapor expansion work and latent heat converted at Carnot efficiency to vertically distributed condensation, we derive the steam-engine power as a sum of the gravitational and condensation-related contributions, $W_v=W_g+W_c$; it is not the net power of a complete moist-air cycle. Using twelve years of GPM/DPR spectral latent-heating profiles and MERRA-2 fields, we estimate $W_v\simeq4.1$ W m$^{-2}$, with $W_c\simeq2.8$ W m$^{-2}$. Separately, we diagnose total atmospheric mechanical power $W=W_P+W_K\simeq4.3$ W m$^{-2}$, comprising gravitational power of precipitation $W_P\simeq1.1$ W m$^{-2}$ and kinetic energy generation $W_K\simeq3.2$ W m$^{-2}$, including $2.4$ W m$^{-2}$ below 500 hPa. Both correspondences $W_v\simeq W$ and $W_c\simeq W_K$ lie within 20--30% uncertainty estimates. To explain these correspondences, we propose that $W_c$ generates the potential energy associated with surface pressure gradients. Cross-isobaric flow in the frictional lower atmosphere converts this energy into kinetic energy. In a horizontally isothermal atmosphere, this positive pressure work would be nearly cancelled by compression aloft. An idealized circulation illustrates how differential heating can offset compression, allowing nearly isobaric upper return flow. In the proposed mechanism, condensation-driven circulation unlocks this thermal compensation thus providing a major pathway for lower-atmospheric kinetic energy generation. We discuss how changes in the coupling between condensation and differential heating could test this proposed causal relationship.

items.title: Statistical Signatures of Velocity-Space Turbulence in the Earth's Magnetosheath
items.summary: In collisionless plasmas, the particle distributions are often far from local thermodynamic equilibrium, providing a significant source of free energy that leads to complex velocity-space dynamics. In turbulent plasmas, the possibility of a cascade of the free energy in velocity space, analogous to the spatial cascade of fluid and electromagnetic field energies, has been suggested. However, observational evidence of plasma turbulence throughout phase space remains limited. Using measurements from the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission in a special campaign in the Earth's magnetosheath, we present the first statistical study of signatures consistent with velocity-space turbulence across a wide range of plasma conditions. We observe two main populations in the ion velocity-space spectrum -- an isotropic $-3/2$ spectrum and an anisotropic $-2$ spectrum organized by the ion $β$ and bulk flow. In addition, the spectral power laws in the spatial and velocity domains are uncorrelated, while the velocity-space spectral index is correlated with estimated real-space energy transfer rates. These results reveal how the ion spectral properties are systematically organized by plasma conditions and related to real-space turbulence. This connection has broad implications for turbulence and the energy partition between thermal and non-thermal particles in space and astrophysical plasmas.

items.title: Numerical Study of Flow and Cavitation in Single-Liquid Injectors with Sharp-Edged and Chamfered Orifice Inlets
items.summary: In the current work, the investigators used Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) to investigate water flow and cavitation in single-liquid injectors with sharp-edged and chamfered orifice inlets. The k-ω Shear Stress Transport (SST) turbulence model was used along with the Zwart-Gerber-Belamri (ZGB) cavitation model and the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method. The CFD predictions for the volumetric flow rate were validated against existing experimental data for the sharp-edged and chamfered orifice inlets. Pressure drops ranging between 0.07 MPa and 0.59 MPa were considered along with orifice length-to-diameter ratios of 2, 5, and 10. Strong cavitation was observed for the sharp-edged orifice inlet cases with a length-to-diameter ratio of 5 and a pressure drop larger than 0.2 MPa. A hydraulic flip was observed for the sharp-edged orifice inlet with a length-to-diameter ratio of 5 and a pressure drop of 0.59 MPa, which was consistent with the findings from the previous experimental study. Cavitation inception was observed for the chamfered orifice inlet cases with a length-to-diameter ratio of 5 and pressure drops larger than 0.2 MPa. For the sharp-edged orifice inlet with orifice length-to-diameter ratios of 2 and 10, a strong cavitation was observed inside the orifice.

items.title: Connecting Microseismicity to Lithology via a Model of Slip Avalanches
items.summary: Fluid injection into the earth's crust can induce small and frequent earthquakes in the subsurface. Predicting their sizes and temporal occurrences via statistical analysis is crucial for safe operations in unconventional oil and gas recovery, enhanced geothermal systems, and geologic carbon storage. Here we show that a simple micromechanical model of slip avalanches in slowly deforming solids predicts the slip statistics observed over drastically different spatial scales, namely meter-scale microseismic observations and nanometer- to micrometer-scale nanoindentation experiments can be described with this model. Microseismic catalogs extracted from high-pressure fluid injection operations into geological basins with various lithologies and nanoindentation experiments on shale across a wide range of temperatures and mineral compositions yield statistics consistent with model predictions. This universality across materials, temperatures, and scales is consistent with the prediction that the slip statistics result from only a few basic properties. Previously debated deviations of the statistics in layered sedimentary formations are explained by finite-size and stress-integrative effects resulting from mechanically weak bedding planes. The slip statistics therefore provide important information about the structure and scales of the bedding planes. Conversely, the basin structure can also be used to predict the probability distribution for the sizes of triggered microseismic events.

items.title: Rotating Capacitive System for Measurement of a Third Order Gravity Gradient Based on a Single-Axis Mechanical Oscillator. Part I, Theory
items.summary: This paper is a feasibility study on a single-axis mechanical oscillator, mounted on a miniature circular rotating platform, that is proposed to be used for measuring a quantity proportional to the second vertical derivative of gravitational acceleration projected onto the oscillator's sensitivity axis. The latter is aligned with the axis of rotation. Part I establishes theoretical feasibility only. Design constraints, quantitative sensitivity, error budgets, and mobile platform performance will be addressed in Part II.

items.title: Interstitial Magnetoelectricity in Altermagnetic Electrides
items.summary: Electrides and altermagnets are two distinct yet intriguing classes of quantum materials, characterized by interstitial anionic electrons and nonrelativistic spin splitting, respectively. The recent prediction of Stoner-instability-driven altermagnetic electride provides a natural bridge between these two fields. Here, we investigate the magnetoelectric response and its related spin-polarized transport in the altermagnetic electride Zr$_2$N monolayer. Using the tight-binding Hubbard model and first-principles calculations, we find that the electric field can break the magnetic compensation between the two interstitial anionic electrons, inducing a finite net magnetization and giving rise to an interstitial electron mediated magnetoelectric response. The magnetoelectric response is further demonstrated through the electrical control of spin conductivity. Our results reveal a magnetoelectric effect in altermagnetic electrides, paving a way towards electride-based spintronic devices.

items.title: An equivariant classical density functional for ionic fluids at complex interfaces
items.summary: Predicting the combined effects of ionic packing and long-range electrostatics at complex interfaces is technologically important, but remains challenging without atomistic simulations. Here we present a machine-learned classical density functional for ionic fluids that combines a symmetry-adapted neural free energy for short-range correlations with explicit long-range electrostatics. Trained on three-dimensional equilibrium densities and bulk correlations of the full-Coulomb restricted primitive model, a single functional transfers to charge-patterned particles and atomically structured electrodes. Around anisotropic charged solutes, it reproduces the ionic structure and mean forces from molecular dynamics, including reversals of the bare electrostatic force. At metal electrodes, self-consistent coupling to metal atoms captures the redistribution of ionic and electrode charge and the loading-dependent capacitance enhancement produced by steps and bumps. Combined with mobilities determined independently from bulk molecular dynamics, the same functional describes the main features of charging dynamics and resolves geometry-dependent spatial relaxation. This framework can be extended to more complex ionic fluids, enabling efficient exploration of how composition and geometry control structure and response.

items.title: Equivariant learning of a transferable three-dimensional classical density functional
items.summary: Liquids exhibit collective behavior that depends sensitively on thermodynamic conditions, interfaces and confinement, yet predicting each new state commonly requires a separate atomistic simulation. Classical density functional theory offers a reusable variational description, but its central excess free-energy functional is generally unknown, and learned approximations for fluids have largely been developed in reduced-dimensional geometries. Here we show that this functional can be learned directly from fully three-dimensional canonical equilibrium density fields while preserving spatial symmetry and variational consistency, without free-energy or chemical-potential training labels. A functional learned from coarse three-dimensional density fields remains predictive at finer resolution, separating the sampling demands of training from the spatial resolution of subsequent predictions. A single learned functional transfers across temperatures, system sizes and statistical ensembles, and recovers the equation of state, liquid--vapor coexistence and interfacial broadening, none of which are used as training targets. Applied to complex three-dimensional geometries, it predicts the potential of mean force between colloids due to solvent mediation, and adsorption isotherms in an interconnected gyroid pore. These results demonstrate that molecular dynamics equilibrium density data can be converted into a transferable thermodynamic generator connecting microscopic liquid structure to response, phase behavior and collective phenomena.

items.title: Accelerating wave-scattering simulations with learned search directions
items.summary: Wave-scattering simulation requires solving a dense boundary-element system for every frequency, incidence and design. Krylov solvers build each search space from scratch, and it grows with problem size. Here we present BEMFormer, a solver that learns to generate search directions across systems of one integral equation and supplies geometry-specific directions through a coarse-grid correction. BEMFormer generalizes to unseen geometries, meshes and excitations, and to acoustic scattering after fine-tuning on eight geometries. It reproduces the measured radar cross-sections of benchmark targets. On a quadcopter with 1.04 million unknowns, 38 times the largest training problem, BEMFormer solves each system 30 times faster than a preconditioned Krylov solver. Both reach a radar cross-section deviation of about 1 dB, comparable to the difference between independent measurements and acceptable for engineering applications. These results show that solving million-unknown scattering problems in minutes is possible when the search space is learned rather than built from scratch.

items.title: photon number correlations in harmonics driven with classical and quantum light
items.summary: Recent reports of nonclassical intensity correlations in harmonic generation raised questions about whether strong harmonic correlations necessarily imply genuinely quantum behaviour. Here, we compare the low-photon-number perturbative harmonic generation driven by classical and bright squeezed vacuum sources. The latter generates strong auto- and cross-correlations in the harmonic spectrum. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and heralding measurements show that the cross-correlations are fully classical and can be explained by the common fluctuations from the driving field. A visible scaling of the measured correlation function with mean harmonic flux is observed, which is well-explained by a click detector-response model.

items.title: ResFrac Technical Writeup
items.summary: ResFrac is a combined hydraulic fracturing, reservoir, and hydraulic fracturing simulator. It describes multiphase fluid flow (black oil or compositional), proppant transport, transport of non-Newtonian fluid additives, and thermal transport. It also includes stress shadowing from fracture propagation and porothermoelastic responses from pressure change in the matrix. It uses constitutive equations that smoothly transition between equations for flow through an open crack to flow through a closed crack (with or without proppant). This document provides a detailed technical description of the code, along with validation simulations to confirm numerical accuracy.

items.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
items.summary: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.

items.title: Distinguishing photothermal and photoelectrokinetic contributions to flow in light-activated microchannel architectures
items.summary: Light-driven flows near Janus surfaces could power microfluidic devices without external hardware. These flows are often attributed to photoinduced electro- or diffusio-osmosis, but illumination also heats the surface, potentially driving natural convection. Here, we map flow and temperature around a UVA-illuminated TiO$_2$-Au Janus membrane using depth-resolved particle tracking and infrared thermometry. Recirculating rolls form on both sides, with no measurable net flow across the membrane. Their cubic, reversing velocity profile identifies horizontal (Hadley) convection, driven by a lateral temperature gradient as the gold film absorbs light. The measured profile agrees with wall-corrected Hadley theory using one fitted parameter. Adding 100 mM NaCl to suppress electrokinetic flows leaves the profile unchanged, indicating that convection dominates. Simulations show that convection falls below 1 $μ$m/s in thin channels, where surface-driven osmotic flows could dominate. Thus, device geometry and surface chemistry determine which mechanism governs light-driven microfluidic flows.

items.title: ESM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Whether AI Agents Understand Earth System Model Physics and Code
items.summary: AI coding agents that modify Earth System Model (ESM) code must preserve both software interfaces and the physical assumptions encoded in them. We introduce ESM-Bench, a benchmark of 60 developer-commit tasks from 6 repositories: Noah-MP, CLM5, SUMMA, ParFlow, MOM6, and VIC. The v5 corpus contains 17 physics-based bug fixes, 16 process-representation modifications, 13 parameterization-scheme selections, and 14 parameter-optimization tasks. Each task includes a scientific objective, parent-commit source files, a reference diff, and three stored prompt variants. An artifact audit confirms that all 60 reference diffs apply to their supplied starting files. We define an eight-item patch-review rubric and audit five archived patch fixtures against the implemented local checkers. None of the five fixture diffs applies to its supplied starting files, yet three text-pattern checkers return a pass. A ParFlow expression replay disagrees with the reference slopes, and a MOM6 pattern check detects an omitted update. Inspection also identifies a retained VIC reference assignment that overwrites the intended vegetation-specific albedo. These findings expose limits of reference patches and local proxies as correctness evidence. The release provides a reproducible corpus and diagnostic tools; complete expert validation, comparative agent performance, and full-model execution remain unmeasured on v5.

items.title: A Boundary Comparison Method for Gaussian Fluctuations in Planar Euclidean Optimization
items.summary: We develop a boundary comparison method for Gaussian fluctuations of optimization costs on planar random points, including traveling-salesman length, minimum perfect-matching length, and the Held--Karp relaxation. A local change can alter an optimal solution far from the modified points, making a direct decomposition into local contributions difficult. Our criterion requires the difference between the changes in the full and local costs caused by the same replacement to be controlled at the boundary scale, allowing a smaller-order $L^2$ excess. Under this condition, the centered difference between the total cost and the sum of independent cell costs vanishes in $L^2$. The multiscale argument shows that a nonvanishing variance of the cutting error would produce Gaussian tails incompatible with the boundary control. We obtain joint Gaussian limits for the three centered costs, using a conditional version for matching, and prove that the limiting covariance is positive definite in the Euclidean case. Convergence holds in quadratic Wasserstein distance for Poisson and fixed sample sizes. The results extend jointly to finitely many planar norms and to fixed sampling laws whose absolutely continuous component has a density positive almost everywhere on the square, with an arbitrary singular component.

items.title: Interior $W^{2,p}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
items.summary: In this paper, we extend Caffarelli's interior $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ regularity theory for the Monge-Ampère equation to the $k$-Hessian equation, $3\leq k\leq n-1$, under sharp Sobolev or Hölder assumptions on the solution. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we establish $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$ regularity for continuous $k$-convex solutions; the exponent $1$ is optimal even for constant density. Higher interior regularity holds under either of two assumptions: $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,k(k-1)/2}$, or $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,β}$ for some $1-2/k<β<1$. Under either assumption, if the density is positive and continuous, then $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,p}$ for every $1<p<\infty$; if the density is positive and belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^α$, then $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,α}$ for $0<α<1$. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we also establish global $W^{2,1}$ regularity on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{1,1}$ domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary values.

items.title: Central limit theorem for energies of determinantal point processes on complex manifolds I
items.summary: We study the Bergman determinantal point process associated with a positive line bundle on a compact Riemann surface. Consider the U-statistic given by the Green function, called the Green energy. For a configuration of $N$ points, the expectation of Green energy is $\frac12 N\log N+O(N)$, and the variance is $(\log 2-π^2/24)N+O(\log^2 N)$. We prove a central limit theorem for the Green energy by combining local Bergman kernel asymptotics with an expansion for the cumulants. A central limit theorem also holds for the logarithmic energy of Bergman determinantal point process on complex manifolds.

items.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
items.summary: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.

items.title: A proof of the chemical recurrence conjecture in two dimensions
items.summary: At the microscopic level, the dynamics of a network of chemical reactions can be modeled, in the well-mixed case, as a continuous-time Markov chain. This process counts the number of particles in each of the $d$ species as a function of time, and its state-dependent, polynomial jump rates are determined by the structure of the underlying reaction graph. Networks of chemical reactions whose reaction graphs are the union of strongly connected components are called \emph{weakly reversible}. The long-standing \emph{chemical recurrence conjecture} states that if a network is weakly reversible, then the associated Markov chain is positive recurrent. We prove this conjecture for $d=2$.

items.title: On the linearization of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation in $\mathbb{R}^N$
items.summary: Let $u$ be a positive radial solution of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation $$-Δu=u^p \qquad \text{in }\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad p>\frac{N+2}{N-2}. $$ In this paper we classify the bounded solutions of the associated linearized operator $-Δw -pu^{p-1}w=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. The resulting classification reveals the role of the threshold value $p=\frac{N + \sqrt{N^2 - 8N}}{4}$. In particular, above this threshold, the solutions are generated by the invariance of the problem under dilations and translations. Below this threshold, many new solutions appear, and their number tends to infinity as $p$ approaches the Joseph-Lundgren exponent and $N$ is large.

items.title: Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$
items.summary: Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$. The polytope is obtained from the dual of the cyclic polytope $C^{n}(2^{n}-1)$ by truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$. The resolution works over an arbitrary field and gives the sharp bound $(q^{n}-1)/(q-1)$ over the field with $q$ elements. More generally, every simple $n$-polytope whose facets can be properly coloured by $k\leq2^{n}-1$ colours becomes, after truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$, the orbit polytope of a small cover with the same chromatic number $k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq4$, a simple $n$-polytope with $χ=2^{n}-1$ which is the orbit space of both a small cover and a quasitoric manifold, and in the oriented case we obtain the sharp bound $2^{n-1}$ for every $n\geq4$.

items.title: Diophantine sets over global function fields
items.summary: Let $q\equiv 3\bmod 4$ be a prime power and let $K$ be a finite separable extension of the field of rational functions $\mathbb F_q(t)$, with constant field $\mathbb F_q$. We show that $\mathbb F_q[t]$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb F_q(t)$ and that the latter is Diophantine in $K$. We deduce from work of Demeyer that $K$ has the DPRM property: Diophantine sets over $K$ are the same as listable sets.

items.title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
items.summary: Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.

items.title: Double-dimer loops in the biased Aztec diamond converge to a diffeomorphic image of nested $CLE_4$
items.summary: We superimpose two independent domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of order $N$, with vertical weight $a>0$ and horizontal weight $1$. Represent each domino by the edge joining the centers of its two squares. The edges used by exactly one tiling form loops. After rescaling by $N^{-1}$, the full loop collection converges in law to the image of the nested conformal loop ensemble $\CLE_4$ under the diffeomorphism \[ w\longmapsto \frac{2(\Re w+\ii a\,\Im w)}{\sqrt{1+a^2}\,(1+|w|^2)} \] from the unit disk onto the liquid region of the rescaled diamond. Thus the bias rescales the horizontal and vertical coordinates of the unbiased limit. The topology of convergence records loop multiplicities and the order of traversal around each loop, up to reversal. Transfer estimates in the Krawtchouk basis control slab traversals and opposite crossings along entire sections, including where they meet the arctic ellipse. These estimates give tightness and, together with finite-puncture observables, identify the limit and rule out backtracking.

items.title: Matching Under Metric Privacy
items.summary: We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Through upper bounds and worst-case constructions, we establish the tight rate $Θ\!\left(n\min\{d,\log n\}/\varepsilon\right)$ for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. Benchmark experiments support $d\approx\log n$ as a practical guide to the transition between directly randomizing point coordinates and using Gumbel matching. Extensions to squared Euclidean costs enable private nonparametric two-sample hypothesis testing. These results show how the application's trust model guides representation and dimension choices for better utility: under local privacy, low-dimensional point representations reduce excess cost, while under central privacy, distance representations achieve the optimal rate even in high dimension.

items.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
items.summary: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm that computes multiplication in $A_n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2\in R^\times$ using $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage, given $A_n$ is defined with doubling parameters that are units with square roots in a fixed commutative algebra finitely generated as an $R$-module admitting a linear surjection onto the base ring preserving the identity. These conditions are satisfied by every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and over finite fields of odd characteristic, where the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ for $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, this is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. In single-core benchmarks over $\mathbb{R}$, an open-source implementation in the library fastCD is approximately $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

items.title: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
items.summary: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linear elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

items.title: Scheduling in Queueing Systems with Uncertain and Evolving Holding Costs
items.summary: In queueing systems, the holding costs of jobs may evolve in uncertain ways. For example, in content moderation for social media platforms, the cost of delaying the review of a content piece is proportional to its view trajectory, which fluctuates and is a priori unknown. To capture such uncertain and evolving holding cost patterns, we consider a queueing model where job states evolve based on a Markov chain with state-dependent instantaneous holding costs. We demonstrate that in the presence of such uncertain and evolving holding costs, the two canonical algorithmic principles, instantaneous-cost ($cμ$-rule) and expected-remaining-cost ($cμ/θ$-rule), are suboptimal. By viewing each job as a Markovian ski-rental problem, we develop a new index-based algorithm, Opportunity-adjusted Remaining Cost (OaRC), that adjusts to the opportunity of serving jobs in the future when uncertainty partly resolves. We show that the suboptimality gap of OaRC scales as $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{N})$, where $N$ is the system size. This bound shows that OaRC achieves asymptotic optimality for overloaded systems when the system size $N$ scales to infinity. Moreover, the bound is independent of the state-space size, which is a desirable property when job states contain contextual information. We corroborate our results with an extensive simulation study based on two holding cost patterns (online ads and user-generated content) that arise in content moderation for social media platforms. Our simulations based on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that OaRC consistently outperforms existing practice, which is based on the two canonical algorithmic principles.

items.title: Toward a Classification of Differentially $3$-Uniform Power Mappings over $\F_{p^2}$ and $\F_{p^3}$
items.summary: We study the classification, up to the CCZ-equivalence, of differentially $3$-uniform power mappings over quadratic and cubic extensions of prime fields. Over $\F_{p^2}$ exhaustive searches for primes $3<p<300$ found only the known families E1 and E4 for $p>23$. Over $\F_{p^3}$, the previously unexplained exponents for $7<p<200$ belong to a single family. We give an elementary proof that this family has differential uniformity at most $3$ for primes $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and prove that the bound is attained for $p>1444$.

items.title: Non-vanishing uniqueness threshold for hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi percolation in dimension at least three
items.summary: We study the threshold for the existence of exactly one unbounded cluster for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$ for $d\geq 3$. By recent results of Grebík and Recke and d'Achille et al., this "uniqueness threshold" $p_u(λ)$ tends to zero as the intensity $λ$ of the underlying Poisson point process tends to zero, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation defined on an ambient space from a family of geometric spaces that includes Cartesian products $\mathbb{H}^{d_1}\times\dots\times\mathbb{H}^{d_k}$ with $k,d_1,\dots,d_k\geq 2$. In contrast, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2$, Benjamini and Schramm have shown that $p_u(λ)$ tends to one as $λ$ tends to zero, and $p_u(λ)>1/2$ for all $λ>0$. An unpublished argument of D'Achille and Curien shows that for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$, the uniqueness threshold satisfies $p_u(λ)\leq 1/2$ for all $λ>0$. Here we will show that $\inf_{λ>0}p_u(λ)>0$ for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$. This answers a question of Grebík and Recke. The ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is a random tessellation of $\mathbb{H}^d$ introduced recently by D'Achille et al. In a sense that can be made precise, it corresponds to the $λ\searrow 0$ limit of the Poisson-Voronoi tessellation. Via a minor adaptation of our proof, we are also able to show that the uniqueness threshold of the ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is strictly positive.

items.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
items.summary: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $κ$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $Ω\left(κ^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1δ\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<δ<1$ and sufficiently large $κ$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $κ$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

items.title: Reconstruction of non-self-adjoint anisotropic and complex inclusions in the Calderón problem
items.summary: We generalize recent results on the monotonicity method, for inclusion detection in the partial data anisotropic Calderón problem, to very general non-self-adjoint perturbations. This involves a forward model that accounts for both the anisotropic real conductivity and the anisotropic permittivity, and the results hold in any spatial dimension $d\geq 2$. We assume that the inclusion boundaries can be reached from the domain boundary via a set on which the background conductivity is self-adjoint, and that a definiteness condition holds near the inclusion boundaries. Away from the inclusion boundaries we allow general $L^\infty$ non-self-adjoint perturbations. We only require unique continuation based on the self-adjoint part of the background conductivity, thus making the methods compatible with generic unique continuation results.

items.title: Self-similar solutions for capillary water waves
items.summary: In this paper we prove the existence of self-similar solutions to the capillary water wave problem. In particular, this implies finite-time formation of singularities in the form of a corner, and retraction from a corner due to the time-reversibility of the equations. Unlike most self-similar smooth solutions, the solutions with $2/3$ time-length scaling are seen in experiments like pinch-off retraction, bubble bursting or jet formation. The proof involves a new argument through the regularization of the Hamiltonian and does not require the existence of an approximate profile. We believe this strategy has further implications in the construction of self-similar solutions of dispersive PDE.

items.title: Cop-Win Edge Completion: Hardness, Structure, and Parameterized Algorithm
items.summary: We study Cop-Win Edge Completion: given a graph $G$, find the minimum number $\copfill(G)$ of edges whose addition lets one cop capture a visible robber. We first give an exact reduction from Dominating Set, constructing for every nonempty graph $H$ a graph $G_H$ on $2|V(H)|+2$ vertices with $\copfill(G_H)=γ(H)$. This resolves a complexity question of Mertzios et al. and implies NP-completeness even for connected graphs of diameter two with a dominating edge and domination number two. Interestingly, while Minimum Fill-in is fixed-parameter tractable in the number $k$ of added edges, Cop-Win Edge Completion, whose target class strictly contains the connected chordal graphs, is W[2]-hard parameterized by $k$, even by $k+γ(G)$. We then give two lower bounds. The first, $\copfill(G)\ge 2n-m-b-c-1$, where $n,m,b,c$ count vertices, edges, nontrivial blocks, and components, is tight for partial 2-trees, giving a linear-time algorithm for the optimum value and a quadratic-time construction; for outerplanar graphs, an optimum completion preserving outerplanarity is found in linear time. The second, based on the cycle space modulo the subspace generated by triangles, gives $\copfill(G)=c-1+\sum_{i=1}^r(\ell_i-3)$ for block-cactus graphs with long cycle blocks of lengths $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$. We also show how the optimum behaves under disjoint unions and joins, yielding a polynomial-time algorithm for $P_4$-sparse graphs, including cographs, and exact formulas for complete multipartite graphs. In contrast to partial 2-trees and block-cactus graphs, an optimum cop-win completion can be much smaller than a minimum chordal one, already on complete bipartite graphs. Finally, we give FPT algorithms for $k+\mathrm{nd}(G)$, for the twin-cover number $t$ alone in time $2^{O(t^3)}n^{O(1)}$, and for $k+\mathrm{tw}(G)$.

items.title: Nowhere Locally Metric-Minimising Saddle Surfaces
items.summary: We study the relation between the saddle property and local metric minimality for smooth surfaces in Euclidean spaces. Anton Petrunin and Stephan Stadler proved that every smooth strictly saddle surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is locally metric-minimising and expressed the expectation that this phenomenon fails in $\mathbb{R}^4$. We confirm this expectation and prove a stronger density result: Every smooth strictly saddle embedding of a closed disc into $\mathbb{R}^4$ can be approximated arbitrarily closely in the $C^\infty$-topology by smooth strictly saddle embeddings that are nowhere locally metric-minimising. In particular, nowhere locally metric-minimising saddle embeddings exist in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every $d \geq 4$. The main ingredient is the construction of non-trivial infinitesimal isometric deformations of saddle immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$ supported in arbitrarily small discs. We also provide an explicit twisted quadratic surface that is saddle in a neighbourhood of the origin but fails to be locally metric-minimising there, by deriving a necessary condition for metric minimality.

items.title: On the space of left orders on the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H \text{ and }G_\infty$
items.summary: We introduce the notion of a left order on a group with a certain specification of signs for the elements of a subset. We obtain an equivalent criterion for the existence of such a left order and apply it to obtain a new proof of the fact that any of the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H,\,G_\infty$ admits infinitely many non-Conradian left orders. We introduce the notion of separation of free subsemigroups of a left ordered group by its left translation induced actions on a point in the group and show that the above three groups admit such left orders. We also construct a subset of the set of left orders on any of the three groups, show the subset is a perfect set and give a new proof of the fact that the sets of the left orders on these three groups are uncountable.

items.title: Birational Algebraic Topology
items.summary: Over any qcqs scheme $S$, we show that inverting dense open immersions in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, $log\mbox{-}\mathcal{H}^\Box(S)$, and $\mathcal{P}_Σ(\mathrm{Sm}_S)$ yields the same birational $\infty$-category $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$. Unlike in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, all Nisnevich truncations and homotopy sheaves (including $π_0^{nis}$) of birational spaces remain birational, and hence $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is Postnikov complete. Moreover, the birational localization $L_{bir}$ commutes with the bar construction, ensuring effective delooping for every grouplike object in $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ and yielding an unstable birational higher-connectivity theorem. Building on these results, we establish birational analogs of the van Kampen theorem, the higher Galois theory of coverings, and the Freudenthal suspension theorem. When $S$ is geometrically unibranch with finitely many generic points, we show that $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is in fact an $\infty$-topos of homotopy dimension zero. Over a perfect field, we identify discrete birational group sheaves with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves whose $\mathbb{G}_m$-contraction vanishes, and deduce that $S^{2,1}$-nullification $L^{2,1}$ agrees with $L_{bir}$ on pointed $L^{2,1}$-connected spaces. Finally, over any field, we prove that $L_{bir}$ preserves generic values of $π_0^{\mathbb{A}^1}$ on motivic colimits of proper schemes; over perfect fields, it therefore detects their $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectivity and yields an equivalence $\mathbb{H}_0^{\mathbb{A}^1} \simeq \mathbb{H}_0^b$ for them, answering a question of Asok and Haesemeyer in greater generality.

items.title: Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees
items.summary: We study the Bergman projection $P_ω$ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_ω$, where $ω$ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_ω$ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $A^p_ω$ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $ω$ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_ω^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $L^p(ω) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $Ω\in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(Ω) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_Ω(\mathbb{D}) $.

items.title: Polynomial mixing for 2D Ising with plus boundary conditions
items.summary: We study the Glauber dynamics of the 2D Ising model at low temperatures. In the absence of boundary conditions, the mixing time on an $n\times n$ box is exponential in $n$ due to a bottleneck between metastable plus and minus phases. When the symmetry is broken via all-plus boundary conditions, it has been predicted in the physics literature since work of Lifshitz (1962) that from an all-minus initialization, the minus droplet shrinks via mean-curvature flow on timescales that are quadratic in $n$, and thus, the system equilibrates in polynomial time. On the rigorous side, the strongest result was a quasi-polynomial mixing time upper bound due to Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli (2013); a proof of polynomial mixing remained one of the major challenges in the field. We prove this polynomial mixing time bound at all low temperatures. The key step is to establish fast mixing of the interface separating the plus and minus phases on a box with Dobrushin boundary conditions. In simpler models of height functions, polynomial bounds tend to rely on exact harmonic properties and connections to a discrete heat equation. However, the Ising interface exhibits microscopic defects that necessitate the development of a more robust method. We address this via a new multiscale approach to bound mixing times of general disordered random-walk bridges that homogenize to a Brownian bridge at mesoscopic scales. Another notable ingredient is a novel application of censoring to reduce the mixing time problem to proving only a weak Poincaré inequality, or warm-start mixing bound, allowing us to assume suitable regularity conditions on the interface and bubbles.

items.title: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
items.summary: We prove that complete expanding Kähler--Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in complex manifolds, provided their closures admit neighborhoods with holomorphic immersions into Euclidean space. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler--Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces.
