On $\mathbb{R}$ and for $p=2$, we characterize which $φ$ generate $2$-WB convex families. The family of log-concave distributions is $2$-WB convex, as is the family of distributions with $s$-concave densities if and only if $s\geq-2$. General unimodality, corresponding to $s=-\infty$, is not preserved.

items.title: Fixed-parameter tractable computation of Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomials via tensor networks
items.summary: We give a thorough analysis of the time complexity of computing Reshetikhin--Tuareg knot polynomials via tensor contractions on the associated tensor networks, showing that the computation is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to a parameter at most linear in the tree-width of the input knot diagram. In particular, this gives a simpler proof to the sub-exponential bound $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$ for the time complexity of computing any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial. We present along with this paper, in SnapPy, the first general-purpose implementation of this algorithm, which computes any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial given its $R$-matrix and ribbon element. We stress the remarkable efficiency of our implementation by demonstrating that: (1) our implementation is several orders of magnitude faster than existing packages on computing the colored Jones polynomial; (2) our implementation is able to compute the Jones polynomial of (i) census knots with large width and over 200 crossings and (ii) some generic random knots with over 2000 crossings, in several hours using less than 10GB RAM, whereas Regina is not able to compute the Jones polynomial of these knots within a memory constraint of 160GB.

items.title: Logarithmic stability from finite-time boundary measurements in an infinite slab
items.summary: We prove logarithmic stability for an inverse convection--diffusion problem in an infinite slab from finite-time partial boundary measurements. The data consist of boundary fluxes generated by a fixed temporal profile and varying spatial Dirichlet inputs. For coefficients with fixed interior support and uniform Sobolev bounds, the data determine the exterior derivative of the drift and a gauge-invariant reaction term with a logarithmic modulus. Prescribing the divergence gives separate stability for the drift and reaction coefficients. The input and observation patches may be arbitrary nonempty open subsets of the same or opposite faces. The proof combines a quantitative passage from finite-time responses to a stationary boundary map with a Runge approximation estimate in the measured $H^{3/2}$ input norm. The first step uses sectorial semigroups on the unbounded slab; the second transfers the partial data to a full boundary map on an interior domain, where magnetic stability estimates apply. We also prove conditional stability for boundary-touching supports and uniqueness from one encoded input with unknown initial state. A tracer-transport application identifies an incompressible velocity and a reaction-loss coefficient.

items.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
items.summary: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set. As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero. An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.

items.title: Quantum Variance of Holomorphic Modular Forms and Benjamini-Schramm Convergence
items.summary: We study quantum variance for holomorphic modular forms of fixed weight on sequences of compact hyperbolic surfaces converging to the hyperbolic plane in the sense of Benjamini-Schramm. We first show that quantum ergodicity need not hold for an arbitrary choice of orthonormal basis, even for sequences with a uniform lower bound on the injectivity radius and a uniform spectral gap. The counterexample is constructed using a tower of coverings and arises from the identity contribution in the automorphic kernel. We then show that this obstruction is exceptional from the point of view of the choice of basis. For a Haar random orthonormal basis of holomorphic modular forms, the quantum variance converges to zero with probability tending to one uniformly over all observables with bounded supremum norm. The proof combines estimates for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a projected multiplication operator with the Haar expectation of the quantum variance, concentration of measure on the special unitary group and a finite-dimensional approximation of the space of observables.

items.title: Infinite polynomial patterns in large subsets of the rational numbers
items.summary: Inspired by a question of Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson, we prove two new results about infinite polynomial configurations in large subsets of the rational numbers. First, given a finite coloring of $\mathbb{Q}$, we show that there exists an infinite set $B = \{b_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}$ such that $$\{b_i, b_i^2 + b_j : i < j\}$$ is monochromatic. Second, we prove that every subset of positive density in the rational numbers contains a translate of such an infinite configuration. The corresponding results in the integers are both known to be false, so our results provide natural and relatively simple examples of combinatorial structures that distinguish between the Ramsey-theoretic properties of the rational numbers and the integers. The proofs of our main results build upon methods developed in a series of papers by Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson to translate from combinatorics into dynamics, where the core of the argument reduces to understanding the behavior of certain polynomial ergodic averages. The new dynamical tools required for this analysis are a Wiener--Wintner theorem for polynomially-twisted ergodic averages in $\mathbb{Q}$-systems and a structure theorem for Abramov $\mathbb{Q}$-systems.

items.title: Revisiting the role of reorthogonalisation in LSQR
items.summary: In this paper, we revisit the role of reorthogonalisation in the LSQR method for large-scale overdetermined linear least-squares problems. Motivated primarily by practical applications where matrix--vector products dominate the computational cost and only a limited number of iterations can be afforded because of time and/or memory restrictions, we investigate when reorthogonalisation can significantly accelerate convergence. Through synthetic test problems with controlled singular value distributions and experiments on practical sparse problems, we demonstrate that reorthogonalisation is particularly beneficial when the least-squares matrix has large outlying singular values. In such cases, loss of orthogonality can severely delay convergence. We explore the effectiveness of full (one-sided) reorthogonalisation when using LSQR, and present alternative reorthogonalisation strategies that can provide substantial acceleration compared to no reorthogonalisation and significant storage savings compared to full reorthogonalisation. The possibility of using low precision arithmetic for the reorthogonalisation is also investigated. We present bounds that demonstrate the quality of the solution depends on the level of orthogonality maintained by the selected reorthogonalisation strategy. Our results suggest that reorthogonalisation should be regarded as a practical tool for modern least-squares applications that can be employed instead of, or in addition to, preconditioning.

items.title: On the measure of Neighborhoods of Kakeya and Truncated Nikodym Sets
items.summary: We show that there exist Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $δ$-neighborhoods have measure $\lesssim |\logδ|^{-(d-1)}$. We also show that the measure of a $δ$-neighborhood of an $ε$-truncated Nikodym set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ $\gtrsim ε^{-1}|\logδ|^{-1}$, for $δ$ small enough. The sufficiently small scale depends on the Nikodym set and on $ε$.

items.title: The Hamilton cycle space in the Erdős--Rényi random graph process
items.summary: Let $G(n,m)$ denote the graph at step $m$ of the Erdős--Rényi random graph process on $n$ vertices. The process starts with the edgeless graph and adds one edge at each step, chosen uniformly at random from the missing edges. Let $τ_3$ be the first step at which the minimum degree of $G(n,m)$ reaches three. We answer a question of Christoph, Nenadov and Petrova [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 176 (2026) 254--267] by proving that, as $n$ tends to infinity through odd integers, with high probability the Hamilton cycles of $G(n,m)$ span its cycle space over $\Ftwo$ simultaneously for all $m\geτ_3$. On the same event, $G(n,m)$ is Hamilton-connected for every $m\geτ_3$.

items.title: Quasisymmetry of self-similar carpets
items.summary: We classify self-similar carpets obtained by repeating a fixed pattern in the same orientation on a square grid. All boundary cells are retained. The first approximation has a nonempty family of Jordan polyomino holes with pairwise disjoint closures in the interior of the unit square. Every quasisymmetry between two such carpets is the restriction of a square symmetry. Thus quasisymmetric, bi-Lipschitz, and isometric equivalence coincide. Two patterns give equivalent carpets exactly when their subdivision parameters have a common positive power and their retained cells agree up to symmetry on the common grid. The criterion extends to patterns periodic from the first generation. We also construct an area-zero square carpet with uniformly relatively separated peripheral circles and a quasisymmetric involution that sends a corner into an open side. Its quasisymmetry group is dihedral of order eight, and its isometries are the four rotations. It belongs to the quasisymmetric class of the standard middle-third carpet and to a different isometry class.

items.title: A uniform Picard-rank bound for Calabi Yau threefolds with finitely many flop chambers
items.summary: We prove that a smooth projective strict Calabi Yau threefold of sufficiently large Picard number either has infinitely many marked flop chambers or admits a fibration on a smooth flop model.

items.title: Global Stability Analysis of an Excitable Infinite-Dimensional System
items.summary: Motivated by the study of excitable control of infinite-dimensional linear systems, we investigate the global stability properties of a closed-loop system consisting of a stable linear infinite-dimensional plant and a non-monotone controller. The controller has piecewise-linear dynamics that resemble the FitzHugh-Nagumo model of neural behaviour. As our main result, we derive a checkable condition for the global exponential stability of the closed-loop system using the circle criterion. Finally we illustrate the stability result for a one-dimensional heat equation.

items.title: Fundamental gaps of the restricted fractional Laplacian on thin planar convex domains
items.summary: We study the fundamental gap $Γ_s(Ω)=λ_{2,s}(Ω)-λ_{1,s}(Ω)$ of the restricted Dirichlet fractional Laplacian for $0 < s < 1$. Building on the thin-rectangle estimates of Dyda and Kulczycki, we establish compact Mosco convergence of shifted quadratic forms and convergence of their eigenvalues on collapsing convex strips. This yields the next-order expansion, with exact coefficients, of each fixed eigenvalue of a thin rectangle. Let $G_s(θ)$ be the infimum of $D^{2s}Γ_s(Ω)$ over bounded open convex planar domains with $|Ω|/D^2=θ$, where $D$ denotes the diameter of $Ω$. As $θ\downarrow0$, we obtain $G_s(θ)\simκ_s\mathfrak{g}_{s+1/2}θ$ for $0 < s < 1/2$, $G_{1/2}(θ)\sim3π^2γθ\log(1/θ)$, and $G_s(θ)\sim3π^2β_sθ^{2-2s}$ for $1/2 < s < 1$. The constants $κ_s$, $γ$, and $β_s$ are determined by the transverse interval ground state. On $I=(-1/2,1/2)$, let $\mathfrak{g}_t$ be the infimum of the fundamental gap of the restricted Dirichlet operator $(-Δ)^t+V$ over convex $V\in C(\overline{I})$. For every $0 < t < 1$, this infimum is positive and is attained by a finite convex potential on $I$. Thin rectangles attain the optimal leading coefficient for $1/2\le s < 1$. For $0 < s < 1/2$, they do so exactly when the zero potential attains $\mathfrak{g}_{s+1/2}$. Finally, after diameter normalization, rescaling by $θ^{-1}$ in a minimum-width direction, and suitable rotations and translations, the closures of asymptotically minimizing domains converge to $[-1/2,1/2]\times[0,1]$ in Hausdorff distance.

items.title: What Environment Invariance Identifies: Minimal Invariant Sets in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
items.summary: Invariant causal prediction identifies the direct causes of a target $Y$ by searching for covariate sets whose conditional law of $Y$ is stable across environments. We state that criterion at the level of operators, calling a set $S$ invariant when the conditional mean embeddings of $Y$ given $X_S$ agree across environments, and characterise the resulting family exactly: under two conditions on the environments, which we state separately because they fail independently, the invariant sets are precisely those containing $PA(Y)$ and no descendant of $Y$. Two consequences follow. Invariance does not identify $PA(Y)$ uniquely, since every descendant-free superset is invariant as well; and $PA(Y)$ is the unique minimal invariant set. In finite samples, recovery requires the non-invariant sets to be separated from invariance by a margin, and the sample size splits into a screening term logarithmic in the ambient dimension and a term inherited from conditional mean embedding estimation, which is the binding one. The characterisation yields two selection rules with different failure modes, of which the conservative one controls false positives. Controlled experiments verify each population prediction directly, including the failure of uniqueness. They also show that invariance testing is a practical bottleneck: two natural designs are severely miscalibrated, while the selected test reduces but does not eliminate Type I error inflation.

items.title: On the quaternionic Goldberg conjecture
items.summary: We prove a quaternionic Kähler analogue of the Goldberg conjecture, namely: Let $(M^8,g,Ω)$ denote a compact $8$-manifold endowed with an $\mathrm{Sp}(2)\mathrm{Sp}(1)$-structure defined by a closed $4$-form $Ω$. If the metric $g$ is Einstein with non-negative scalar curvature then it is quaternionic Kähler i.e. $Ω$ is parallel. In fact we prove a slightly stronger result allowing for the scalar curvature to be negative under a suitable pinching condition by the square norm of the intrinsic torsion.

items.title: Scaling-invariant conditions for two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations
items.summary: We study the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with either far-field vacuum or non-vacuum. Under suitable smallness conditions on explicitly constructed scaling-invariant initial quantities, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions involving initial vacuum states and large oscillations. The two far-field regimes present distinct analytical difficulties and require different approaches to the {\it a priori} estimates. Although the two smallness criteria have different forms, they arise from the same intrinsic scaling of the equations. Our results provide a unified scaling-invariant framework for the global well-posedness of strong solutions in both far-field regimes.

items.title: Geometry of ground states in the long-range Ising model
items.summary: We study the ground states of the ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with long-range interactions and prescribed exterior data. We first show that the half-space configuration is a ground state, by means of a discrete calibration (which is the lattice counterpart of the calibrations of Cabré and Pagliari for nonlocal minimal surfaces). In dimension $d\ge2$ and for positive kernels, the half-space configuration is the unique minimizer in every finite domain, and it is "stable" with respect to perturbations of the exterior datum whose energy is below half of a positive excitation gap. This rigidity has no counterpart in the continuum. For general exterior data and positive kernels, we show that along a monotone family the minimizer is unique except for finitely many data. This can be considered a "generic uniqueness result" that provides the discrete counterpart of a recent work of Dipierro, Fernández-Real and Valdinoci in the continuum. We then introduce a pointwise notion, called perception, which is the lattice counterpart of the instability and stickiness phenomena for nonlocal minimal surfaces discovered by Dipierro, Savin and Valdinoci. We give a local criterion for the half-space configuration to be perceptive at a given site. Finally, we consider a box with exterior datum $+1$ above and below a slab and $-1$ on its sides. For fractional kernels with small exponent, the minimizer is $+1$ in the whole box, and its positive phase is connected. For short-range kernels, instead, the negative phase may enter the box, and the positive phase may be disconnected. Moreover, if the datum is $-1$ around the box and $+1$ only at distance two from it, the configuration identically $-1$ is perceptive at every boundary site of the box for fractional kernels with small exponent.

items.title: Wirsing type approximation over totally real and totally $p$-adic extensions
items.summary: In this paper, we establish Wirsing-type bounds for approximation of real and $p$-adic transcendental numbers by totally real and totally $p$-adic algebraic numbers, respectively. More precisely, for every $n\ge 1$, we show that every transcendental $ξ\in\mathbb{Q}_p$ admits infinitely many totally $p$-adic algebraic approximants $α$ of degree at most $n$ satisfying $0<|ξ-α|_p\ll H(α)^{-1-\lceil n/2\rceil}$. We improve this bound for even $n\ge 4$. For each $n\geq 2$, we also show that every real number $ξ$ that is not algebraic of degree at most $n$ admits totally real approximants of degree at most $n$ with a bound stronger than Wirsing's. In both cases, we can also restrict the approximants to be totally $\ell$-adic for every prime $\ell$ in a fixed finite set.

items.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
items.summary: We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $ν^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $ν$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-\mathsf{r}ν^{\frac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-νt}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim ν^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $ν$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$.

items.title: Polynomial spaces are locally Paley-Wiener: local spectral geometry, sampling, and interpolation
items.summary: We identify the local Paley-Wiener structure of multivariate polynomial spaces on centrally symmetric convex bodies and apply it to sampling and interpolation. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density in the interior, the normalized reproducing kernel at scale $1/n$ converges to the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on the dual unit ball of the Baran metric. We call this set the local spectral body. It describes the frequencies available to polynomials near each point. By recovering local bandlimited functions together with their $L^2$ norms, we obtain bulk universality and Christoffel asymptotics uniformly on compact subsets of the interior. This connection allows us to use Fourier methods to study polynomial sampling. If weighted sampling is uniformly stable with asymptotically one node per polynomial coefficient, almost every local spectral body must admit an exponential Riesz basis. Combining this result with Ortega-Cerdà's theorem for smooth spectra, we show that in dimension $d\ge2$, a $C^2$ boundary with everywhere positive curvature forces a positive proportion of extra sampling nodes. This rules out uniformly stable complete interpolation on such bodies. The same lower bound on the number of nodes applies to positive cubature exact through degree $2n$, since such a rule preserves the squared $L^2$ norm of every polynomial of degree at most $n$. The corresponding local-to-global problem remains open. If the local spectral body at every interior point admits an exponential Riesz basis, can one choose exactly as many nodes as polynomial coefficients at each degree so that sampling and interpolation are uniformly stable on the whole body?

items.title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times
items.summary: We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. The dynamics are difficult to recover as each vehicle's position is measured only at two points, and its trajectory between them is unknown. By combining Neural ODEs with a local density approximation, we learn a follow-the-leader model whose speed--density relation is a neural network. With such sparse data, an unconstrained network may learn physically unrealistic relations, such as negative speeds or non-zero speeds on a fully congested road. We therefore introduce a normalization that, applied to a monotone neural network with a learned regime change, enforces the endpoint conditions, guaranteeing an admissible speed--density relation while provably retaining the ability to approximate any admissible one. We validate the method on first- and second-order simulations, recovering the speed--density relation of the first-order model and reconstructing the trajectories of both models, with mean maximum position errors of 2.50~m and 2.51~m, respectively, on a 125~m road segment. On real-world ring-road data, the proposed model still yields an admissible relation, whereas both baselines violate the constraints; the large spread in the data, however, highlights the limitations of a first-order model with homogeneous driver behaviors.

items.title: Equilibrium Numbers in Non-Square Bimatrix Games
items.summary: Bimatrix games may have an exponential number of mixed Nash equilibria if both dimensions of the game are allowed to grow. Bounds on their maximal number give structural insights that have been used to construct hard-to-solve games. We show new sharp or asymptotically sharp bounds on the (polynomial) number of equilibria for generic games where one dimension of the game is fixed and the number of strategies of the other player grows. These results go beyond the hitherto studied square games. Our methods employ combinatorial properties of polytopes, and recent obstructions that relate to the graph of those polytopes. For $n\ge5$, we construct $3\times n$ games that have all $2n+1$ vertices of the best-response polytope as equilibrium strategies, proved using a simple case of the 4-color theorem for planar graphs. Generic $4\times 5$ games are shown to have at most 17 equilibria, using computer calculations with existing datasets for all combinatorial types of the relevant polytopes. For $d\times n$ games, we construct games where all but a fraction of $O(1/n)$ of the maximum number of vertices are equilibrium strategies.

items.title: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
items.summary: A long-standing Conjecture of S. Negami states that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. It is known that the Conjecture is equivalent to the fact that \emph{the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ has no finite planar cover}. We prove three theorems showing that the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ admits no planar cover with certain structural properties, and that the minimal planar cover of $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ (if it exists) must be $4$-connected.

items.title: Restrictions of planar doubling measures to piecewise C1 Jordan domains
items.summary: We compare the class $\mathscr R(Ω)$ of restrictions of full-support planar doubling measures with the class $\mathcal D(Ω)$ of internal doubling measures on a piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domain. These classes coincide in the absence of zero-interior-angle cusps. At any such cusp, $\mathscr R(Ω)\setminus\mathcal D(Ω)$ is nonempty. For power-comparable widths, $\mathcal D(Ω)\subsetneq\mathscr R(Ω)$; for infinitely flat widths the two classes are disjoint. Under smooth endpoint regularity, finite versus infinite contact order gives these two alternatives. Under only $C^1$ regularity, finite logarithmic order does not determine whether the classes intersect, and examples with nonempty intersection and neither class containing the other also occur. For an individual internal measure, membership in $\mathscr R(Ω)$ is characterized by a potential inequality for its axial projection. We prove this criterion by a positive-kernel construction and Whitney mass replacement, and also obtain sufficient conditions for variable-power widths and an independent finite-system criterion.

items.title: Finite simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes
items.summary: A theorem by Guralnick classifying finite simple groups with subgroups of prime power index implies that $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ is the unique finite non-abelian simple group whose maximal subgroups all have prime power index. Motivated by this result and appealing to Li and Li's classification of primitive permutation groups of degree $p^a q^b$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, we classify all finite non-abelian simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes, proving that they are precisely $A_5$, $A_6$, $A_7$, $A_8$, ${\rm PSL}(2,7)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,8)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,11)$, ${\rm PSp}(4,3)$, ${\rm PSU}(3,3)$, and ${\rm PSU}(3,4)$.

items.title: Dirichlet heat kernel estimates for fractional Laplacian under non-local perturbation
items.summary: For $d\geq 1$ and $0<β<α<2$, consider a family of non-local operators $$\mathcal{S}^{b}f(x):=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\mathcal{A}(d,-β)\int_{ \{z\in \mathbb{R}^d: |z|>\varepsilon\}}(f(x+z)-f(x))\frac{b(x,z)}{|z|^{d+β}}\,{\mathrm{d}z},$$ and $b(x,z)$ is a bounded measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with $b(x,z)=b(x,-z)$ for every $x,z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$. Here ${\mathcal{A}}(d, -β)$ is the normalizing constant for which $\mathcal{S}^b=-(-Δ)^{β/2}$ when $b(x, z)\equiv 1$. It is known that if $b(x, z) \geq -\frac{\mathcal{A}(d, -α)} {\mathcal{A}(d, -β)}\, |z|^{β-α}$ for a.e. $z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, then $\mathcal{L}^b$ admits a unique fundamental solution $p^{b}(t,x,y)$, which determines a conservative Feller process $X^{b}$ with the strong Feller property. In this paper, we study the subprocess $X^{b,D}$ of $X^{b}$ killed upon leaving a $C^{1,1}$ open set $D\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. We establish explicit small-time upper and lower bounds for its transition density function $p^{b}_{D}(t,x,y)$. These estimates are uniform in $b$: all constants depend on $b$ only through an upper bound of $\|b\|_{\infty}$. Moreover, $b$ enters the form of the upper bound only through the size of its large positive part, $\mathrm{ess\,sup}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d},\,|z|>λ}b(x,z)^{+}$ for a fixed $λ>0$. When the jump kernel of $\mathcal{L}^b$ satisfies matching upper and lower bounds, either of $α$-stable type or of mixed $α$- and $β$-stable type, the small-time estimates for $p^{b}_{D}(t,x,y)$ are sharp. For bounded $D$, we also obtain large-time estimates governed by the principal eigenvalue of the generator of $X^{b,D}$. Under a non-degeneracy condition on the jump kernel, we further establish sharp two-sided estimates on the Green function of $X^{b, D}$ in bounded $C^{1,1}$ open sets.

items.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
items.summary: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.

items.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. II
items.summary: This paper is the second in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we solve the linear preserver problem for the Cullis' determinant defined on the spaces of matrices of size $n\times k$ with $k \ge 4,\; n \ge k + 2$ and $n + k$ is odd. In comparison with the case when $n + k$ is even, in this case linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant could be singular and are represented as a sum of two linear maps: first is two-sided matrix multiplication and second is any linear map whose image consists of matrices, all rows of which are equal.

items.title: Proper and Optimal Scoring Rules for Risk-Averse Agents
items.summary: Scoring rules are used to elicit probabilistic beliefs through payments that depend on reports and realised outcomes. We ask how these rules should be designed to induce truthful reporting and incentivise costly information acquisition when the agent is risk averse. For agents with entropic risk preferences in finite state spaces, we characterise proper scoring rules through an exponential transformation, derive optimal structures for information acquisition under bounded payments, and obtain explicit optimal coefficients in the binary case. The risk-neutral limit preserves properness and, in the binary case, optimality, while recovering the optimal betting structure for nonbinary states. For optimal design in the binary model, it suffices to focus on rules whose associated concave function is affine on each side of the prior. The optimal coefficients depend only on the prior and the risk-aversion parameter. The binary optimal rules we construct also admit an exact transformation from a particular risk-neutral optimal rule. In the nonbinary model, optimal design reduces to choosing the best prior bound in a transformed betting mechanism.

items.title: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
items.summary: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.

items.title: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
items.summary: In this paper, we study positive solutions to the problem \begin{equation*} -Δu = |x|^{-s_2}u^{2^*(s_2)-1} - \la |x|^{-s_1}u^{p-1} \quad \text{in }\Om, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partial\Om, \end{equation*} where $\Om\subset\R^N$ ($N\ge 3$) is a bounded domain with $0\in\partial\Om$, $0\le s_1<s_2<2$, $2^*(s)=\frac{2(N-s)}{N-2}$, $2^*(s_2)<p<2^*(s_1)$, and $\la>0$. This is the Li--Lin open problem \cite{LL} in the form studied by Cerami, Zhong, and Zou \cite{CZZ} and by Tang and Tang \cite{TT1}. Assume that $\partial\Om$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $0$ with a leading term of homogeneity $1+α$, and set $θ=\frac{(N-2)(2^*(s_1)-p)}{2}$. We prove that a solution exists for every $\la>0$ if $θ>α$ and the $α$-mean curvature of $\partial\Om$ at $0$ is negative, whereas $\la^*=\sup\{\la>0:\text{a solution exists}\}$ is finite if $θ\leα$, without any curvature assumption. For $α=1$, this removes the restriction to almost every $\la$ in \cite[Theorem 1.6]{CZZ}, answers a question of Zou \cite{Z}, and disproves the conjecture in \cite[Remark 1.7]{TT1}. The proofs rely on a scale-invariant estimate uniform in $\la$, a Hadamard-type identity for the half-space extremal and a localized Pohozaev identity combined with sharp decay estimates. Notably, no regularity of $\partial\Om$ is required away from $0$.

items.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
items.summary: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models for autonomous driving use chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to guide action generation, but incur substantial memory and computational costs. We study structured pruning for these models, focusing on preserving both scene understanding and trajectory prediction. Our analysis of Taylor importance in Alpamayo-1.5-10B shows that reasoning and trajectory objectives assign different importance to the same vision-language model (VLM) structures. In the action expert, MLP channels exhibit more stable importance rankings across denoising steps than query heads, and a small fraction of channels accounts for most of the measured importance. Based on these findings, we propose MoOP, which combines importance ranks from both objectives for VLM pruning and aggregates stepwise importance to select a fixed subset of expert MLP channels. At 24.0% total parameter reduction, VLM-only pruning with MoOP performs comparably to or slightly better than the strongest baselines in driving, while retaining 94.0% of the dense model's LingoQA score, far above all other methods. At a higher reduction of 30.0%, MoOP degrades much less than every other method, as it is the only one whose reasoning does not collapse. Removing 93.75% of expert MLP channels increases total parameter reduction to 39.4%, with nearly unchanged open-loop errors relative to VLM-only pruning and competitive closed-loop performance. The resulting model achieves a 1.37x end-to-end inference speedup and 36.6% lower peak memory than the dense model, without post-pruning fine-tuning.

items.title: Efficient Cost-Aware LLM Evaluation via Bayesian Bandit Gittins Indices
items.summary: Exhaustively evaluating every candidate LLM configuration on every benchmark item to identify a high-performing one is costly. We formulate configuration selection as a cost-aware Bayesian bandit problem and propose GittinsEval, inspired by Bayesian-optimal Gittins-index policies for Markov chain selection. We augment this policy with a separate anytime recommendation rule over both fully and partially evaluated configurations, using an LCB-style score to account for posterior uncertainty. GittinsEval is computationally efficient, requiring only lightweight online updates after offline precomputation. Across tasks with varying numbers of candidates and examples, GittinsEval is consistently competitive, with particularly strong gains over the Bayesian optimization baselines on few-candidate large-example benchmarks and over cost-unaware frequentist baselines on large-candidate tasks. Crucially, GittinsEval often attains near-zero simple regret using only 1%-2% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost; it also offers a stopping rule that typically triggers at 1%-10% with an appropriate cost--quality tradeoff parameter.

items.title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
items.summary: Exploring a scene from as little as a single photo requires generating a long, camera-controlled walkthrough that extends far beyond what was captured, yet remains consistent upon return. Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them. Layout-conditioned methods provide such an anchor and precise control over what appears where, but rely on layouts that are typically authored by hand. Both limitations arise because, beyond what was captured, nothing anchors the video model unless a human authors one. To overcome both, we propose Lyris, a long video generation framework that never leaves the video model without an anchor: a persistent point-cloud memory where the scene has been observed or generated, and a 3D layout that a vision-language model authors where it has not. Our key insight is that the interface between the two models can be surprisingly coarse. A layout of one labeled 3D box per object is simple enough for a vision-language model to author (and for a user to edit), yet expressive enough for a video model to follow once rendered along the camera path. We demonstrate walkthroughs of over three minutes and 50 meters from a single photo, passing through doorways into rooms it never shows. When evaluated on minute-long round trips across four datasets, Lyris outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a wide margin, reducing camera error by 3.8x and improving consistency upon return by 22% on average.

items.title: Modern Self-Supervised Vision Transformers Are Pareidolic
items.summary: In human perception, pareidolia is the tendency to perceive a meaningful pattern, such as a face, in a random or ambiguous stimulus.We find a similar phenomenon in modern self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs): on white noise, which contains neither objects nor spatial structure, a few directions of their features still form spatially coherent patterns across the patches, imposed by the features themselves.We call this behavior pareidolia, and the span of these directions the pareidolic subspace.On natural images, it holds most of the feature variance in DINOv2 and DINOv3 but little in DINO.This excess explains why DINOv2 and DINOv3, despite stronger dense features, fall far behind DINO in object emergence, the hallmark ability of self-supervised ViTs to identify the patches of an object on their own.Our experiments further show that scaling down their pareidolic subspaces steadily restores their ability to discover objects, so their object emergence is hindered rather than lost.These findings naturally lead to a training-free calibration: Pareidolia Subspace Calibration(PSC) measures the pareidolic subspace only on a noise input and then calibrates the features of natural inputs by scaling its directions down to the variance level of the remaining directions.Across diverse object emergence tasks, PSC improves DINOv2 and DINOv3 by up to 31.7 CorLoc on object discovery, 30.2 maxF on saliency detection and 59.9~$\mathcal{J}$ on video object segmentation.To identify the cause of pareidolia, we trace it block by block and find that it forms in the middle blocks of every self-supervised model we examine but stays strong to the last block only in models trained with a patch-level loss; controlled training confirms that an image-level loss alone lets it fade.

items.title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
items.summary: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To address this challenge, we introduce Integral, which converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across the two capabilities. Integral implements this design through two complementary components. Abstraction Fusion constructs shared visual tokens by aggregating hierarchical representations from the frozen vision encoder, while Block-wise MoT introduces a lightweight generative stream that interacts with the vision-language model only at block boundaries. Our approach effectively preserves the pretrained understanding capability while extending it to strong visual generation. Controlled comparisons further demonstrate that sharing visual representations between understanding and generation substantially improves generative learning compared with using a separate visual representation space, despite comparable reconstruction fidelity. These results suggest that representations learned by pretrained vision-language models already provide an effective foundation for visual generation.

items.title: Two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems
items.summary: Quantum interactive proof systems can be parallelized to three messages, as shown by Kitaev and Watrous (STOC 2000), perhaps their most striking distinction from classical counterparts. In this work, we establish that any quantum interactive proof system can further be parallelized to two messages, with the verifier sending halves of EPR pairs (``quantum public coins'') and, after the prover's response, using only stoquastic verification. Technically, we strengthen ${\sf QIP}(3) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}$ of Jain, Ji, Upadhyay, and Watrous (JACM, 2011) and fully characterize two-message quantum interactive proof systems by proving \[ {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf StoqAM} = {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf QAM} = {\sf QIP}(2) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}. \] Our main technical contributions show that Close Image to Uniform (CIUniform), which is naturally in the stoquastic version of ${\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf QAM}$, is $\sf PSPACE$-hard via transforming the sum-check protocol of Shamir (JACM, 1992) and Shen (JACM, 1992) into a CIUniform instance consisting of an efficient sampler whose image distribution is exactly uniform for some input distribution when the underlying quantified Boolean formula is true.

items.title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: CLIP-style dual encoders map images and text through two separate towers into a shared embedding space, where the two modalities occupy distinct regions separated by a modality gap. Retrieval fails when wrong matches, or hard negatives, outrank the correct one, and the gap is the usual suspect. Yet removing it post hoc degrades retrieval on every CLIP checkpoint we test. We introduce a paired statistic that identifies directions where the two towers agree more on hard negatives than on matched pairs. Mildly attenuating these directions improves retrieval while largely preserving the gap. We arrive at this correction through weight-space programming: guided by the statistic, an LLM agent inspects both towers and writes closed-form weight edits without backpropagation. Free to edit any component, the agent improves COCO test retrieval on all 13 CLIP checkpoints and edits an output projection in 12 of the 13. We distill and refine its recurring correction into TowerBridge, a closed-form recipe motivated by a first-order analysis of the hard-negative margin. Computed in seconds from 25,000 labelled pairs, it requires no model-specific tuning and leaves the architecture and inference cost unchanged. TowerBridge improves COCO test retrieval by 16.8 RSUM and Flickr30k test retrieval by 6.6 on average across all 21 evaluated CLIP checkpoints, including 8 unseen by the agent, while limiting any drop in ImageNet zero-shot accuracy to 0.5 points. It also reduces hubness on all 21 checkpoints and improves retrieval on 4 of 5 dual encoders from other families.

items.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
items.summary: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-4, 14.7B) across 15,200 math benchmark attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors within each model's capability frontier. Applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations across these failure points, we demonstrate a consistent decoupling between monitoring and control. On monitoring, all four models fail to detect their own errors. Verbalized confidence does not distinguish mistake steps from sound reasoning, yielding near-chance within-position AUROCs between 0.500 and 0.561. Even at a model's first reasoning error, trajectory confidence remains saturated at 95.1% to 99.9%, with noticeable drops ($\ge 10$ points) appearing on fewer than 9% of errors in Llama and under 1.6% in the other three models. In contrast, models respond readily to external uncertainty: injecting a low-confidence tag (10%) at the error step significantly increases downstream correction across all models (+3.7 to +22.5 points over format-matched 95% certainty; all $p \le 0.0022$), reaching up to 38.5% under active rethinking instructions. However, injecting doubt onto already-correct steps causes models to discard valid reasoning, reducing solve rates by up to 22.8 points. Inference-time self-correction is thus bottlenecked by in-situ error detection rather than downstream repair capacity: models readily steer toward recovery when prompted with doubt, yet fail to self-monitor during generation.

items.title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling
items.summary: Understanding how genetic perturbations affect cellular behaviour is essential for studying gene function and regulatory mechanisms. Large-scale CRISPR screens measure these effects across thousands of genes, but cover relatively few cellular contexts. Predicting perturbation responses in unseen cell types and identifying perturbed genes from their transcriptional effects therefore remain challenging. Here, we show that both tasks can be addressed through a common linear decomposition of transcriptional responses into shared and perturbation-specific components. Building on this principle, we introduce BiPert, a simple linear framework for both forward perturbation prediction and inverse identification. For forward prediction, BiPert outperforms existing methods that use no external biological knowledge when predicting gene expression changes in unseen cell lines. Its few-shot extension, BiPert-FS, adapts to new cell lines using as few as ten measured perturbations. For inverse identification, BiPert-ID identifies perturbed genes from single-cell expression profiles, outperforming deep-learning methods in unseen cell lines and donors. We further show that perturbations whose effects transfer more consistently across cellular contexts are also easier to identify, even after controlling for perturbation effect size. Together, these results establish a connection between perturbation transfer and identification, and demonstrate that simple linear models provide strong, interpretable baselines for both tasks.

items.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
items.summary: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image. MIPA encourages this by maximizing mutual information between cross-view assignments while avoiding trivial solutions in which all real samples are assigned to only a few synthetic prototypes. Evaluations on image classification benchmarks show that synthetic data generated by MIPA yield higher-quality representations than existing distillation approaches while reducing time and storage demands during distillation.

items.title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automation will help future mobile networks translate high-level network intents into concrete network optimization or control actions. However, existing approaches often focus on intent management and orchestration, leaving the adaptation of underlying network optimization and control functions largely unaddressed. This article proposes a triadic agentic AI framework that co-designs intent management and intent fulfillment through three agents: an interpreter, powered by a language model, that translates and refines intents into machine-readable optimization templates; an optimizer that adapts controller policies to intent specifications; and a controller that performs fast decision-making. We discuss the design space of each agent and how the workflow can be embedded across network architectural domains. Finally, we develop a concrete realization combining a language-model interpreter with Bayesian optimization for the optimizer and multi-objective reinforcement learning for the controller, and evaluate it in a radio resource management case study for differentiated connectivity. Results demonstrate how the agentic AI framework can connect high-level intents with runtime network control, showing adaptability of intent specifications and control policies to service requirements and changing network conditions.

items.title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
items.summary: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each finding segmented. On the 200 ReXGroundingCT validation scans, CTLink achieved a hit rate of 0.816, an instance F1 score of 0.456, and a mean Dice score of 0.400, compared with 0.533, 0.175, and 0.234 for VoxTell, a publicly available text-prompted segmentation model (P < .001 for all). On the test set of the MICCAI 2026 ReXGrounding challenge, an ensemble of seven CTLink models achieved the highest hit rate (0.782) and instance F1 score (0.386) of all 48 participating teams. On 50 test scans segmented twice by independent radiologists, CTLink matched or exceeded inter-rater agreement. Diffuse non-focal findings remained the main limitation, partly because their extent is outlined inconsistently even between radiologists. The CTLink model weights are available at https://huggingface.co/rajpurkarlab/CTLink, and the dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGroundingCT.

items.title: A Mixed-Methods Study of Personal Software Creation
items.summary: People have long wanted software shaped around their own data, routines, and preferences. We refer to such software as \emph{personal software}. For decades, programming expertise limited who could build it: people without that expertise could build software only within constrained end-user programming tools, such as spreadsheets. AI coding agents seem to remove this bottleneck by letting people build full applications from natural-language descriptions, and many people now build and share personal software publicly. Yet personal software has rarely been studied at scale: we know little about what people build and why, how they build it, and what opportunities and challenges they encounter. We investigate these questions with a mixed-methods study. A grey-literature review examines 6,168 web and Reddit posts, and an observation study follows eight people as they build software for their own needs with AI coding agents and use it for up to a week. We find that creators value personal software for how closely it fits a particular person or community. The software takes shape as creators react to what the agent builds: most functionality emerged during building, and creators' effort shifted from writing code to checking it.

items.title: LeJEPA Features Are Not Isotropic, and Should Not Be
items.summary: The SIGReg term in LeJEPA regularizes features to have an isotropic Gaussian distribution. Our first result is to show that this regularizer, in practice, cannot achieve its goal. We design a modified regularizer to enforce the objective better. This leads to slightly improved performance. For example, on ImageNet-100, our modified regularizer reaches the final accuracy of SIGReg in 1.3$\times$ fewer epochs. Our second result argues that self-supervised encoders should not have isotropic Gaussian features. We show that the alignment term in LeJEPA conflicts with SIGReg, because it couples the magnitude of the features with their directions. In contrast, isotropic Gaussian features would entail independent magnitude and directions. Features obtained with LeJEPA are, in fact, not isotropic. So LeJEPA has two issues. Its regularizer is weak, and the isotropic Gaussian target is too strict. Our third result is about reformulating the isotropic Gaussian regularizer to enforce only the marginal distributions of the magnitude and direction, without enforcing independence. This leads to a simple regularization term, PolarReg, that can be optimized reliably across many different datasets, batch sizes and embedding dimensions without any hyper-parameter changes. On ImageNet-1k, our technique matches the accuracy of LeJEPA and its variants in 4.7$\times$ fewer epochs. It improves the final accuracy by 1.8 points.

items.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning. Every question is verified to require exploration and answered from 3D annotations, masked-evidence questions test whether models know when to abstain, and over 95% of sampled questions are confirmed correct by human verification. Evaluations of 23 proprietary, open-weight, and spatially specialized VLMs reveal that the strongest models do seek evidence with purpose but lose much of it to limited memory, whereas weaker and specialized models explore no better than a random walk or fail to reason over the evidence they are given, pointing to memory and evidence-grounded reasoning as the next targets for active spatial intelligence.

items.title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation
items.summary: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models. By casting diverse understanding and generation problems into a shared token representation, GPT enables a single architecture and unified optimization loop to master heterogeneous tasks across massive corpora, giving rise to powerful foundation models for natural language. In contrast, 4D spatiotemporal vision lacks a common representational protocol: perception (such as depth and camera estimation) and generation are either handled by separate one-way pipelines or bolted together from unaligned single-modality spaces. In this work, we introduce WorldLatent, a framework that formulates a unified 4D latent space as a common protocol for both world perception and generation. Rather than relying on fragmented, task-specific models or stacked single-modality representations, our framework proposes a multimodal VAE architecture that compresses and fuses complex 4D visual appearance, geometry, and dynamics into a single structured latent representation. Within this formulation, perception and generation operate as complementary denoising processes over the same latent space, enabling one generative model to learn both capabilities simultaneously within a single training loop. Experiments across representative 4D benchmarks verify that our fused latent protocol achieves specialist-level zero-shot 4D perception, coherent 4D generation, and controllable editing from a single model. By demonstrating that diverse 4D tasks can be seamlessly unified under a shared representational protocol, our work provides a scalable foundation for general-purpose 4D spatial intelligence.

items.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
items.summary: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents. This allows independent work to progress concurrently while supporting tightly coupled manipulation when necessary. Across 72 real-world rollouts covering 25 task/platform settings, ACAP reduces task-balanced time cost by 28.2% compared with a single-agent Direct Policy, with improvements across Fully Parallel, Parallel-Sequential, and Collaborative tasks. Across all eight Collaborative settings, ACAP also achieves lower mean time cost than Fixed Delegation, where only member agents can control their assigned groups. An additional 90-rollout study shows lower mean 30-minute-capped time cost than Direct on all six tasks. We further demonstrate mobile manipulation using the same member interface for chassis and torso control. We present the framework and a real-world rollout dataset containing observations, generated programs, actions, and feedback to support research on how coding agents reason and act in the physical world.

items.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
items.summary: LLM agentic workflows increasingly employ different models for specialized roles. Users may prefer different trade-offs between task quality and deployment cost, sometimes also considering latency. Finding good assignments incurs a separate search cost from evaluating multiple candidates. We introduce Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of single-objective cost-aware Gittins search for Pareto recommendation. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs: assignments that cost more to deploy also cost more to evaluate. The search alternates between seeking higher quality and lower deployment cost, reusing each evaluation to inform both searches. After each batch, CC-Gittins recommends assignments that are nondominated under uncertainty-adjusted estimates of quality and deployment cost. We evaluate CC-Gittins on eight quality--cost matrices from workflows with two to five roles and up to 1,681 candidate assignments. We also evaluate the method with latency as a third objective. Across the eight benchmarks, CC-Gittins recovers a substantial fraction of the true Pareto frontier at roughly 10% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost, and recovers most of the frontier with few false positives by 30%.

items.title: Decoupling Faults from Uncertainty: Message-Efficient Byzantine Agreement with Local Predictions
items.summary: Byzantine Agreement protocols are traditionally designed under worst-case uncertainty about which processes are faulty, coupling the adversary's corruption budget $t$ with the system's epistemic uncertainty. Recent work showed that auxiliary failure predictions can improve round complexity, but cannot improve communication complexity when prediction errors are unconstrained. In this paper, we initiate a theoretical study of the complementary question: how much can Byzantine Agreement benefit when each process is guaranteed a local bound on its prediction error? We study this question through the local $k$-error prediction model, in which each process receives a local classification vector differing from the ground truth in at most $k$ positions. The predictions need not be common, and honest processes may hold substantially different views about whom to trust. Under this promise model -- where correctness relies on the local error bound holding -- we present a synchronous Byzantine Agreement algorithm requiring $n \ge t + 4k + 1$, where $n$ is the total number of processes, $t$ is the maximum number of failures, and $k$ is the local error bound per honest process. In the regime where local uncertainty is small ($k \ll t$), our protocol decouples communication from the total fault budget $t$: in an execution where the actual maximum prediction error is $s \le k$ and the actual number of failures is $f \le t$, the protocol terminates in $O(s+1)$ rounds and sends $O((f+k)ks + nk)$ honest messages, achieving $o(n^2)$ communication when $t = Θ(n)$ and $k = o(\sqrt{n})$. Finally, we show that it is not possible to solve Byzantine Agreement in the local $k$-error prediction model with fewer than $Ω(nk)$ honest messages.

items.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
items.summary: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.

items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.summary: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol. ToolSmith consistently improves over the base library across deployed agents of varying scales, with larger backbones reaping greater gains, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Our code and data are available at https://threesr.github.io/toolsmith/.

items.title: VITA-WAM: Manifold-Aligned World-Action Modeling for Real-Time Robot Control
items.summary: World action model (WAM) is a promising paradigm for visuomotor control by jointly modeling world dynamics and actions. Notably, existing WAMs often rely on large generative models and iterative sampling which incur substantial latency for action generation, limiting real-time deployment. In particular, there are two root causes of inefficiency in conventional flow matching or diffusion based action models in WAMs: 1) transporting uninformative Gaussian noise into precise actions necessitating multiple ODE steps, and 2) repeatedly injecting task context through expensive cross-attention modules. Our key insight is that jointly learning and aligning the source and action manifolds streamlines the transport between them, substantially accelerating action generation. Building on this insight, we introduce VITA-WAM, a WAM architecture with manifold-aligned flow-matching (VITA flow matching) that directly transports latent observation representations containing visual, language, and proprioceptive information into latent actions. More specifically, a flow latent alignment (FLA) mechanism is employed to facilitate manifold alignment between latent observation and action representations, enabling accurate generation with few ODE steps. The resulting architecture also eliminates costly attention for observation conditioning during repeated denoising steps. Notably, with a single ODE step, VITA-WAM outperforms 10-step FastWAM by 21.47 pp on LIBERO-Plus and by 1.65 pp on LIBERO, achieving these gains through the FLA objective without distillation, while inferring at 55.67~ms latency, a $2.10\times$ speedup compared to FastWAM.

items.title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations for fMRI generation. We first train a separate EEG encoder to predict each fMRI signal, learning target-specific temporal and spectral features from the same EEG window. After training, we freeze the encoders and project their concatenated hidden features into a shared neurovascular code. Conditioned on this code, stochastic interpolant transforms Gaussian noise into a vector of fMRI signals, allowing different responses to be sampled for the same EEG window. We evaluate our approach on eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets, including four resting-state and four task-based datasets with 61,646 volume-level pairs. Under within-subject and held-out-subject evaluation, our model improves average Pearson correlation over the strongest encoder baselines by 19.1% and 19.8%, respectively. The corresponding improvements over the strongest generator baselines are 18.8% and 47.9%. Beyond reconstruction accuracy, we also evaluate the generated signals using subject-identification classifiers trained on real fMRI. Our method achieves the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated generators. We hope that our work opens up new opportunities for cross-modal brain modeling.

items.title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
items.summary: Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these resources. Local communication can overload one rack's BSMs while others remain idle; reaching those idle resources incurs additional optical loss and retries through switches and quantum frequency converters (QFCs). Programs remain locked into this locality-contention tradeoff as their communication patterns change. We propose Schism, an architecture that lets programs dynamically change which QPUs share each BSM pool. Schism places BSM pools at aggregation switches and QFCs on their core-facing uplinks. Top-of-rack switches establish reconfigurable native-wavelength circuits from QPUs to these pools, forming scale-up domains bounded by the optical loss budget. Reconfiguration reshapes resource sharing across racks without moving QPUs or migrating quantum states. Our key insight is that QPU grouping jointly determines photon-path loss and contention for BSM resources: locality alone cannot identify the best grouping, and a grouping pays off only if its savings outweigh the delay of reconfiguring to it. We develop an optimization framework that combines graph partitioning with resource-constrained completion-time estimates and dynamic programming to select how QPUs share BSM pools and when those groupings reconfigure, between or within circuit phases. Our evaluation using SeQUeNCe with trapped-ion parameters shows that Schism achieves communication speedups of 4.9-7.3x across 11 workloads on 32 QPUs compared to Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6-8.3x compared to SwitchQNet. Schism also outperforms a hypothetical network-wide switch by 1.35-1.38x on the eight workloads whose phases fit in a pool, and trails it by 1.1-1.75x on the other three.

items.title: EditThinker: Enhancing Image Editors via Iterative Reasoning with a Plug-and-Play VLM
items.summary: Image editors can produce realistic images while still failing to satisfy the requested changes. Improving their instruction following requires identifying these failures and translating visual feedback into instructions that the editor can execute. We introduce EditThinker, an 8B vision-language model (VLM) that enhances existing image editors through iterative reasoning while keeping their weights fixed. EditThinker jointly critiques semantic consistency and visual quality, reasons about editing failures, and refines the instruction in a structured response. It interacts with the editor through a Critique-Refine-Repeat loop, providing a plug-and-play interface for feedback-driven editing. Learning effective refinements requires more than imitating plausible expert suggestions: the instructions must work with the capabilities of the underlying editor. We therefore combine supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations with reinforcement learning from executed editing outcomes, using format, critic, and edit rewards. To support this training, we construct ThinkEdit-167k, a dataset of 167k step-wise samples with unified supervision for critique, reasoning, and instruction refinement. Across four tested editors, EditThinker improves overall scores on GEdit-Bench-EN, ImgEdit-Bench, RISE-Bench, and KRIS-Bench. Ablations examine the joint model design, data allocation, and training across VLM backbones. In our GEdit round-budget study, refinement achieves higher scores with fewer editor calls than best-of-N selection. We will release our data construction framework, datasets, and models.

items.title: SAVOR: Score Once, Learn Deeper in On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own samples with token-level scores from a stronger teacher, and it effectively transfers reasoning ability to small language models. Each training step pays for student rollouts and teacher scoring, yet common OPD configurations make a single pass over the scored batch and then discard it. We observe that reusing the batch alone is not enough, because no single fixed teacher target suits every batch. In our runs, a fixed $α$ of 0.3 exceeds a KL envelope at every training step, while 0.2 leaves over a quarter of it unused. We propose SAVOR, which selects for each batch the strongest teacher target inside the KL envelope, freezes the scored batch, and reuses it for a fixed number of student updates without further teacher calls. On five math reasoning benchmarks with a 1.7B student and a 30B-A3B teacher, SAVOR raises macro accuracy over TOP-D from 15.41 to 17.78 with two passes and to 19.36 with three passes at about the same teacher budget. With three passes, SAVOR nearly matches the final accuracy of TOP-D after one third of training while using 67.2% fewer teacher-scored tokens. These results suggest budgeting reuse depth explicitly in OPD.

items.title: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems often return queries that execute successfully but answer the wrong question. Detecting these errors at deployment is hard because execution correctness is defined against a gold query, which exists only in labeled data. We formulate confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation under a latent correctness variable that is observable at calibration time through gold-SQL execution and latent at deployment. Our estimator separates generation from validation. A generator LLM writes and executes the query, and a different critic LLM judges the query and its execution result. The critic's validation and execution-grounded alignment scores are fused with the generator's verbalized confidence, token-level uncertainty, and SQL-structural features in a Random Forest, using two sequential LLM calls. Two calibration steps give finite-sample guarantees. A Learn-then-Test threshold ensures, with probability $1-δ$, that the error rate among accepted queries stays below a user-chosen budget. A conformal p-value bounds the false abstention rate. On Spider we use GPT-OSS-120B as generator and Gemma-4-31B as critic. The estimator obtains an AUARC of 0.899. Without abstention, 22.6% of queries are wrong. With a 15% risk budget ($δ=0.1$), a threshold is certified on all 10 resampled splits, and the system accepts 52.4% of queries on average with 9.1% observed error. Five different critic models give similar results. In a controlled comparison on Spider with Olmo-3-32B as generator, the estimator obtains an AUARC of 89.5, compared with 81.2 for the strongest logit-based baseline. Applied to BIRD without retraining, the confidence scores remain informative (AUROC 0.72, against 0.79 on Spider), but the risk guarantee does not transfer, as expected without exchangeability.

items.title: Roundtable Policy: Confidence-Weighted-Consensus Aggregation Improves Multi-Agent-System Reasoning
items.summary: Multi-agent systems have demonstrated exceptional performance in downstream tasks beyond diverse single agent baselines. A growing body of work has explored ways to improve their reasoning and collaboration, from vote, debate, to complex interaction protocols. However, it still remains opaque why specific choice would be preferred in multi-agent systems. Inspired by the decision-making mechanism of democratic committees and The Society of Mind, we introduce Roundtable Policy, an inference-time reasoning framework for multi-agent systems that performs inference through the weighted consensus of multiple LLMs. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate its that this approach significantly enhances reasoning in complex heterogeneous scientific tasks. Roundtable Policy emphasizes structured and interpretable inference rather than opaque convergence, while requires only black-box access and uniform procedures, making it broadly applicable to diverse multi-agent systems.

items.title: Fully Interpretable Minimal Transformers: From Geometry to Algorithm
items.summary: We present a framework for building and interpreting minimal transformer models. By constraining a transformer's embedding dimension and head size to 2, we enable full two-dimensional visualization of its internal representations.
