Four theorems formalize a structural capacity $κ$, the Rényi-2 analog of Shannon and von Neumann's Rényi-1 entropies, quantifying how a signal's information is organized rather than how much information it contains. AD is related to prior work in invariant estimation, minimax robust estimation, algebraic signal processing, and compressed sensing.

items.title: Characterizing Frozen SSL Encoders and Backends for Cross-Domain Speech Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are the dominant front end for speech deepfake detection, and the prevailing recipe fine-tunes the full encoder on a small spoofing corpus, maximizing in-domain accuracy at the cost of known degradation under domain shift. Taking a recent cross-attention fusion of SSL and constant-Q cepstral features as a fixed reference recipe, we freeze its encoder and ask which encoder and which backend behave best across domains. We cross two frozen encoders, the massively multilingual XEUS and Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53, with two backends, multi-head factorized attentive (MHFA) pooling and AASIST, and evaluate on ASVspoof 2019 LA, ASVspoof 2021 LA and DF, In-the-Wild (ITW), and ASVspoof 5, training every system in one pipeline over three seeds. We report three findings. First, encoder and backend interact: MHFA suits the stronger encoder, while AASIST recovers more from and stabilizes the weaker one. Second, within this recipe, the frozen encoder produces large, repeatable differences. With MHFA, frozen XEUS lowers error relative to frozen XLSR-53 by 58-77% on LA21, DF21, and ASV5, and more modestly on ITW. This ordering persists in a matched-aggregation ablation, and a capacity-matched WavLM Large diagnostic shows that parameter count alone does not explain XLSR-53's weaker performance. Third, against a three-seed fine-tuned baseline, frozen XEUS updates under 0.4M parameters versus 316M, wins on ASVspoof 5 (in EER and min-DCF) and modestly on LA21, trails on DF21 and ITW, and shows lower seed variation on three of the four out-of-domain sets.

items.title: Where does pancreatic lesion segmentation fail on public CT? An attenuation-stratified analysis of a duct-guided pipeline on PanTS
items.summary: Lesion segmentation is a building block of most CT pipelines for pancreatic cancer detection, yet lesion overlap scores stay low. Instead of proposing a new architecture, we report where an end-to-end pipeline fails on a large public dataset. On PanTS we built a three-stage pipeline: pancreas segmentation, maps of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) and common bile duct (CBD), and a lesion model that receives the CT with or without the predicted duct maps. Both lesion models were trained identically on 4007 scans and evaluated once on 737 held-out test scans (127 with a lesion) under a comparison rule fixed before the test run. Lesion Dice was 0.213 with duct maps and 0.209 with CT only (paired difference +0.004, 95% CI -0.011 to +0.019). The duct maps raised the share of lesions touched by a prediction (+0.079, 95% CI +0.024 to +0.134) but also enlarged predictions in lesion-free scans, and lesion-like regions were predicted in all lesion-free test scans. Out of fold, keeping only the predicted components that touched the lesion raised Dice only from 0.285 to 0.309; the loss came mainly from the extent of correctly located predictions. Clearly hypoattenuating lesions, which intensity alone separates from normal pancreas, had the lowest coverage (median 16.6%). From the predicted maps alone, the MPD diameter separated lesion from lesion-free test scans with AUC 0.794 (95% CI 0.747 to 0.839), while the CBD diameter was weak (AUC 0.603) and added nothing. Code for training, inference and evaluation is publicly available.

items.title: Context-Aware Proactive Self-Adaptation: A Two-Layer Model Predictive Control Approach
items.summary: In self-adaptive software systems, the role of context is paramount, especially for proactive self-adaptation. Current research, however, does not fully explore context's impact, for example on priorities of the requirements. To address this gap, we introduce a novel contextual goal model to capture these factors and their influence on the system. Using this, we propose a two-layer control mechanism with a context-aware model predictive control to achieve proactive adaptation for the software system and adaptation for the controller itself. By contextual prediction and a more accurate system model, our approach utilizes model predictive control to facilitate timely and efficient system adaptations, improving both performance and adaptability. Meanwhile, we perform requirement adaptation to update the contextual goal model, which in turn updates the objective function and constraints of the controller. Our experimental evaluations across two scenarios demonstrate the significant benefits of our approach in enhancing system performance.

items.title: Is Classical Error Control Ready for IMT-2030? Information-Loss Interfaces in Channel Estimation, FEC, CRC, and ARQ for Machine-Type Services
items.summary: Fault tolerance and structured error control in mobile communication networks--historically implemented as a modular cascade of pilot-aided channel estimation (CE), forward error correction (FEC), cyclic redundancy check (CRC), and hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)--remain foundational to 5G New Radio (NR). Although finite-blocklength coding, joint estimation-decoding, and grant-free access have been active academic topics for over a decade, commercial 3GPP specifications up to Release 18 still enforce rigid cross-layer boundaries between these blocks. In short-packet machine-type communications (MTC) for IMT-2030 (6G), inserting separate redundancy for channel training, error correction, and error detection shrinks the net payload entropy resolved per channel slot, while standardized UE processing timelines and HARQ round-trip delays collide with sub-millisecond reliability targets. Combining a multi-user MIMO short-packet simulation with real 3GPP TS 38.214 numerology latency budgets, this article diagnoses the structural bottlenecks of the legacy reliability pipeline and outlines an interoperable roadmap for 3GPP Release 20+--spanning soft-output universal decoding, sensing-assisted priors, grant-free joint detection, and task-oriented error control.

items.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
items.summary: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.

items.title: Extreme Value Theory for Peak Power in Discrete-Time Complex Gaussian Processes
items.summary: The peak power for a band-limited, radio frequency (RF) signal, often expressed using the dimensionless peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), is an important quantity for signal analysis and the design of RF transmitters and receivers. Modern digital instrumentation, like vector signal analyzers, collect and process discrete-time samples of the complex baseband signal. Also, computer-based simulations of continuous-time processes must be carried out with discrete-time sequences. Therefore, to design such measurements and simulations, accurate models for the distribution of the PAPR for discrete-time complex baseband processes are required. In particular, band-pass thermal noise and modern communication signals, like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), are often modeled as complex Gaussian processes. To address this problem, we present a new analytical model for the PAPR distribution of a stationary, discrete-time, complex Gaussian process. We demonstrate that the new discrete-time model subsumes prior models based on asymptotic extreme value theory as special cases while providing a larger domain of efficacy. Specifically, using Monte Carlo simulations of filtered complex white Gaussian noise, we show that the new model is more effective for practical sample sizes and dual-band spectra than previous approaches.

items.title: Supply Chain Networks: Equilibrium, Sensitivity, Dynamics and Shortage Games
items.summary: We model production in a supply chain network in which every node sets a Newsvendor order target, upstream demand is the sum of downstream orders routed through a substochastic matrix, and every node has a capacity. The clearing vector of production quantities is the unique Nash equilibrium of the ordering game and the unique optimal solution of a linear program, and it has the form of the Eisenberg--Noe interbank clearing model. Nodes that produce their order target are hedged; the others are unhedged. We give comparative statics and a closed form for the stationary covariance of node demands. Inventory drawdown after a capacity shock is a Skorokhod reflection problem with a closed-form solution: the network and the unhedged nodes determine who is eventually rationed and by how much, and inventories determine when. When rationed nodes can inflate their orders, the equilibria never lower aggregate deliveries and can make suppliers with no physical shortage unhedged. With endogenous prices, a per-epoch price equilibrium exists and, under mild conditions, is unique when supply is price-elastic. We illustrate the model on global crude-oil trade.

items.title: Transferring the driveshaft inertia to the grid via the DC-link in MV drive systems
items.summary: This paper investigates a control approach that renders the driveshaft inertia completely available on the grid side and enhances the fault ride-through behavior of medium-voltage (MV) drive systems. Two main contributions are presented. First, we show how the rotational inertia of the driveline shaft can be synchronously coupled to the grid through a modification of the speed control reference signal and through an adapted DC-link control strategy. For the latter, we pursue two alternatives: one based on conventional cascaded control and another based on synchronous machine (SM) model matching. Second, we demonstrate that both the standard phase-locked loop (PLL) and the matching control approach can be interpreted, via the ray-circle complementarity, as feedback optimization schemes with distinct steady-state maps. This perspective allows us to revisit matching control, reveal its embedded PLL, highlight its current-limiting and tracking capabilities, and provide an extensive simulation study.

items.title: Blind Channel and Noise-Variance Estimation for MIMO Thermal Noise Modulation Systems via Generalized Expectation-Maximization
items.summary: Thermal Noise Modulation (TNM) is a communication paradigm in which information is conveyed through different thermal-noise variance levels rather than deterministic signal waveforms. Its stochastic nature makes conventional pilot-based channel estimation challenging, while pilot transmission introduces additional overhead and reduces spectral efficiency. This paper proposes a pilot-free blind receiver for M-ary TNM systems based on the Generalized Expectation-Maximization (GEM) framework. The proposed receiver jointly estimates the channel matrix, latent transmitted symbols, mixture probabilities, and unknown transmit-noise variance levels directly from received observations, without requiring pilot symbols or prior knowledge of the variance constellation. The modulation order M and receiver-noise variance are assumed to be known. Since the maximization step has no closed-form solution, a gradient-ascent procedure is incorporated into the GEM framework to iteratively update the unknown parameters. The proposed approach enables simultaneous channel estimation, symbol detection, and variance learning within a unified blind-receiver framework. Simulation results demonstrate accurate channel Gram matrix estimation and effective symbol detection without pilot overhead. Moreover, the proposed variance learning scheme achieves performance close to that obtained with perfectly known transmit variance levels, with only moderate BER degradation, demonstrating its potential for practical MIMO TNM systems.

items.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape
items.summary: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study between Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) applied to a spatial Cable-Suspended Parallel Robot (CSPR) actuated by four cables. The robot is modeled in two parallel ways: (i) via an analytical dynamic model with included cable elasticity and frictional losses, and (ii) in MATLAB Simscape Multibody, capturing realistic physical effects. Both controllers are implemented under identical reference trajectories, system constraints, and tuning strategies. Our results show that NMPC achieves superior tracking accuracy and stronger disturbance rejection compared to SMC, but at the cost of higher computational demand. Moreover, both controllers were tested on an analytical model of the robot and a Simscape model. The close agreement between the two, for both control schemes, confirms the accuracy of the analytical formulation and its consistency with the physics-based simulation. The study highlights the value of physics-based simulation as a complementary tool for validating advanced controllers under realistic conditions, and demonstrates that NMPC offers superior performance for the studied high-precision, constrained CSPR.

items.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
items.summary: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.

items.title: Cache-Aided Asymmetric MIMO Communications: Achievable DoF Analysis
items.summary: Integrating coded caching (CC) into multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications significantly enhances the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF). This paper investigates a practical cache-aided asymmetric MIMO configuration with cache ratio $γ$, where a server with $L$ transmit antennas communicates with $K$ users. The users are partitioned into $J$ groups, and each user in group $j$ has $G_j$ receive antennas. We propose four content-aware MIMO-CC strategies: \emph{min-$G$} enforces symmetry using the smallest antenna count among users; \emph{Grouping} maximizes intra-subset spatial multiplexing gain at the expense of some global caching gain; \emph{Super-grouping} aggregates users into optimized \emph{min-$G$}-based super-sets with identical effective receive multiplexing gains before applying \emph{Grouping} across them; and \emph{Phantom} redistributes spatial resources assuming "phantom" antennas at the users to bridge the performance gains of \emph{min-$G$} and \emph{Grouping}. We develop these asymmetric strategies under three reference symmetric CC placement-delivery policies with guaranteed linear decodability: a finite-search DoF-optimized policy attaining the best single-shot achievable DoF lower bound, and two closed-form policies, namely combinatorial and linear cyclic low-complexity constructions, with the cyclic policy attaining DoF performance close to the others in many operating regimes. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate significant DoF improvements across various system configurations, and that policy-strategy combinations offer flexible trade-offs between DoF and subpacketization complexity.

items.title: MedTimeQ: Query-guided fusion of time-series foundation models and LLMs for multi-lead ECG classification
items.summary: Accurate classification of medical time series, such as electrocardiograms (ECGs), requires capturing waveform morphology, long-range temporal structure, inter-lead dependencies, and clinical semantics. Existing large language model (LLM)-based approaches often map signal patches directly into the language embedding space, potentially underusing pretrained time-series knowledge and transferring redundant or irrelevant information. We propose MedTimeQ, a parameter-efficient framework that integrates a lead-aware temporal foundation encoder with an LLM-reprogrammed ECG pathway through gated residual fusion. A Query Former uses learned diagnostic queries to select and compress fused representations into informative soft tokens for a frozen LLM. Semantic prototype learning further guides classification through multiple clinical descriptions per category, statistics-based prompt selection, and knowledge distillation. Both foundation backbones remain frozen, limiting training to lightweight interface and classification components. We evaluate MedTimeQ on PTB-XL, Chapman-Shaoxing, and MIT-BIH for recording-level diagnosis, rhythm classification, and heartbeat classification, respectively. MedTimeQ achieves the best performance in 11 of 12 dataset-metric comparisons, with consistent class-balanced gains across all three tasks. On PTB-XL, it achieves 76.93% accuracy and 58.14% macro-F1, exceeding MedTsLLM by 10.08 and 7.07 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the benefits of selectively integrating pretrained temporal representations with clinical language semantics. Code: https://github.com/kkianamm/MedTimeQ

items.title: SpA2V: Harnessing Spatial Auditory Cues for Audio-driven Spatially-aware Video Generation
items.summary: Audio-driven video generation aims to synthesize realistic videos that align with input audio recordings, akin to the human ability to visualize scenes from auditory input. However, existing approaches predominantly focus on exploring semantic information, such as the classes of sounding sources present in the audio, limiting their ability to generate videos with accurate content and spatial composition. In contrast, we humans can not only naturally identify the semantic categories of sounding sources but also determine their deeply encoded spatial attributes, including locations and movement directions. This useful information can be elucidated by considering specific spatial indicators derived from the inherent physical properties of sound, such as loudness or frequency. As prior methods largely ignore this factor, we present SpA2V, the first framework explicitly exploits these spatial auditory cues from audios to generate videos with high semantic and spatial correspondence. SpA2V decomposes the generation process into two stages: 1) Audio-guided Video Planning: We meticulously adapt a state-of-the-art MLLM for a novel task of harnessing spatial and semantic cues from input audio to construct Video Scene Layouts (VSLs). This serves as an intermediate representation to bridge the gap between the audio and video modalities. 2) Layout-grounded Video Generation: We develop an efficient and effective approach to seamlessly integrate VSLs as conditional guidance into pre-trained diffusion models, enabling VSL-grounded video generation in a training-free manner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpA2V excels in generating realistic videos with semantic and spatial alignment to the input audios.

items.title: Scaled Relative Graph Separation for Unbounded Nonlinear Systems
items.summary: We investigate stability analysis of one-channel nonlinear feedback systems based on the recent notion of scaled relative graph (SRG). Our focus is on the SRG separation in the complex plane for feedback stability analysis that involves possibly unbounded open-loop nonlinear systems. Subject to a technical assumption, a homotopy-based SRG separation theorem is developed as the main result, where the incremental directed gap is utilized as a key instrument to quantify robust feedback stability along the homotopy path. Doing so enables us to incorporate commonly used integrators as unbounded systems in the SRG-based framework. Specializations of the main result to linear systems, along with illustrative examples, are also provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.

items.title: DIBEM: Diffusion-Based Error Mitigation for Uncertainty-Aware UWB Localization
items.summary: Ultra-wideband (UWB) localization degrades substantially under Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) propagation, where multipath and obstruction induce complex ranging error distributions that are poorly represented by fixed parametric models. We propose Diffusion-based Error Mitigation (DIBEM), an uncertainty-aware framework that learns the conditional ranging error distribution directly from six compact Channel Impulse Response (CIR) statistics. Rather than predicting a deterministic correction or restricting uncertainty to a Gaussian or fixed mixture family, DIBEM uses a conditional diffusion model with denoising diffusion implicit model sampling to generate link-specific error samples. The resulting empirical distributions are incorporated into maximum likelihood position estimation. This allows localization to account for heterogeneous ranging uncertainty across anchor-tag links. Experiments across four indoor environments show that DIBEM achieves the lowest negative log-likelihood for NLoS ranging errors and the lowest or tied-lowest mean localization error across all environments. Compared with least squares approaches, DIBEM reduces mean localization error by up to 64.8 percent, while improving over Gaussian and mixture density probabilistic models by up to 15.8 percent and 14.0 percent, respectively. Results demonstrate the potential of diffusion-based conditional error modeling for uncertainty-aware UWB localization, particularly under challenging NLoS propagation.

items.title: Anomalous Sound Detection Using Separation Features and Paired-Mixture Representation Learning
items.summary: Acoustic monitoring often relies on normal machine recordings with limited information about operating conditions. We first train a separator to estimate a normal target recording from a mixture of machine sounds. With the separator frozen, we train regional attention on pairs of mixtures that share the target recording and contain different interfering sounds. Differences between the paired embeddings provide the covariance estimate for correction before cosine nearest-neighbor scoring. We evaluate the method on the development-test recordings of seven machine types in the 2022 Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events challenge. We summarize detection performance by the harmonic mean of source-domain, target-domain, and partial areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve. On the original recordings, a separator trained without external pre-training achieved a three-run mean of 64.56%, close to the 64.87% obtained by distillation from a pre-trained audio transformer. Using the same transformer as a frozen encoder gave a mean of 64.88%. With competing machine sounds added to the test recordings, both implementations outperformed distillation at all seven tested interference levels.

items.title: Native-Space 3D CarveMix for Multi-Site T1w Stroke Segmentation
items.summary: Segmenting ischemic stroke lesions on T1-weighted (T1w) MRI acquired across different scanners and protocols without intensity standardization is difficult because lesions are subtle and share intensity characteristics with cerebrospinal fluid. Standard deep learning architectures trained across multiple centers plateau around Dice 0.66, with acute lesions ($\le 7$ days post-stroke) performing substantially worse due to severe sample scarcity. We combine a MedNeXt-L ($k=5$) backbone with on-the-fly 3D CarveMix augmentation that pastes real lesion patches into recipient training patches. By generating synthetic lesion placements dynamically within each fold with subject-level split isolation, the model sees more diverse lesion patterns without requiring pre-generated copies on disk. We evaluate on 1,453 native T1w scans from 55 clinical centers in the ISLES 2026 challenge. MedNeXt-L with CarveMix achieved a mean five-fold cross-validation Dice of 0.648 after 500 epochs. For comparison, the estimated Dice for plain MedNeXt-L at epoch 500 was 0.630, obtained by interpolation from its 1,000-epoch training trajectory.

items.title: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
items.summary: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Finite-size security analyses of high-dimensional protocols fix the dimension in advance, and the dimension-adaptive schemes reported so far have been analyzed only asymptotically. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. Each block is therefore a standard fixed-length protocol, and composable finite-key security against coherent attacks follows from sequential composition; an inaccurate channel model reduces the key rate but does not weaken security. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel--Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31\%--47\% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8\% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario, while every fixed dimension drops to 73.5\% or less in at least one scenario. Running the link's measurement statistics on a superconducting quantum processor shows device errors close to a constant offset; with these errors included, the best daytime dimension changes from eight to four, and the controller adjusts accordingly.

items.title: S$2$SCORE: A Textless Unified Evaluation Metric for Speech-to-Speech Translation Systems
items.summary: Evaluating speech-to-speech translation (S$2$ST) systems requires assessing multiple dimensions of translated speech, including semantic adequacy, speaker similarity, and acoustic naturalness. Existing approaches are largely text-based, relying on ASR transcripts and primarily assessing semantic adequacy, while other dimensions require separate metrics. We propose S$2$SCORE, a unified text-free evaluation framework that jointly models these dimensions within a multi-task architecture and produces a human-calibrated overall quality score. S$2$SCORE is trained using supervision derived from established evaluation models, enabling scalable learning without direct human annotations. Evaluated across five language pairs, S$2$SCORE shows strong agreement with human judgments, independent reference metrics, and the training supervision metrics, indicating robust generalization. The reference-free variant, S$2$SCORE-QE, consistently outperforms S$2$SCORE-REF and achieves stronger semantic adequacy prediction than BLASER~$2.0$.

items.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows
items.summary: An inspection robot may owe several measurements at the same station, each with a different window in which a dwell can begin. We ask what a feedback controller must retain about earlier visits to guarantee all remaining deadlines under bounded disturbances. For a common spatial predicate and dwell length, removing redundant windows orders the remaining obligations by both endpoints. On every history without an expired obligation, the served windows form a suffix. One boundary and one capped run length therefore preserve the future satisfaction of the original task. On a verified library of branching motion primitives we use this state to recover a feedback policy. For one task type a scalar threshold per run length suffices, with work linear in the number of listed branches per time layer for fixed dwell. Multiple types require a joint recursion. On a quadrotor inspection library the threshold sweep reduced the cost of constructing a reusable full-domain policy, while a sparse Boolean baseline answered a single initial query faster. In a two-station MuJoCo patrol, three task-aware filters all met every window in twelve paired runs each. Of eight initially certified runs, the completion filter retained the certificate in all eight, compared with three for safety-only filtering.

items.title: Optimal Allocation of Grid-Forming Frequency Shaping Control
items.summary: Various inverter-based control strategies have been proposed to improve frequency security for power systems with high renewable penetration. Among them, the grid-forming frequency shaping control is particularly promising due to its ability to shape the post-contingency aggregate system frequency dynamics into first-order with prescribed rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and steady-state frequency deviation. Moreover, the shaped aggregate dynamics depends on the harmonic sum of all inverter transfer functions rather than on their distribution. In light of this, here we explore how to allocate shaping control resources to minimize the transient control effort needed to achieve ideal coherent dynamics. We formulate it as a constrained optimization problem by tackling two main difficulties. First, we make the squared $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm legitimate quantification of transient control cost under step power imbalances through a system transformation. Second, we simplify the $s$-domain constraint for Nadir elimination into a standard constraint that is easy to implement in optimization. The resulting non-convex optimization problem can be solved by existing successive convexification method. The effectiveness of the allocation has been verified on the modified Icelandic Power Network test case.

items.title: Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD) with Divide and Conquer Strategy for DRL-Based BS Localization
items.summary: Optimal base station (BS) placement is a fundamental challenge in wireless localization. Conventional optimization approaches may become computationally demanding as the geometric complexity of the environment increases, limiting their scalability to realistic building layouts. This paper proposes an Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD)-based divide-and-conquer framework integrated with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for optimizing BS placement. The proposed approach exploits the geometric structure of building layouts by partitioning the original environment into smaller sub-regions using cuts associated with reflex vertices. Furthermore, the proposed solution is bench-marked against DRL without ACD and with the optimal solution obtained by exhaustive search. Results show the superiority of the proposed approach and that it approaches the optimal solution.

items.title: RF-Florence: Unified RF Detection and Physical Grounding with a Foundation Model
items.summary: Reliable signal detection is essential for spectrum sharing and intelligent sensing in sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. Wideband radio-frequency (RF) monitoring must locate emissions and identify those satisfying waveform-family and physical constraints. The latter task, physical grounding, requires query meaning to agree with measurable signal attributes. RF-Florence unifies three tasks---full-scene detection, physical grounding, and supplied-region recognition---through a shared pretrained foundation model. Calibrated spectrograms connect localization coordinates to time and frequency, while common event targets and explicit predicates align task outputs with requests. On synthetic mixtures with family--attribute combinations withheld from training, structured queries improve mean grounding F1 by 7.66 percentage points over natural language. Under the tested two-path channel, direct grounding with structured queries exceeds a You Only Look Once (YOLO) detector followed by rule-based filtering by 3.44 points in mean F1. These results show the value of aligning query expressions with the signal families and physical variables that define the requested event set.

items.title: Voice Agents: From Auditory Intelligence to Auditory Agency
items.summary: Voice systems increasingly combine streaming speech, persistent state, reasoning, tool use, and embodied control. Once these functions share a runtime, spoken input can change digital or physical state, and recognition or response quality alone no longer characterizes the system. This article studies the interfaces through which spoken evidence becomes consequential. \emph{Auditory intelligence} denotes the capabilities required to perceive, understand, coordinate, and generate spoken interaction; \emph{auditory agency} denotes the causal path from that interaction to stateful decisions and observable consequences. The \emph{commitment boundary} marks where revisable auditory evidence becomes persistent state, a plan, or an executable request. \emph{Agency closure} then follows an authorized action through observation, verification, recovery or compensation, and communication of the outcome. Evidence from full-duplex interaction, reasoning, memory, tools, embodiment, and human control shows a consistent systems-level mismatch: integration is advancing faster than end-to-end observation of what the integrated system actually does. The resulting design problem is to preserve a trace from spoken evidence to consequence while keeping commitment, execution, and verification attributable.

items.title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
items.summary: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(ω)\propto[1+2α(ω-ω_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|ω-ω_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $α\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $α$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $α$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $α$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.

items.title: From Tokens to Energy Flexibility: Quantization-Enabled Demand Response for Data Centers with LLM Inference Workloads
items.summary: The rapid growth of large language model (LLM) inference is creating significant data-center loads that face increasing energy-management challenges under tightening grid conditions and demand response (DR) requirements. Conventional data-center energy management mainly relies on temporal and spatial workload shifting and campus-level energy asset scheduling, but it usually treats LLM inference demand as an aggregate load. As a result, these approaches fail to exploit the internal characteristics of LLM serving and therefore overlook the flexibility offered by LLM-specific techniques such as model quantization. To unlock this flexibility, this paper proposes a quantization-enabled energy management framework for grid-responsive LLM inference data centers. First, a quantization-to-power model is established to map each model--quantization configuration to a compact set of dispatchable parameters. Second, a two-stage quantization-enabled DR model is developed to account for model instance switching, request routing, and precision selection. Third, a multi-campus co-optimization method is introduced for DR participation by integrating grid-side electricity and carbon signals with the quantization-enabled DR model. Case studies show that the proposed framework reduces total data-center operating cost by 31.8% without curtailing served token volume, validating model quantization as an effective flexibility lever for grid-responsive LLM data-center energy management.

items.title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk. Asynchronous early inference can hide latency, but its results may be inconsistent with the arriving actual inputs. Unconditional reuse risks acting on mismatched inputs, whereas full recomputation discards useful precomputation. We propose SR-VLA, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair. During current chunk execution, a lightweight action-conditioned predictor generates next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state. These predictions, together with the task instruction, drive the frozen VLA to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk. After real inputs are available to VLA, predicted--real differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the action chunk or trigger selective KV repair. On LIBERO, SR-VLA achieves $2.67\times$ and $1.27\times$ query speedups over the respective synchronous $π_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA-OFT baselines, while maintaining competitive average task success rates. Under target-motion perturbation, success remains baseline-comparable, with $1.52\times$--$1.93\times$ query speedup.

items.title: Self-Aligned Resonant Beams for Adaptive Beamforming in 6G IoT
items.summary: The integration of communication, sensing, and wireless power transfer (WPT) is becoming an important direction for 6G Internet of Things (IoT). However, conventional beamforming typically depends on channel state information (CSI) acquisition, beam training, and active beam scanning, which can introduce substantial overhead in dynamic or passive-device scenarios. This article reviews the radio-frequency resonant beam system (RF-RBS) as a physical-layer self-alignment mechanism for reducing this dependence. By using retro-directive antenna arrays (RAAs) at the transceivers, RF-RBS can form a cyclic electromagnetic feedback loop in which phase-conjugated waves reinforce a dominant round-trip path. This mechanism enables self-aligned, high-gain beam formation under suitable loop-gain, propagation, and hardware conditions. We discuss the RF-RBS architecture, its operating principles, and its potential roles in WPT, self-aligned communication, and passive positioning. We also examine implementation challenges, including analog hardware integration, multi-user interference, limited coverage, and line-of-sight (LoS) dependence, and outline its potential value for latency-sensitive 6G IoT scenarios such as unmanned systems and industrial automation.

items.title: On linear MMSE receivers in the presence of data-like multiuser interference
items.summary: Linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receivers have been of great interest for many decades for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in radiocommunications networks in particular. Despite the extensive literature on this subject, this topic remains relevant to several current and emerging applications. In this context, the paper presents a continuous-time approach showing that most of LMME receivers of the literature are suboptimal. In particular, they are typically implemented at the symbol rate following matched filtering to the pulse-shaping filter and require a prior knowledge of the MUI channels, which can be difficult and costly to acquire in practice. The main contribution of this paper is to address the key challenge of designing new LMMSE receivers that achieve the performance of the optimal receiver without requiring prior knowledge of the MUI channels. To this end, two novel receiver LMMSE structures are proposed and analyzed for linearly modulated signals impaired by data-like MUI: a two-input receiver and a three-input receiver. The proposed receivers are shown to be quasi-optimal over a broad range of scenarios. These results provide new perspectives for practical implementation of the optimal LMMSE receiver in the presence of data-like MUI, relying only on knowledge of the signal-of-interest (SOI) channel.

items.title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
items.summary: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.

items.title: Specification-Aware Sparse Differentiation: Planning under Signal Temporal Logic with Sparsemax Robustness
items.summary: Gradient-based optimal control under a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification involves solving a nonlinear program whose constraints are smoothed robustness functions of the trajectory, and automatic differentiation without knowledge of sparsity computes the Jacobian and the Hessian that its solver needs in full. This often renders the problem computationally intractable. The dynamics and the specification prescribe a sparsity pattern through the STL syntax, the windows of the temporal operators and the variables that the predicates read. Standard tools such as CasADi recover this pattern by structural detection. In this work, we propose a method to prescribe such a pattern directly from the task specification. We show that our method allows us to exploit SparseMax, a recently proposed smooth robustness operator that is certifiably sparse and sound. Its derivative is exactly zero at every operand at or below a data-dependent threshold, which structural detection cannot see. We derive the patterns that expose this trajectory-dependent sparsity to sparse automatic differentiation, with a margin test for their reuse and Hessians confined to the variables of each constraint's support. We demonstrate the method on a dual-arm coordination task in which two arms share a hand-off zone divided into cells and one until constraint per scheduled visit keeps the other arm out of a cell until the visitor has left it. The two scenes are a zone of five cells and a circle of 64 cells, with single solves and closed-loop re-planning on a rigid-body simulation. Our exact-Hessian interior-point solves are up to 27 times faster than those with the sound log-sum-exp robustness in CasADi and IPOPT.

items.title: Self-Distilled Pronunciation and Accent Control for Neural Text-to-Speech
items.summary: Text-to-speech that reads raw text has no lexicon: a rare word is read as guessed, and a native Japanese listener accepts a word only if its reading and pitch accent are both right. A known remedy installs a reading-and-accent channel into a released model, but it needs many recordings. This paper removes the recordings: the frozen backbone reads a sentence containing a common word it already says correctly, and that output serves as the teacher for the same sentence with the word replaced by an annotated reading with its pitch accent. Screened raters judged the tag right on 0.80 to 0.93 of unseen difficult words on four backbones spanning autoregressive, diffusion, and encoder-decoder synthesis; plain kana, which cannot express an accent, got 0.38 to 0.60. On words needing no edit, naturalness is non-inferior on one backbone; on the other three, listeners prefer the unedited rendition by 0.19 to 0.26.

items.title: SWIFT: A Handcrafted, Arithmetic-Minimal FPGA Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Generative voice cloning threatens voice-based authentication, yet current deepfake detectors rely on power-hungry, high-precision models unsuited to edge hardware. We present SWIFT (Streaming Whiten-Integer Forensic Trust-Engine), a handcrafted detector that works in the high-frequency noise domain where synthesis artifacts concentrate. A first-order integer high-pass residual drives nine families of fixed-point descriptors, among them integer lifting-wavelet cepstral quantiles, Mahalanobis anomaly distances, Poincaré phase-space geometry, and phase jitter, fused by calibrated gradient-boosted trees and a sparse L1-regularised meta-learner. Under leakage-controlled nested cross-validation, with one shared preprocessing chain for real and fake audio, this reference model reaches accuracy of up to 99.86% and an Equal Error Rate (EER) as low as 0.03% across eight benchmarks. Its integer front-end and a fixed-point linear classifier run on the programmable logic of a PYNQ-Z2 (Zynq-7020) board, with a 7.85 microseconds per-frame datapath latency (127.4k frames/s) at 1.734 W and 11.2% LUT utilisation. Integer-only audio deepfake feature extraction is thus feasible at the edge without pretrained neural models or floating-point units.

items.title: WAFT: A Fourier-Analytic Framework for Steady-State Performance of Walker Constellations
items.summary: The Walker configuration is predominantly adopted by nongeostationary orbit constellations exemplified by Starlink and Kuiper. The steady-state distribution of aggregate downlink interference power is critical for spectrum coexistence regulation. Large-scale time-stepped simulation and stochastic geometry (SG)-based models are the mainstream methods for obtaining the distribution, but are either computationally expensive or subject to inherent bias. This paper models the aggregate downlink interference power as an additive observable and proposes the Walker-constellation Analysis via Fourier Transform (WAFT) framework to derive the steady-state performance. Modeling the constellation as a periodic impulse array on the phase torus, the spectral representation of the observable is derived via 2-D Fourier analysis. Analytical expressions for the expectation, variance, and steady-state complementary cumulative distribution function are further derived, and the periodicity of receiver performance along longitude is characterized. For a Starlink sub-constellation example, numerical validation shows that the percentile discrepancies of WAFT relative to a finite-duration time-stepped simulation remain within 0.09~dB. Comparisons with isotropic and intensity-matched SG models reveal that the conditional independence of satellite positions alone makes the models assign a substantial probability mass to physically infeasible values, producing percentile discrepancies.

items.title: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
items.summary: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.

items.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
items.summary: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

items.title: Advanced 400G-SerDes Modulations and Equalizers for GPU Cluster in AI Era
items.summary: High-speed GPU cluster interconnects are evolving from 200 to 400 Gbps to meet the growing computing demands of artificial intelligence. We investigate high-order modulation and advanced equalization for 400 Gbps interconnects. Theoretical bit error rate (BER) expressions for 4/8-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) and approximate expressions for six PAM6 formats generated from 32-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (32QAM) are derived. In additive white Gaussian noise, PAM6 generated by framed-cross 32QAM achieves the best BER performance among the PAM6 formats. PAM6 and PAM8 incur peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) penalties of approximately 4.2 and 7.2 dB, respectively, relative to PAM4 at the KP4 forward error correction (KP4-FEC) limit. Simulations compare PAM4, PAM6, and PAM8 at a line rate of 440 Gbps (net rate of 400G) under different bandwidth limitations. As bandwidth becomes more constrained, bandwidth requirements increasingly dominate performance over noise tolerance. PAM4 requires the lowest PSNR to reach the KP4-FEC limit in mildly bandwidth-limited channels, whereas PAM6 performs best under moderate limitations. PAM8 offers a significant advantage under severe limitations because of its lower bandwidth requirement and reduced susceptibility to high-frequency attenuation. With maximum likelihood sequence estimation, PAM6 and PAM8 reach the KP4-FEC limit under all evaluated channel conditions, while PAM6 requires a lower PSNR in most channels, highlighting its potential for 400G-SerDes systems.

items.title: SatMend: LLM Agents for Automated Software Repair in Satellite Constellations with Intermittent Ground Contact
items.summary: Satellite constellations rely on onboard software to sustain services across cooperating spacecraft. Maintaining this software requires handling related component versions and different failure causes while delivering repairs through intermittent ground contact. Automated software repair in satellite constellations remains underexplored, particularly the coordination of repairs across related versions with verified onboard recovery under intermittent ground contact. To address this gap, we propose SatMend, a software repair method driven by ground-based large language model (LLM) agents. SatMend organizes related versions into persistent sessions to retain diagnostic context and combines source and runtime evidence to select code repair or state recovery actions. It validates each version separately and submits ready candidates during continued repair, allowing ground preparation to overlap with onboard delivery and verification. Experimental results show that across configurations with 16 to 64 satellites, SatMend restores 192 of 224 faulty applications within 600 s, compared with 40 for SWE-agent, 77 for Agentless, 124 for RepairAgent, and 115 for SWE-Search. These results demonstrate SatMend's effectiveness in restoring applications and supporting service continuity in satellite constellations with intermittent ground contact.

items.title: Sparse Neural Approximations for Bilevel Adversarial Problems in Power Grids
items.summary: The adversarial worst-case load shedding (AWLS) problem is pivotal for identifying critical contingencies under line outages. It is naturally cast as a bilevel program: the upper level simulates an attacker determining worst-case line failures, and the lower level corresponds to the defender's generator redispatch operations. Conventional techniques using optimality conditions render the bilevel, mixed-integer formulation computationally prohibitive due to the combinatorial number of topologies and the nonconvexity of AC power flow constraints. To address these challenges, we develop a novel single-level optimal value-function (OVF) reformulation and further leverage a data-driven neural network (NN) surrogate of the follower's optimal value. To ensure physical realizability, we embed the trained surrogate in a physics-constrained NN (PCNN) formulation that couples the OVF inequality with (relaxed) AC feasibility, yielding a mixed-integer convex model amenable to off-the-shelf solvers. To achieve scalability, we learn a sparse, area-partitioned NN via spectral clustering; the resulting block-sparse architecture scales essentially linearly with system size while preserving accuracy. Notably, our approach produces near-optimal worst-case failures and generalizes across loading conditions and unseen topologies, enabling rapid online recomputation. Numerical experiments on the IEEE 14- and 118-bus systems demonstrate the method's scalability and solution quality for large-scale contingency analysis, with an average optimality gap of 5.8% compared to conventional methods, while maintaining computation times under one minute.

items.title: Extracting Exact Lie Derivatives Without Backpropagation: A Dual Compiler for Neural Control Barrier Functions
items.summary: A safety filter based on a neural control barrier function (CBF) evaluates, at each control cycle, the trained network and its Lie derivatives along the system vector fields. This paper presents a compiler whose emitted C++ code performs this evaluation on embedded processors by forward-mode differentiation with dual numbers. The derivatives are exact in the sense of automatic differentiation, which means that they are free of truncation error and subject to floating-point roundoff. One evaluation of the network in this arithmetic, called a dual pass, returns the barrier value and its Lie derivative along one vector field, and an extension to hyper-dual numbers returns the second-order Lie derivatives of CBFs of relative degree two. Apart from scalar variables, the memory that a dual pass writes is at most four floating-point numbers per neuron of the widest layer and does not depend on the network depth. On an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, we compare the emitted code with code for reverse-mode differentiation (i.e., backpropagation), which is also generated before the program runs and uses fixed-size arrays. In three experiments, the reverse-mode code has a lower execution time than the dual and hyper-dual passes executed one after the other. For single-input networks, the measurements do not establish such an ordering between the reverse-mode code and a variant of the dual pass that propagates the real part once. For networks of increasing depth, the working memory of the dual passes is constant, whereas that of the reverse-mode code increases. While the emitted code runs, no dynamic allocation is recorded. We report the maximum observed execution time of the complete filter step, which includes the dynamics and a breakpoint search for the quadratic program with input bounds and one affine constraint. The compiler and the experiments are open source.

items.title: Rateless Lattice Codes over Fading Wiretap Channels: Finite-Length Secrecy and the Secret-Key Capacity of Degraded Sessions
items.summary: In rateless transmission the transmitter keeps sending until the legitimate receiver (Bob) can decode. Over a wiretap channel this has a useful side effect: the eavesdropper (Eve) sees only as many symbols as Bob needs, although the transmitter knows neither channel. We study the secrecy of rateless lattice codes in this setting. First, using a public dither and privacy amplification, we prove a finite-length secrecy bound, in total variation distance, for every channel realization, even if Eve knows all codes and seeds and combines all packets. Second, stopping when Bob acknowledges successful decoding, as in hybrid ARQ, costs at most the logarithm of the number of possible feedback outcomes in secret bits. Third, for degraded sessions with state-based stopping and without a pre-shared key or other public discussion, the secret-key rate of a session cannot exceed its accumulated Gaussian secrecy capacity, and adaptive key generation with shaped rateless lattice codes comes within any $ε>0$ of this limit when Eve's channel states are revealed after the session. If only their statistics are known, choosing the key length after the session guarantees a prescribed secrecy-outage probability. Finally, over block Rayleigh fading with a CRC-based acknowledgement and joint belief-propagation decoding, and with Eve $20$~dB weaker on average, the scheme reaches $59$--$69\%$ of the outage-weighted throughput of an ideal infinite-length secure hybrid-ARQ benchmark for Bob SNRs of $8$--$20$~dB.

items.title: FGAS: Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation
items.summary: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) has made high-fidelity generated audio widely available across the Internet, driving the advancement of audio steganography. Benefiting from advances in deep learning, current audio steganography schemes are mainly based on encoder-decoder network architectures. While these methods achieve promising perceptual quality, they typically require network pre-training, and maintaining anti-steganalysis performance at high payloads remains challenging. To address these issues, we propose Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation (FGAS). Adversarial perturbations carrying a secret message are embedded into the cover audio to generate stego audio. The sender and receiver independently construct the same fixed decoder from a shared architecture and initialization key, avoiding the transfer of trained decoder parameters. In FGAS, we propose an Audio Adversarial Perturbation Generation (A2PG) strategy with an optional robust extension and design a lightweight fixed decoder. The fixed decoder guarantees reliable extraction of the hidden message, while adversarial perturbations are optimized to keep the stego audio perceptually and statistically close to the cover audio, thereby improving anti-steganalysis performance. The experimental results show that FGAS significantly improves stego audio quality, achieving an average PSNR gain of over 10 dB compared to SOTA methods. Furthermore, FGAS demonstrates strong robustness against common audio processing attacks. Moreover, FGAS exhibits superior anti-steganalysis performance across different relative payloads; under high-capacity embedding, it achieves a classification error rate about 2% higher, indicating stronger anti-steganalysis performance than current SOTA methods.

items.title: Implementation and Software-in-the-Loop Evaluation of a Trans-Domain Digital Twin Architecture for Autonomous Guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV Without Online GNSS
items.summary: Autonomous UAV guidance in emergency response, infrastructure monitoring, and cargo transportation requires reliable navigation. However, satellite-based positioning may become unavailable or unreliable in enclosed spaces, blind spots caused by natural obstacles and structures, and environments affected by radio interference and signal spoofing during electronic warfare. This study designs, implements, and evaluates a system based on a Trans-Domain Digital Twin (TDDT) for autonomous guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV. Independent navigation, flight dynamics, and meteorological models are coordinated within a cycle of state estimation, prediction, decision-making, command execution, and feedback. Data from inertial, magnetic, pressure, and airspeed sensors, together with environmental information, form the basis for estimation and prediction. Furthermore, a shared state, temporal synchronization, preservation of information provenance, and command traceability establish continuity between models and decisions. The system was tested with a simulated physical twin in a software-in-the-loop environment. Vertical takeoff, movement toward the destination, landing, and autonomous stopping were recorded, and the dynamic model was adjusted to a limited extent based on sensor-derived feedback. Separating the evaluation reference from navigation inputs enabled independent assessment of positioning error and computational performance. The results confirm operational coordination, decision traceability, and closed-loop guidance under the tested conditions, providing a reproducible platform for the development and evaluation of navigation without satellite-based positioning.

items.title: From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling and Analysis of Dense LEO Satellite Networks Using an Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process
items.summary: In dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, several accessible satellites cover the same location. A footprint therefore identifies where communication is feasible but does not determine which satellite serves each user. The service region of a satellite, namely the set of locations it serves, governs satellite load, resource sharing, and user throughput. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, we model each service region as the intersection of a satellite's spherical-cap footprint and its spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. We then use Palm calculus to derive exact expressions for the mean area and perimeter and a coverage--load identity. After coverage saturates, mean area and load decrease inversely with population. In contrast, adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting mean perimeter. We connect this geometry to an approximate noise-limited user rate. Along the tested densification paths, the increase in user rate comes mainly from the decrease in mean satellite load rather than from the improvement of the serving link. We also compare the model with Walker constellations with Starlink-type parameters, using Cox parameters matched to the local orbit and satellite densities at each latitude. The model reproduces the mean area and perimeter of these constellations over broad latitude ranges, with larger differences near component maximum latitudes. These results show that service-region geometry, and hence satellite load and user rate, depend not only on the total satellite population but also on its allocation across orbital planes.

items.title: Combatting Fraud in Artificial Currency Based Government Benefits Programs
items.summary: Benefits programs are policy tools for providing targeted aid, such as food assistance or transit subsidies. However, these programs are often susceptible to misreporting fraud, wherein users misreport private attributes to obtain excess aid. To address this problem, we introduce a two-stage audit game between an administrator and users in which the administrator can audit users at a cost and levy fines on misreporting users, with player payoff structures designed to reflect real-world benefits programs. We show that the administrator's least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibria can be computed tractably via linear programming and derive prescriptive bounds on the administrator's excess payments and users' misreporting probability as functions of audit costs and fines. We further establish that, with an appropriately chosen budget level, the reduction in excess payments in any least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibrium offsets the audit budget required to sustain the mechanism, yielding total costs no greater than those of a baseline without an auditing authority, which we corroborate through a case study of Washington D.C.'s federal transit benefits program.

items.title: Effect of Transmission Line Switching on Damping of Interarea Modes
items.summary: This paper will explore the impact of switching transmission lines on the damping of interarea oscillation modes. This phenomenon played a central role in the 2025 Iberian blackout and in some North American oscillation events. The paper first assesses the effectiveness of line switching for enhancing mode damping by studying the problem in classical test power systems. The paper then tests these observations in realistic large-scale models of the Western Interconnection that represent recent real-time system conditions. It is shown that the switching of key transmission lines can have a significant impact on the damping of inter-area modes depending on system operating conditions.

items.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
items.summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.

items.title: FAS-Assisted Self-Interference Mitigation for In-Band Full-Duplex Communications
items.summary: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) communication relies on effective self-interference cancellation (SIC) to overcome the strong loopback self-interference (SI). While fluid antenna system (FAS)-assisted SIC offers superior SI suppression by dynamically selecting the FAS port to minimize the residual SI power, it incurs high pilot overhead to acquire channel state information (CSI) for both forward and loopback channels. This raises the question of whether forward channel CSI is necessary for effective SI mitigation. To address this challenge, we propose a pilot-efficient FAS-assisted SI mitigation (FAS-SIM) approach that selects the FAS port solely based on the loopback SI channel. Theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal is provided. Numerical results then reveal that FAS-SIM achieves SI suppression and a forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method, while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%, offering a low-overhead solution for IBFD communications.

items.title: Construction of Universal Safe Stabilizing Formulas with Weighted Centroid Methodology
items.summary: Control Lyapunov and control barrier functions ensure stability and safety, respectively, by imposing state-dependent affine constraints on the control input. Controller design can therefore be viewed as the problem of selecting an admissible input from the set defined by these constraints. This paper adopts this perspective and develops a weighted-centroid methodology for constructing explicit feedback formulas that are provably smooth. The selection method relies on the fact that weighted centroids of a convex set lie within the set. We establish conditions on the weight functions that guarantee smoothness and continuity for several classes of constraints, including single constraints, mirrored constraints, linearly independent multiple constraints, and two-constraint Gaussian constructions. The framework recovers Sontag's universal formula and generates other new explicit formulas. When specialized to control-theoretic settings, the resulting formulas yield smooth safety filters, stabilizing controllers, and safe-stabilizing controllers. Simulation and hardware experiments on a small quadrotor illustrate the practical benefits of the proposed construction.

items.title: StreamingDPD: A 1.28-GSa/s Instantaneous-Power-Gated Depthwise TCN Accelerator for Real-Time 320-MHz Digital Predistortion
items.summary: State feedback between successive samples limits the streaming throughput of recurrent neural networks for digital predistortion (DPD). We present StreamingDPD, an accelerator that processes 320-MHz signals at 1.28 GSa/s. Its 207-parameter instantaneous-power-gated depthwise temporal convolutional network (IPG-DWTCN) uses $|x[n]|^2$ to gate feature channels and causal dilated depthwise convolutions to model power amplifier memory. The network maps to a spatially unrolled fixed-point pipeline with shift-based quadratic activations and layer-wise mixed precision, sustaining one complex sample per cycle per lane. Its algorithmic cost is 554 floating-point operations per complex sample, 30.1% fewer than the recurrent baseline with the best linearization performance. In RF playback measurements on three power amplifiers driven by 40- to 320-MHz Wi-Fi 6/7 and 5G NR waveforms, IPG-DWTCN achieves the lowest mean adjacent-channel power ratio (ACPR) and ranks first or ties for first in mean error vector magnitude (EVM) against five neural baselines of comparable size. Four-lane FPGA hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 320-MHz 4096-QAM Wi-Fi 7 waveform achieve -45.82 dBc ACPR and -42.94 dB EVM at 1.28 GSa/s. At the same sample rate, post-layout evaluation of a single-lane 12-nm FinFET ASIC yields a 0.10 mm$^2$ core, a 52-cycle (40.63 ns) latency, and an estimated typical-corner power of 142.21 mW (111.10 pJ/sample). Relative to the prior 22-nm recurrent DPD ASIC, the design provides 5.1 times the throughput at about one-seventh the energy per sample.

items.title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation
items.summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) restoration models can reduce noise and motion artifacts, but they rarely estimate whether the restored waveform is reliable for downstream analysis. We propose TrustFlow-ECG, a reliability-aware restoration framework that combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow restorer with a lightweight window-level risk predictor. The predictor uses the noisy ECG, restored ECG, and correction residual, then applies validation-set isotonic calibration for selective ECG analysis. We evaluate on MIT-BIH ECG windows corrupted with NSTDB artifacts, powerline interference, and mixed noise across multiple SNRs, with an external 9,675-window PTB-XL stress check without retraining. TrustFlow achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, while calibration reduces ECE from 0.0385 to 0.0098. At 80% coverage, selective rejection reduces RMSE from 0.1848 to 0.1345, improves R-peak F1 from 0.8778 to 0.9175, and reduces HR MAE from 6.26 to 4.88 bpm.

items.title: Deliverable Frequency Regulation Reserve for VPPs via Transmission-Distribution Co-Simulation
items.summary: Aggregations of distributed energy resources can provide frequency regulation services. However, device-level power headroom may not accurately represent the power deliverable at the transmission-distribution interface. This paper proposes a bidirectional, storage-aware power-sharing framework for a virtual power plant (VPP). Delivery factors obtained from the perturbations used to construct the voltage-sensitivity matrix account for feeder losses and voltage-dependent loads, while battery energy limits and state-of-charge weights are included in the allocation. The framework is evaluated using the IEEE 8500-node feeder and IEEE 14-bus system. The proposed method tracks the feeder-head request within 2% compared with 23-26% over-delivery under the injection-headroom framework. It also sustains the requested power response 22% longer before reaching the storage energy limit. Moreover, communicating the updated VPP reserve to the transmission system operator reduces the post-transient integrated area control error by 80% relative to fixed reserve registration.

items.title: Lightweight Detection and Model Attribution of Synthetic Speech via Residual Statistical Fingerprints
items.summary: As speech generation technologies advance, so do risks of impersonation, misinformation, and spoofing. We present a lightweight, training-free method for synthetic speech detection and source model attribution. Our method builds on model-specific fingerprints that are computed as the average of the differences between audio signals and their filtered versions, referred to as residuals. Leveraging the Mahalanobis distance of the residual for a given audio signal to these model-specific fingerprints allows to identify the source model as well as to distinguish real from fake audio. A broad set of experiments across multiple synthesis systems and languages demonstrate a supreme performance of the proposed approach on four tasks: open-world single-model attribution, closed-world multi-model attribution, real vs. synthetic speech classification, and out-of-domain detection.

items.title: Speech Emotion Recognition Across Languages: Prosodic Patterns and Self-Supervised Learning
