To this end, we integrate an existing pretrained privacy-preserving prosody encoder into a speech synthesis model, enabling prosody-preserving speaker anonymization. By conditioning speech generation on prosody features, we find that human subjects more reliably perceive intended prosodic meaning, while anonymization performance is competitive with previous work.

items.title: Intervention-Robust VLA: Diverse Demonstrations for Robot Deployment with Safety Filters
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown strong potential for learning complex robotic behaviors from demonstrations. However, learning safe behavior directly from data requires extensive coverage of safety-critical situations, which is often impractical in real-world settings. Test-time safety filters provide an alternative by correcting unsafe actions during deployment, but these interventions can drive the robot into states poorly covered by the training data, thereby degrading task performance. We introduce InteR-VLA, an intervention-robust framework for VLAs that leverages diverse task-completing demonstrations to broaden task-relevant state coverage and maintain competence under safety interventions. By better aligning the training distribution with safety-filtered deployment under the same data budget, our approach mitigates intervention-induced distribution shift while preserving task performance. Real-world experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings show that InteR-VLA maintains safety, increases Safe Success Rate up to 90% from 0% for nominal policies, and consistently outperforms nominal-data training on both evaluated VLAs.

items.title: Control and Cryptosystem Co-Design for Encrypted Nonlinear Multi-Agent Coordination
items.summary: A cloud that must not see the agents' states can steer them on data encrypted under CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic. Its stored estimate admits only so many multiplications before a refresh that costs time and error, and every decrypted command is flooded with noise of a mandated size, constraints no controller designed in exact arithmetic meets. For networked agents with polynomial dynamics, we prove one closed-loop bound tying the controller and the cryptosystem in both directions. If the exact loop contracts on a region, the encrypted loop stays within a certified radius of it, set by the per-cycle and refresh errors, the refresh interval, the flooding and the delay. The errors and the bound's probability are derived from the library's circuits, not measured. Inverted, the bound turns the tolerance and a failure-probability target into the refresh interval, and with it the precision, security parameters and period. Conversely, costs shape the realization: a tracing backend tallies any pipeline's operations before a ciphertext exists, and evaluating the prediction about each agent's reference holds the released error below its sixteen-agent level. A full satellite-train mission encrypted at 128-bit security ran inside its certified radius, and the certificate holds across six graphs and at 32, 64 and 128 agents. Security enters the design twice, in time and precision. The cryptosystem is therefore part of the control design, derived from the same specification and certified by the same guarantee as the controller.

items.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration for Informative Sim-to-Real Adaptation
items.summary: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) can transfer agile robot skills from simulation to the real world, but closing the sim-to-real gap by domain randomization requires expert physics knowledge, and simulator calibration from real data typically targets a few hand-picked parameters. Even then, simulators miss real-world effects, and environments reconstructed from onboard perception inherit sensing errors that limit policy improvement. We propose Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), which uses conditional flow matching to calibrate simulator physical parameters and residual fidelity domains online during deployment. Residual fidelity captures sim-to-real dynamics discrepancies and perception-induced environment uncertainty. NFC operates in a latent space so that realistic environments can be sampled from the inferred posterior for real-to-sim policy fine-tuning. The framework is informative: the pretrained policy is fine-tuned only when an anomaly is detected, sequential NFC seeds its proposal from the simulation-pretrained estimator, and a hallucination policy modulates posterior uncertainty following optimism in the face of uncertainty. NFC attains the most accurate posteriors among established simulation-based inference methods on five robots with up to 39 physical parameters and a 128x128 residual terrain. On a wheeled robot with a broken wheel axle deployed on snow, mud, and wet grass, NFC raises success on rough terrain from 26% to 70% and reduces orientation jerk by 88%. Code and videos will be released upon publication.

items.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
items.summary: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.

items.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration: Turning Field Anomalies into Simulation Fine-Tuning
items.summary: A policy that transfers from simulation to a lab robot often fails in the field. Calibrating a simulator from real-world data typically targets only a few hand-picked parameters, and even calibrated simulators fail to capture unmodeled dynamics, while environments reconstructed via onboard perception inherit sensing noise and artifacts. We propose Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), a framework based on conditional flow matching that infers online, directly from a robot's execution data, both simulator physical parameters and residual fidelity - the remaining dynamics discrepancy and the gap between perceived and true environment geometry. A simulation-trained anomaly detector determines when recalibration or fine-tuning is required using onboard sensory signals alone, while an exploration policy actively modulates posterior uncertainty using optimism in the face of uncertainty. Across five robot platforms with up to 39 calibrated parameters and a 128x128 residual terrain map, NFC achieves the most accurate posterior distributions compared to established simulation-based inference baselines. In physical outdoor experiments with a wheeled robot suffering an axle failure across snow, mud, and wet grass, NFC increases rough-terrain navigation success from 26% to 70% while reducing orientation jerk by 88%.

items.title: Physiological Information Reliability: Contextual-Bandit Allocation of Coding Redundancy and Computation in Multimodal Cardiovascular Sensing
items.summary: A packet can arrive intact and still be nearly worthless. On a body-worn node the radio and processor share one small battery, yet ECG and photoplethysmography (PPG) windows differ widely in how much an estimator can recover from them. We propose Physiological Information Reliability (PIR): a hand-designed window-value proxy, PIV, built from signal quality and cross-modal heart-rate agreement, joins channel, energy and compute telemetry in one state vector, and a LinUCB bandit chooses coding redundancy and processing site. Over 25 paired seeds on a synthetic burst-erasure testbed, PIR-LinUCB used 4.3% less energy than a hand-written rule, with lower error and higher delivery. A rule that also reads PIV matches it on error and delivery but spends 3.7 mJ more per window. On five real fetal ECG recordings, PIV tracked heart-rate error better than signal quality alone (mean within-record Spearman $ρ= -0.50$ against $-0.40$). The evidence is simulated, small and non-clinical.

items.title: Granary-v2: Scalable Multilingual Speech Data Curation for Predictable and Controllable Model Outputs
items.summary: Speech-language models that follow instructions need training data that connects the same recording to different output forms and tasks. We present Granary-v2, a multilingual speech dataset and reusable curation system that provides a data foundation for these models. Granary-v2 extends Granary-v1 with aligned transcript variants and instruction-target pairs for multi-task speech-language training. Language coverage increases from 25 to 48 languages. Built with NeMo Curator, the system combines language-dependent ASR labeling, transcript improvement, and text label generation. It produces aligned targets for speech-faithful transcription, written forms with and without disfluencies, and code-switched transcription. Additional targets include transcript-derived captions and question-answer pairs, with context and translations for selected records. The full processed collection contains approximately 843,600 unique audio hours, with translations covering about 142,800 hours into English and about 55k hours of English audio into 31 target languages. We evaluate label-quality filtering with two English Transformer-TDT models under the same training-step budget. Filtering reduces the unweighted mean word error rate across nine benchmarks from 4.91% to 4.67%, with improvements on six benchmarks. We also report curation throughput and downstream ASR and speech translation results from Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, which uses Granary-v2 as part of its training data. We release the Granary-v2 pipeline, built with NeMo Curator, and model training recipes as open source. We release a public subset of the generated labels and instruction-target pairs through Hugging Face.

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems. Technical validation covered signal integrity, numerical checks on feature estimators and completeness of the released files. In every task, the median proportion of recording time retained after preprocessing was 100%. To illustrate reuse, we report saved participant-held-out evaluations comparing XGBoost using all seven families on eight-second windows with a predictor based only on recruitment-group prevalence in the training fold. Recruitment-group discrimination was stronger in Robots than in the three Slackline conditions. These descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity. The dataset, curation software and aggregate results for the predictive example are publicly available.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning for Prediction of Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in Head and Neck Cancer
items.summary: To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-aware multimodal learning framework for predicting radiation-induced xerostomia in patients receiving head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy. We developed a Bidirectional Attention-enhanced Diffusion Transformer (BA-DiT) that combines self-supervised multimodal representation learning with supervised Bayesian fine-tuning. The model integrates pretreatment CT images and three-dimensional dose distributions, focusing on bilateral parotid glands while incorporating surrounding anatomical and dosimetric information. During pretraining, bidirectional cross-attention integrates anatomical and dosimetric features, while a latent Diffusion Transformer learns joint representations through diffusion-based learning, feature reconstruction, and contrastive alignment. Supervised fine-tuning employs a Bayesian classifier to predict individualized xerostomia risk and quantify predictive uncertainty, with a learnable label-transition model accounting for potential toxicity label uncertainty. BA-DiT was developed using four independent cohorts (Moffitt, Emory, MSHS, and TCIA) and evaluated against baseline and ablation models. Evaluation included predictive performance, calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision curve analysis, and patient-level case studies. In independent MSHS and Emory cohorts, BA-DiT achieved AUCs of 0.83 and 0.80, respectively, outperforming baseline models. Predictive uncertainty peaked near the decision boundary, with aleatoric uncertainty being the predominant component. Uncertainty-based selective prediction generally improved net benefit among retained patients, with greater gains at lower prediction coverage. BA-DiT enables individualized xerostomia risk prediction while providing complementary uncertainty estimates, potentially supporting informed clinical decision-making and personalized toxicity management.

items.title: Control Barrier Functions in Motion Control
items.summary: Projection-based controllers (PBCs) have significant engineering success in industrial high-precision motion systems by restricting their input-output behavior to performance-enhancing sector-sets thereby overcoming fundamental limitations of linear control. The projection results in continuous control signals, but their vector fields are discontinuous, potentially causing unwanted excitation of higher-order dynamics in the plant. Inspired by these projected controllers and the recent interest in control barrier functions (CBFs), we propose a new class of CBF-based motion controllers that (i) can mimic and exceed the performance benefits demonstrated by PBCs and (ii) have continuous dynamics thereby resulting in smooth control signals. We specialize our novel CBF-based control design to integrator dynamics, essentially connecting to a projected integrator, called Hybrid Integrator-Gain System (HIGS), thereby introducing CBF-HIGS. We analyze the CBF-HIGS's behavior using a describing function analysis, which reveals improved phase characteristics and a favorable trade-off in higher-order harmonic distortion compared to HIGS. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that CBF-HIGS enhances disturbance attenuation and reduces the excitation of higher-order harmonics compared to HIGS due to its continuous vector field, without compromising robustness properties. The paper provides the first use of CBFs for performance improvement of mechatronic motion systems.

items.title: What Graph Unlearning Cannot Erase: Physics-Induced Leakage of Cyberattack Information in Electric Vehicle Charging Networks
items.summary: Electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) can expose distribution feeders to cyberattacks. While machine learning methods, including graph neural networks (GNNs), can localize which bus is compromised, significant challenges remain in data sharing and model training. For example, data-sharing agreements grant EVCS operators the right to withdraw their charging power for privacy or security reasons from a deployed model, yet retraining from scratch on every request would repeat the full-retraining (FR) cost. To address this, we study graph unlearning (GU) for EVCS cyberattack localization, formulated as a feature-level unlearning problem on a graph-level multi-label classification task. We benchmark fine-tuning (FT) against two GU baselines on the IEEE 34-bus, 123-bus, and 8500-node distribution networks across three GNN backbones and cumulative unlearning scenarios. Experiments show that a GNN unlearned or retrained without the withdrawn power still localizes cyberattacks at the forgotten EVCSs. This physics-induced leakage floor arises because a cyberattack on an EVCS also shifts the voltages of electrically coupled buses. The distribution system operator can thus promise an EVCS operator that the deployed GNN model no longer uses its charging power data, but the voltages still reveal cyberattacks at its EVCS.

items.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
items.summary: Small modular reactors (SMRs) are being considered as compact, high-energy-density power sources for future all-electric ships. In such systems, propulsion-load variations can propagate through the electrical network, turbine-generator set, steam generator, and reactor, producing coupled nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical transients. This paper presents an integrated dynamic load-following analysis of an SMR-powered all-electric ship with and without battery energy storage system (BESS) support. The model couples an integral pressurized water reactor, a once-through moving-boundary steam generator, a simplified turbine model, a synchronous generator, an AC shipboard electrical network, an asynchronous propulsion motor, and a grid-connected BESS. A propulsion-load reduction is applied through the motor torque command, and the responses of the SMR-alone and SMR+BESS configurations are compared. The results show that, without BESS support, the sudden decrease in propulsion motor power creates a temporary surplus between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand, causing a large over-frequency transient and rapid steam-cycle adjustment. With BESS support, the battery absorbs excess electrical power during the transient, reducing the frequency peak from approximately 61.1 Hz to about 60.06 Hz. The BESS also indirectly smooths the upstream steam-cycle and reactor responses, including steam flow, steam-generator pressure, feedwater flow, coolant temperature, reactivity, reactor thermal power, and steam-generator region lengths. These results demonstrate the importance of modeling nuclear-powered electric ships as coupled multi-domain systems and show that BESS integration can improve short-term load-following performance.

items.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
items.summary: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity. For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz the closed forms agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for the slope and the intercepts and to 10% for the bandwidth. They underestimate the group delay by a third. The response is tied to atomic constants, and the sensing volume escapes the Chu limit. However, the noise figure of a warm vapor rules it out as a general replacement for an antenna and low-noise amplifier.

items.title: Unsupervised End-to-End Array Calibration for Multi-Target Integrated Sensing and Communication
items.summary: In this work, we consider end-to-end calibration of an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) base station (BS) under gain-phase and antenna displacement impairments without collecting signals from predefined positions (labeled data). We consider a BS with two impaired uniform linear arrays used for simultaneous multi-target sensing and communication with a user equipment (UE) leveraging orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing signals. The main contribution is the design of a framework that can compensate for the impairments without labeled data and considering coherent receive signals. We harness a differentiable precoder based on the maximum array response in an angular direction at the transmitter and the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm at the sensing receiver. We propose an ISAC loss as a combination of sensing and communication losses that provides a trade-off between the two functionalities. We compare two sensing objective alternatives: (i) maximize the maximum response of the angle-delay map of the targets or (ii) minimize the norm of the residual signal at the output of the OMP algorithm after all estimated targets have been removed. The communication objective maximizes the energy of the received signal at the UE. Additionally, our framework leverages an approximation of the channel gradient that avoids the impractical knowledge of the gradient of the channel. Our results show that the proposed method performs closely to using labeled data and knowledge of the channel gradient in terms of sensing position estimation and communication symbol error rate. When comparing the two sensing losses, minimizing the norm of the OMP residual yields significantly better sensing position estimation with slightly increased complexity.

items.title: Terrain-Aided Navigation Without Raycasting: A Sliding Grid Approach for Point Cloud Processing
items.summary: We investigate the use of a point cloud measurement in terrain-aided navigation. Our goal is to aid an inertial navigation system, by exploring ways to generate a useful measurement residual for effective nonlinear state estimation. We compare two such measurement models that involve the scanning of a digital terrain elevation model: a) one that is based on typical ray-casting from a given pose, that returns the predicted point cloud measurement from that pose, and b) another computationally less intensive one that does not require raycasting and we refer to herein as a sliding grid. Besides requiring a pose, it requires the pattern of the point cloud measurement itself and returns a predicted point cloud measurement. We show that the sliding grid achieves comparable accuracy to raycasting, especially at higher altitudes, while being orders of magnitude faster computationally. By eliminating the need for raycasting, the sliding grid removes the dependency on dedicated GPU hardware or high-performance CPUs, making it well-suited for real-time terrain-aided navigation on resource-constrained embedded platforms.

items.title: FR3-Band Capacitive-Piezoelectric Thin-Film LN Resonator for Heterogeneous Integration
items.summary: This letter presents a capacitively coupled piezoelectric lateral-field-excited bulk acoustic wave resonator (XBAR) in single-crystal lithium niobate (LN) for frequency range 3 (FR3, 7.125-24.25 GHz). We develop a platform that simultaneously maintains high electromechanical efficiency (\(k_t^2\)) and quality factor (\(Q\)) while alleviating challenges associated with parasitic galvanic interconnections and is fit for heterogeneous integration above integrated circuits. A 100 nm air gap excites the second-order symmetric Lamb wave (S2) mode in a 500 nm thick periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) LN from a fused silica substrate via flip-chip bonding, yielding a resonance frequency (\(f_s\)) of 7.16 GHz with an extracted \(k_t^2\) of 12.25\% and \(Q\) of 100, facilitating a high \(Q\cdot k_t^2\cdot f_s\) product of 87.71. The results demonstrate strong piezoelectric transduction through a nanoscale air gap, supporting further development of the platform for heterogeneous integration of compact, low-loss microwave components.

items.title: Asymmetric Phase Coding Audio Watermarking
items.summary: The proliferation of deepfake audio challenges voice-based authentication, and passive forensic detectors are sensitive to evolving generative models and to real-world channel distortions. We propose Asymmetric Phase Coding (APC), a training-free cryptographic signing layer for audio that anyone holding the public key can verify offline, designed as a compact and auditable provenance primitive that can stand alone or be stacked with learned watermarks. APC combines Ed25519 digital signatures (EdDSA, FIPS 186-5; 64-byte signatures) with Reed-Solomon error correction, pseudo-random STFT phase-bin selection, and a redundant quantization-index-modulation (QIM) code on log-magnitude differences of adjacent bin pairs, yielding a compact, non-repudiable, blind-extractable watermark. A successful verification proves who signed the embedded message and that the message is intact. On 1,905 LibriSpeech test-clean clips (10 s, 44.1 kHz) under eight attack configurations (identity, 10% and 20% end-cropping, 8 kHz low-pass, 16 kHz round-trip resampling, FLAC, MP3 at 128 kbps and OGG-Vorbis at 128 kbps), APC verifies 98.3% to 99.8% of clips on every condition at an identity PESQ of 3.82 and accepts no wrong-key or unsigned clip. On 2,048 clips from 18 sets of 15 public corpora spanning music, meeting, telephone, multilingual and mostly vocoded speech, it verifies between 97.1% and 99.4%. It also survives platform processing chains, repeated MP3 and OGG coding at 128 kbps, cropping up to bounds predicted in closed form, integer time shifts through an optional decoder-side search, and the DNS64 and DeepFilterNet3 speech enhancers on most clips, and it verifies a signed 10 s clip in 3.17 ms on one CPU core. We compare APC with neural baselines (reproduced AudioSeal and WavMark, and published SilentCipher results), including a capacity-matched operating point, and show that it stacks with AudioSeal.

items.title: Emotion-Aware Prefix: Towards Explicit Emotion Control in Voice Conversion Models
items.summary: Recent advances in zero-shot voice conversion have exhibited potential in emotion control, yet the performance is suboptimal or inconsistent due to their limited expressive capacity. We propose Emotion-Aware Prefix for explicit emotion control in a two-stage voice conversion backbone. We significantly improve emotion conversion performance, doubling the baseline Emotion Conversion Accuracy (ECA) from 42.40% to 85.50% while maintaining linguistic integrity and speech quality, without compromising speaker identity. Our ablation study suggests that a joint control of both sequence modulation and acoustic realization is essential to synthesize distinct emotions. Furthermore, comparative analysis verifies the generalizability of proposed method, while it provides insights on the role of acoustic decoupling in maintaining speaker identity.

items.title: 20 GHz Longitudinal Surface Acoustic Wave Resonators in 100-nm X-Cut Lithium Niobate on Silicon Carbide
items.summary: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators above 15~GHz require a fast acoustic mode that retains strong electromechanical coupling ($k^2$). This work reports longitudinal SAW (L-SAW) resonators designed for high $k^2$ in 100-nm X-cut lithium niobate (LN) on 4H silicon carbide (SiC), operating up to 21.7~GHz and reaching a $k^2$ of 8.1\%, a maximum Bode $Q$ of 70, and a figure of merit (FoM) of 5.7 at 20.24~GHz. In this thin-film waveguide, shrinking the wavelength ($λ$) keeps the normalized LN thickness ($h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$) large, sustaining both $k^2$ and acoustic confinement. Conversely, increasing $λ$ from 292 to 471~nm lowers $h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$ from 0.34 to 0.21 and raises the L-SAW phase velocity from 6.32 to 7.05~km/s, within 1.1\% of the 7126-m/s shear-wave velocity of 4H-SiC. As the velocity approaches this limit, more of the acoustic energy spreads into the non-piezoelectric SiC, and $k^2$ falls from its 8.1\% peak at $λ= 322$~nm to 1.7\% at $λ= 471$~nm. No L-SAW resonance is observed for $λ\geq 518$~nm ($h_\mathrm{LN}/λ\leq 0.19$), where the mode becomes leaky. Overall, the FoM stays within 5\% of its maximum for $h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$ between 0.26 to 0.31, defining a design window for L-SAW resonators in thin LN on SiC at K-band and beyond.

items.title: Bayesian Bias Learning-Enabled Probabilistic Voltage Estimation with Unknown Uncertainty Modeling of DERs in Distribution Grids
items.summary: One key challenge in distribution system state es- timation is unknown input statistics from the growing inte- gration of distributed energy resources (DERs), which may largely deviate from Gaussian uncertainty. Existing model-based estimators often rely on the assumption that all inputs follow known Gaussian distributions, while data-driven methods suffer from overfitting and failure in out-of-distribution scenarios. This paper proposes a Bayesian bias learning (BBL)-enabled probabilistic voltage estimation method in distribution systems with unknown DER generation statistics. The proposed learning- enabled method consists of two stages: probabilistic uncertainty inference and computationally efficient voltage estimation. First, a physics-constrained probabilistic density inference network is developed to learn Gaussian mixture representations of DER generation from historical data. Then, the resulting probabilistic representations, treated as pseudo-measurements, are integrated into a BBL-enabled voltage estimator via a decomposition- and-parallelization mechanism. Furthermore, utilizing a linear analytical solution, the proposed BBL-enabled voltage estimator efficiently captures linearization-induced biases and attains ac- curate probabilistic estimation. By integrating learning-enabled probabilistic uncertainty modeling into the parallel estimation structure, the proposed method achieves uncertainty-aware scal- able voltage estimation. Case studies on two unbalanced IEEE distribution networks show that the proposed estimator achieves significantly higher accuracy and computational efficiency under unknown uncertainty, outperforming recent data-driven and model-based methods.

items.title: EID-Net: Endoscopic Illumination-aware Degradation Correction Network
items.summary: Endoscopic images captured under complex illumination conditions often suffer from spatially non-uniform exposure degradation, including local under-exposure, over-exposure, and illumination-induced color variation. These degradations are usually entangled with tissue structures, making it challenging for general-purpose low-light enhancement and image restoration methods to improve visibility while preserving local structural and chromatic cues. In this paper, we propose EID-Net, an endoscopic illumination-aware degradation correction network for structure-preserving endoscopic illumination correction. Rather than treating illumination correction as a global intensity adjustment, EID-Net explicitly extracts an endoscopy-oriented degradation prior from the input image to characterize illumination-related variations in a unified representation. This prior is then introduced into the decoder through an illumination-modulated transposed attention mechanism, where it adaptively guides feature aggregation by modulating the key-value feature subspace. Extensive experiments on CEC, Endo4IE, EndoVis17, and EndoVis18 datasets demonstrate that EID-Net performs favorably against recent endoscopic enhancement and general image restoration methods. The code is available at https://github.com/JUNZHIlius/EID-Net.

items.title: A Spatial Clustering and Resource Allocation Approach for Critical Services in Massive MIMO-Enabled Cellular Networks
items.summary: In this work, we address the challenge of providing quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees for critical real-time services in cellular networks where both real-time and non-real-time applications must be supported. Leveraging the spatial multiplexing capabilities of Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology, we propose a joint clustering and resource allocation framework that limits network interference and enhances the ability to meet the QoS requirements of real-time services while still serving other applications. Our approach begins by clustering active users according to the direction of their channel vectors. Specifically, a downlink probing strategy is employed to group users whose channels lie in the same direction. Channel estimation and the derivation of the corresponding signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) are then performed based on this clustering. Subsequently, we formulate a resource allocation optimization problem across the user groups to satisfy the required QoS for critical real-time services while accommodating the remaining users. We rigorously prove that, in general, finding the global optimum of the resource allocation problem is NP-hard, and for a special case of the formulated problem, we establish a polynomial-time solvable algorithm based on linear programming. We then propose a suboptimal solution for the general problem using a linear relaxation technique. Simulation results are provided to confirm the effectiveness of our proposed approaches.

items.title: Underwater Spectral Recovery via Multi-View Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Underwater imaging suffers from wavelength-dependent absorption and scattering that distort scenes and obscure spectral signatures. While RGB restoration improves visual clarity, the outputs remain broadband and tied to the sensor's color space. We introduce a physically grounded framework that lifts underwater restoration to continuous spectral radiance using multi-view hyperspectral imaging. By representing continuous spectra via low-rank basis functions and leveraging multi-distance observations, our framework jointly constrains scene radiance and water parameters. We employ a robust sparse-to-dense pipeline: water parameters are estimated from consistent multi-view matches and then applied globally to invert the light transport model across the full images. Validated on physics-based synthetic data rendered via the Mitsuba 3 spectral path tracer, our method recovers physically meaningful radiance spectra and, as a downstream application, outperforms standard image restoration baselines.

items.title: Simplifying Gas-Phase Kinetic Measurements with a Dual-Arm Flow Tube
items.summary: We demonstrate a simple dual-arm flow tube reactor that provides well-defined reaction times ranging from one second to several minutes for gas-phase kinetic measurements near ambient temperature and pressure. Constructed entirely from standard tubing, the flow tube reactor eliminates the need for injector translation. It operates in two configurations: a variable-length configuration, in which the tube length is changed at fixed flow, and a variable-flow configuration, in which an exhaust branch allows the flow through the reaction section to be adjusted while maintaining constant reactant inlet flows. With 3.96 mm i.d. tubing, the measured tracer pulses had a typical full width at half maximum of about $10\%$ of their mean arrival time. A kinetic demonstration using the ozonolysis of 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene (TME) yields an apparent rate coefficient for TME loss $k_{\mathrm{app}} = 2.0(5) \times 10^{-15}\,\mathrm{cm}^{3}\,\mathrm{molecule}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. Fitting the same kinetic data with a reaction network including secondary OH and peroxy-radical chemistry yields $k = 1.18(19) \times 10^{-15}\,\mathrm{cm}^{3}\,\mathrm{molecule}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at 293 K for TME + $\mathrm{O}_{3}$, consistent with the IUPAC recommendation. This compact, low-cost reactor provides an alternative to conventional movable-injector flow tubes for atmospheric chemistry, fundamental kinetics, and gas-liquid or gas-solid uptake studies.

items.title: A Dual-Mode Protocol for Space-Time-Coding Metasurfaces in OFDM ISAC Systems
items.summary: Existing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks assisted by space-time-coding metasurfaces (STCMs) rely on idealized surface models, which neglect the frequency-selective and angle-dependent response of the meta-atoms, and are typically limited to narrowband single-carrier communications. This paper addresses these limitations by developing a physics-based signal-processing framework for STCM-assisted ISAC systems employing wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms, which accounts also for beam squint effects across the STCM aperture. On this basis, we propose a dual-mode protocol, in which the STCM operates as a time-varying surface during a short acquisition phase and as a conventional reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) during data transmission. In the acquisition phase, the angle of arrival (AoA) and the composite channel are jointly estimated by maximum likelihood from a single pilot OFDM symbol transmitted over a subset of active subcarriers, together with deliberately introduced virtual carriers; these estimates are then used to configure the RIS for data transmission. Numerical results validate the considered framework and quantify the gains achievable by the proposed dual-mode protocol.

items.title: Fault-Geometry-Aware Control Allocation for Emergency Quadrotor Landing under Single-Motor Loss of Effectiveness
items.summary: Partial single-motor loss of effectiveness (LoE) changes the remaining control-authority geometry of a quadrotor and can change which control allocator performs best during emergency landing. We compare three allocators in Crazyflie software-in-the-loop simulation: bounded weighted least squares (reported as PINV), a finite-candidate residual allocator (QP-lite), and the same residual allocator with scoring parameters tuned offline by the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM). For this study, fault geometry is represented by the known failed-motor index. At $η= 0.496$ remaining effectiveness, matched development trials select CEM for M1, M3, and M4 and PINV for M2; the M3 selection is a one-trial margin (29/30 versus 28/30). After freezing this routing map, the policy achieves 117/120 safe first-contact touchdowns on fresh seeds and 115/120 in a separate randomized-order integrated-supervisor evaluation. For the critical M2/PINV branch, Firth regression gives a nominal $η_{50} \approx 0.4956$ with a within-model 95% bootstrap interval of approximately $[0.4955, 0.4956]$. One-factor-at-a-time $\pm 10\%$ plant perturbations shift $η_{50}$ by up to $0.05495$ for thrust coefficient and $0.04974$ for mass; the most frequent violated first-contact criterion also changes from vertical speed in many conditions to angular rate for mass $-10\%$ and thrust-coefficient $+10\%$. At fixed $η= 0.496$, PINV has a higher M2 safe count than frozen CEM in 9/11 tested plant states and ties in 2/11; the two ties are both 0/30. The experiments therefore distinguish motor-conditioned allocator selection from sensitivity to plant-model mismatch.

items.title: Feasibility of Multifrequency Neural Network-Based Wave Inversion in Ultrasound Time-Harmonic Elastography
items.summary: Ultrasound time-harmonic elastography (THE) is a non-invasive imaging technique that measures soft-tissue stiffness. Relying on the same principle of time-harmonic shear wave excitation as established magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), THE offers full field-of-view stiffness mapping at short acquisition times and sub-second temporal resolution across organs. However, reconstruction of shear wave speed maps from acquired tissue wavefields remains challenging due to speckle noise and sparse spatial coverage of the lateral component. Deep learning methods have shown promising results for image reconstruction in transient-based ultrasound elastography modalities but remain unexplored in THE. In MRE, MF-ElastoNet, a 2D multifrequency neural network-based wave reconstruction method trained on synthetic physics-based wave data, has shown high generalizability across dynamic ranges and resolutions. We investigated the potential of a multifrequency neural network-based wave inversion for THE, by performing a first feasibility analysis. To this end, we adapted the processing pipeline of MF-ElastoNet from MRE to THE. We tested our approach on THE acquired phantom data from the algorithms for mapping elastic modulus Challenge, as well as on in vivo liver THE in 4 healthy volunteers and 14 patients with focal liver lesions, including benign focal nodular hyperplasia, and malignant hepatocellular carcinoma and adenocarcinoma. MF-ElastoNet was successfully adapted to THE with in vivo liver testing. Compared with k-MDEV, the state-of-the-art wave inversion method for THE, Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -0.02 m/s (95% limits of agreement: -0.36 to 0.33 m/s).

items.title: Optimal Uniform Pricing for Multi-Interval Dispatch without Make-Whole Uplifts
items.summary: In a network with ramp-limited generators and inaccurate net-demand forecasts, practical rolling-window dispatch can drive locational marginal prices (LMPs) below generators' bid-in offers. In such cases, out-of-market (OOM) settlements are used to compensate generators and maintain dispatch-following incentives, but OOM can have negative consequences, including nontransparent real-time price signals, discriminatory compensation, and incentives for untruthful bidding. This paper presents an optimal uniform pricing rule that minimizes demand payments, eliminates OOM make-whole payments, preserves LMP-based congestion charges, and ensures revenue adequacy. We derive the proposed pricing rule in closed form and relate it to existing pricing schemes. Numerical comparisons demonstrate favorable generator profits and reduced price volatility. However, higher generator profits are accompanied by increased demand payments, reflecting the in-market, uniform allocation of ramping costs while preserving the LMP-based congestion charges widely used in real-time market settlements. The numerical results also show that, under LMP with OOM settlement, a price-taking generator has an incentive to inflate its offer, whereas this incentive is absent under the proposed pricing rule within the tested bid range.

items.title: Eliminating Make-Whole Uplifts with a Minimum-Cost Uniform Price Adder
items.summary: Co-optimizing energy and flexible ramping reserves may dispatch generators at locational marginal prices (LMPs) below their submitted energy offer prices, necessitating out-of-market make-whole payments. Such payments create discriminatory settlements among generators and may incentivize strategic bidding for higher profits. This paper proposes LMP+U, an in-market uniform price adder to LMP for transmission-constrained networks, which minimizes demand payments subject to zero out-of-market make-whole uplift, preserves LMP-based congestion charges, and provides locally truthful bidding incentives for price-taking generators. We also identify conditions under which a price-taking generator can increase its profit by inflating its energy offer under conventional LMP with make-whole uplift. Numerical simulations illustrate the properties of LMP+U and its advantages over conventional LMP in congested networks.

items.title: Iteration-Dependent Temporal Resilience in Diffusion Models for Approximate Computing
items.summary: This paper empirically analyzes iteration-dependent resilience in diffusion models by replacing MACs with efficient SAC approximations. Results on Q-Diffusion show early steps are highly sensitive while later steps are robust, enabling iteration- aware approximation that improves efficiency and reduces hardware cost with minimal quality loss.

items.title: Passivity Correction of the Thermistor Model in Bolometric Power Sensors and Its Dependence on Bead Temperature
items.summary: This paper closes a series of works on thermistor bolometric power sensors, coaxial and waveguide, by treating what the two have in common. The per-state transformation m introduced in the waveguide work, which corrects the thermistor impedances of the model in each bridge state so that the two-port of the mount is passive, is analyzed on the eleven sensors of the preceding papers: the corrections are a few tenths of a percent in the coaxial mounts and one to two percent in the waveguide mounts, follow one pattern within each family, and the hottest state is the one whose efficiency departs most from the others. The transformation is tested by an independent measurement: the substituted powers of the three states, read with the manufacturer's procedure against a leveled source whose reflection is obtained from the closure of three Apollonius circles, give efficiency ratios of 0.999 +/- 0.016 and 0.997 +/- 0.008 (k = 2), which contain the values at the passivity floor (0.996, 0.998) and exclude those of the first pass (0.941, 1.023). Three sensors were swept in the bridge resistance, 23 and 31 states, and a fourth is treated apart: the correction reduces to one constant per state, the parallel resistance of the bead, represented by a law with one term scaling with the bridge resistance and one exponential in the bead temperature, with one thermal coefficient per family. The same property explains why the cross-ratio of four measured reflection coefficients, invariant under any state-independent two-port, departs from that of the four bridge resistances.

items.title: On Robust Strictly Positive Real Synthesis for High-Order Interval Polynomials
items.summary: We establish two complementary results on common strictly positive real (SPR) numerators for Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial families. First, for every order $n \ge 10$, we construct a monic Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial family with rational endpoints and positive width in every nonleading coefficient such that every nonzero real numerator of degree at most $n$ produces a strictly negative real part at some member and some positive frequency. In particular, robust Hurwitz stability alone does not guarantee equal-degree SPR synthesis in high orders. Second, for every order $n \ge 1$, we prove that a common real SPR numerator of exact degree $n$ always exists whenever the lower endpoint of each interior coefficient interval is at most $10^{-5}$ times its upper endpoint, while the constant and leading coefficients vary over arbitrary compact positive intervals.

items.title: Hierarchical Agentic Mid-Band Agility for Reliable Low-Latency Space-Air-Ground Integrated V2X Networks
items.summary: Upper-mid-band spectrum offers bandwidth opportunities for the integrated networks of ground vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to support 6G wide-area vehicle-to-everything (V2X) connectivity. However, V2X services' latency and reliability are sensitive to the mid-band selection due to frequency-dependent propagation and rain attenuation. This paper investigates environment-aware spectrum agility over candidate frequency range 3 (FR3) bands within 7.125-24.25 GHz, jointly with end-to-end (E2E) multi-path traffic splitting and transmit power control. Each data packet is partitioned into non-overlapping subflows over direct and UAV-assisted paths, with failed sky-link subflows selectively retransmitted subject to retransmission and freshness constraints. We formulate latency- and reliability-oriented problems, followed by a unified sequential optimization problem incorporating band-switching costs and average quality-of-service (QoS) violation budgets. To coordinate optimization decisions across heterogeneous timescales, we develop an agentic AI-assisted hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (AA-HMARL) framework. A high-level agentic supervisor integrates recurrent memory, analytical evaluation of candidate bands, and event-triggered replanning to coordinate slow environmental adaptation with fast channel and retransmission dynamics, while distributed ground vehicles and UAV agents optimize data splitting and power using constrained MAPPO. Simulation results demonstrate an adjustable reliability-latency trade-off. Particularly, AA-HMARL reduces the mean E2E completion latency and the mean number of retransmission rounds among successfully delivered updates by 17.8-25.5% and 57.6-61.5%, respectively, and reduces the mean age of information (AoI) by 12.7-14.6% relative to fixed-band MAPPO across two traffic types.

items.title: Set-Theoretic PAPR Reduction in Multi-Antenna Systems
items.summary: In this study, we propose an optimization framework for PAPR reduction in multi-antenna systems with beamforming. Unlike previous techniques, the proposed approach permits full control over the distorted symbol constellation via arbitrary (convex) constraints on the frequency domain symbols, while minimizing the PAPR at each individual transmit antenna. We propose an iterative algorithm based on an extrapolated alternating projection method, which relies on an iterative soft-thresholding subroutine to compute projections onto sublevel sets of the objective function, and we compare its performance to optimal solutions obtained with general-purpose convex solvers.

items.title: Geometrical Estimation of Electromagnetic Degrees of Freedom in Reflecting Environments
items.summary: The number of spatial degrees of freedom (NDoF) of electromagnetic communication channels in reflecting environments is investigated using a full-vector formulation based on dyadic Green's functions and equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents. The channel correlation eigenproblem characterizes the electromagnetic communication modes and their coupling strengths, while the leading-order NDoF is estimated geometrically from the receiver-accessible phase space volume in the electrically large regime. By combining two geometrical projection Jacobians, the phase space volume is related to the mutual shadow area, establishing the equivalence between the two geometrical NDoF formulations and yielding a two-polarization estimate equal to twice the mutual shadow area divided by the squared wavelength. The free-space mutual shadow formulation is extended to perfect electric conductor (PEC) reflecting environments through image construction and phase space ray tracing, accounting for specular reflections and geometrical visibility constraints. The formulation is validated against the eigenvalue spectra of full-vector electromagnetic channels involving planar PEC reflectors, a parabolic reflector, a parallel-plate waveguide, and a non-line-of-sight L-shaped corridor. The geometrical predictions agree with the observed spectral transitions across configurations involving multiple reflections, focusing, and blockage.

items.title: Planar Formation Control with Minimal Sensing and No Common Orientation: An Almost-Global Result
items.summary: Formation control based on geometric constraints often requires either rigid interaction graphs or a common orientation reference. This paper investigates whether a prescribed planar formation can instead be achieved using only $N-1$ pairwise interactions while preserving global rotational freedom. To this end, a guiding-vector-field-inspired framework is developed in which each selected distance relation is represented by a parameterized circular manifold and the remaining geometric freedom is coordinated through relative virtual phases, based on which, a distributed controller is then constructed. The closed-loop system is shown to possess only the desired equilibrium set and a degenerate undesired equilibrium set corresponding to collapse of the central edge. The latter is proved to form a saddle-type equilibrium manifold with a measure-zero stable set, yielding almost-global convergence to the desired formation. In addition, the controller admits an implementation under mutually misaligned local frames using locally expressed relative measurements and scalar phase information.

items.title: Unlocking Heterogeneous Accelerator Flexibility in AI Data Centers: Sizing and Workload Allocation
items.summary: AI data centers are an emerging electricity demand, but limited local grid capacity could delay their connection and expansion. While existing operational strategies consider spatio-temporal workload flexibility, few studies address the strategic sizing and allocation of diverse accelerator archetypes with different capital and energy-efficiency trade-offs. This paper unlocks the flexibility potential of heterogeneous accelerators by jointly sizing and allocating different AI workloads (training, delay-tolerant batch work, and online inference requests) across sites and hours to meet the time-varying grid constraint at minimum cost. Workload-specific throughput and energy coefficients link these decisions to facility power. In a representative two-site case, heterogeneous sizing reduces daily cost by 6.5% relative to spatio-temporal scheduling with fixed capacity. When evaluated using workload-specific performance, a capacity design based on workload-averaged hardware coefficients costs 7.7% more than the proposed design. The proposed design also eliminates the envelope violations of an unconstrained design at a 0.25\% daily cost increase. These results show how hardware heterogeneity and workload flexibility jointly shape economical, grid-compliant capacity plans.

items.title: Incentive-Based Regulatory Mechanism for Tariff Design in District Heating and Cooling Networks
items.summary: Low-temperature district heating and cooling networks exchange heat bidirectionally at near-ambient temperatures. When one supplier owns the shared loop, it controls both the tariff and the network temperature that sets every user's conversion efficiency. Existing price-cap and cost-based rules leave this non-price instrument unregulated and reach neither the first-best dispatch nor an explicit division of gains. This paper proposes a two-part, incentive-based tariff that anchors the supplier's lump-sum fee, per building and hour, to an audited outside alternative and divides the participation gains through one regulated share. We model a mixed-integer bilevel Stackelberg game in which the supplier sets hourly tariffs and the temperature regime, anticipating the buildings' co-optimization of electricity and thermal exchange. We prove that the mechanism attains the first-best welfare, posts the shadow price of the efficient dispatch as its tariff, keeps every building at or above its outside option every hour, and keeps the supplier solvent whenever operation adds surplus. A Belgian case study confirms these properties. The mechanism reproduces the centralized welfare whenever operation is worthwhile, declines to operate otherwise, holds the loop at its first-best temperature, and outperforms cap-based regulation and Ramsey pricing in welfare, user protection, and cost recovery.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics
items.summary: Start-ups and grade changes remain largely operator-driven, while developing and maintaining dynamic models for model-based control requires substantial engineering effort. Hybrid Offline Learning and Online Optimisation (HOFLON) uses one-step offline reinforcement learning to select actions from historical transition data. In its original implementation, the online objective combines the predicted return from a tree-ensemble critic with an adversarial-autoencoder (AAE) penalty for unfamiliar state-action pairs. We examine the effect of this penalty and replace the critic and AAE with a sparse variational Gaussian-process (sGP) critic. Actions maximise $μ- κσ$, an uncertainty-adjusted estimate of the return from one action followed by the historical operating practice. On the HOFLON polymerisation-reactor benchmark, removing the AAE from HOFLON led to 4 failed start-ups in 15 runs over five critics. At its published weight, the variation in the AAE penalty is four orders of magnitude smaller than the variation in the tree-ensemble critic. Nevertheless, it changes actions when the predicted returns of competing candidates are nearly equal, and paired runs with and without the penalty diverged from the first move. With a Matérn-5/2 sGP critic, $κ= 0$ led to failure in 13 of 15 runs, whereas with $κ= 3$ none of 15 runs (five critics, three noise realisations) failed. The median and lowest returns were 13,464 and 13,398 (HOFLON: 13,393 and 12,411). A squared-exponential sGP critic with learned inducing inputs needed $κ\geq 3$ to remain within the empirical data support in steady state, and then settled with a temperature offset of 2.0 K.

items.title: From Surface Lakes to Subsurface Signatures in Antarctica with BIOMASS P-Band TomoSAR
items.summary: Spaceborne remote sensing of the cryosphere is fundamental to map ice structure and dynamics. Accurate mass balance estimation requires a better understanding of melt/refreeze processes and firn hydrology, whereas spaceborne optical and Radar sensors are mostly limited to near-surface observations. The BIOMASS P-band Synthetic Aperture Radar, launched by European Space Agency in 2025, provides an unprecedented opportunity to gain a more direct access to englacial processes, thanks to the 70 cm wavelength paired with polarimetry, interferometry and tomography. This paper investigates subsurface beneath a region of historical supraglacial lake activity with BIOMASS tomography, at the Riiser-Larsen Ice Shelf in East Antarctica. The main result is that subsurface scattering appears to be related to historical supraglacial lake recurrence, with structural and depth variations over time. This suggests that recurrent supraglacial lake activity may leave persistent hydrological signatures within the firn. Overall, this study highlights the potential of gaining valuable insights into ice sheet hydrology with P-band.

items.title: TITAN: DRL-Based Dynamic Scheduling and Resource Allocation for Tactile Internet
items.summary: Tactile Internet (TI) applications require ultra-reliable, low-latency tactile communication alongside video traffic. However, tactile Quality of Service (QoS) requirements vary with the interaction context, making fixed resource allocation inefficient. In this paper, we propose TITAN (Two-Timescale Integrated Tactile Internet over 5G Access Networks), a dynamic scheduling and resource allocation (SRA) scheme. TITAN receives time-varying tactile QoS profiles from a higher-layer module and adapts SRA to the current QoS profile and network state. A deep reinforcement learning-based agent splits the available network bandwidth between tactile and video streams at a slow timescale, while a fast-timescale scheduler allocates resource blocks among active user equipment. Through simulations, we show that TITAN simultaneously satisfies both tactile and video QoS targets and achieves a performance gain of 7.64 percentage points (pp) in the joint satisfaction rate over the best-performing static SRA baseline.

items.title: From Tokens to Pixels: Training-Free Guided Upsampling of Frozen CARL Features for Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Camera-agnostic foundation models such as CARL map spectral images from arbitrary sensors into a shared feature space, but deliver their features only on a token grid at one eighth of the input resolution. The usual bilinear interpolation blurs material boundaries over about one token and rounds off corners. We investigate how much spatial accuracy image-guided upsampling recovers for frozen CARL features without training the encoder or the upsampler. We compare joint bilateral upsampling (JBU), a guided filter and the pretrained AnyUp, each with the hyperspectral image or an RGB rendering as the guide. A hyperspectral ColorChecker dataset acquired specifically for this study, with model-independent reference geometry measured to sub-pixel precision, serves as the evaluation benchmark. JBU with the hyperspectral guide raises the Boundary IoU from 13 to 67 % and reduces the effective edge width of the features from 38 to 4 px, close to the resolution of the raw spectra. The effect occurs in all 24 patches of the ColorChecker and replicates on an additional recording. On placenta and oral cavity images, the feature edges also become markedly qualitatively sharper. For sharp, high-contrast boundaries, JBU is the most accurate and most economical method. On tissue with softer transitions, the pretrained AnyUp yields qualitatively sharper contours. An analysis of 78 simulated band configurations shows that the gain persists in every configuration as long as the head matches the configuration. Image-guided upsampling is thus a simple, training-free step for applications that use CARL frozen with linear heads.

items.title: Where Delay Compensation Belongs in a Decentralized Mean-Field-Game Swarm with a Control-Barrier Safety Filter
items.summary: Large robot teams are often run as a plan-then-execute stack. We study a decentralized instance for drone swarms, a mean-field-game (MFG) routing field with a per-agent control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filter, when communication is limited by a shared TDMA channel. Neighbors are known only through noisy range and bearing measurements exchanged in round-robin slots, so the frame, and with it the age of every estimate, grows with swarm size. In simulation this delay reaches both layers but breaks only the safety layer. Without delay, swarms of up to 100 agents do not collide, even with each measurement's noise held for a whole frame; with it, stale estimates at the CBF cause collisions beyond a frame period of 125 to 175 ms, or 75 to 100 ms at 100 agents with held noise, and swarm size sets where that limit lies and how steeply collisions rise. At the MFG, staleness makes the local density noisier without biasing it, and throughput drops by at most a tenth. We then compensate with lightweight on-board predictors, from constant-velocity fits to a small learned network, that estimate each neighbor's position from its last broadcasts. A layer-split experiment shows where prediction is needed: at the CBF it restores safety and extends the tolerated frame period by 1.4 to 1.7 times with an untrained constant-velocity fit and about 2.3 with the learned network when the noise is redrawn each step; with noise held for a frame the two extend it about equally, while at the MFG it only refines the congestion correction. A constant wider safety margin, the simplest alternative, makes collisions more frequent in a bottleneck. With the routing solved offline, that layer is robust to the delay because it sees neighbors only through a crowd average; compensation belongs in the safety filter, switched on only above the uncompensated limit, since below it the predictor's own error adds collisions.

items.title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.

items.title: Beyond Outlier Rejection: Transient-Aware Reconstruction of Multi-Stack MRI
items.summary: Clinical MRI typically acquires the organ of interest as consecutive stacks of 2D slices in different orientations. Reconstruction methods such as SVRTK and NeSVoR fuse them into one volume and down-weight what does not fit, although in living tissue the change during the scan is often the signal itself and can contain clinically relevant physiological information, such as fetal motion and uterine contraction. We propose an analysis-by-synthesis decomposition that explains every acquired voxel through its exact acquisition geometry as a static anatomy shared by all stacks, a rigid and smooth non-rigid motion per stack, and a sparse transient field per stack for changes during one acquisition only. A robust reweighting keeps such changes out of the anatomy. The model is fitted per subject without training data, with one configuration for all datasets. On a digital phantom with known ground truth, static changes are kept entirely in the anatomy, and the transient field of the stack that saw a transient recovers 68% of it at 12mm radius. From identical inputs, the anatomy predicts held-out stacks better than SVRTK and NeSVoR on uterine (NCC 0.897 against 0.874 and 0.863, 123 patients) and on prostate MRI from unseen sites and scanners (0.847 against 0.795 and 0.757, 85 patients), and on fetal brain MRI as well as SVRTK and better than NeSVoR (0.771 against 0.763 and 0.747, 83 fetuses). The transient fields flag corrupted fetal slices with an AUROC of 0.94 against expert raters. As the input of a frozen anomaly detector trained on healthy subjects only, the anatomy localizes radiologist-delineated uterine lesions better than the SVRTK and NeSVoR volumes (AUROC 0.76 against 0.71 and 0.71, 37 patients).

items.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
items.summary: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. Users compare focal choices on one photograph, so content stability across edits matters alongside quality and speed. Recent generative methods rerun large diffusion models for every edit, even when they first restore an all-in-focus image, so content can change inconsistently between edits. Yet only this restoration is highly ill-posed and benefits from a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders each edit with a lightweight network. A one-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality. The renderer uses an explicit defocus map for control and defocus-bias attention to promote information exchange between tokens with similar blur magnitudes. Because every edit reuses the same reconstruction, in-focus content stays consistent across edits, and editing the map enables tilt-shift and two-plane effects. We further collect 3CReal, a benchmark of 89 pairs from three camera-lens systems, to evaluate generalization to unseen optics. For zero-shot bokeh rendering on EBB! Val176 and 3CReal, FlashReFocus leads the evaluated methods in fidelity and perceptual quality. At 1536x1536, a complete refocus takes 2.45 s and each subsequent edit 0.46 s on one RTX PRO 6000.

items.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
items.summary: Robots can be controlled to perform tasks with guaranteed correctness when the task instructions are stated in a formal language. Large language models (LLMs) have been widely used to allow users to provide such instructions in natural language (NL), by translating NL into formal language. When deploying such translators on a robot, however, we face limited computing and energy resources, while offloading computation or data to the cloud may be infeasible or undesirable. Yet an LLM is a general-purpose text generator, whereas a formula in a fixed formal language fragment follows a well-defined syntax. We therefore ask whether text generation is needed at all. For the formal language of linear temporal logic (LTL), we show that this translation can instead be broken down into answering a set of questions with pre-defined answers. We then construct a System-One model, a recent class of NL-based classifier, to provide such answers and enable us to translate a natural language instruction into an LTL instruction. On three benchmarks, our translator matches or exceeds the accuracy of the best local LLMs available, at up to one order of magnitude lower runtime and energy consumption. We show that it generalizes to unseen atomic propositions and temporal patterns.

items.title: Incentive-based Fleet Rebalancing in Vehicle-Sharing Systems via Equilibrium-Constrained Optimal Control
items.summary: We propose an incentive-based fleet rebalancing scheme for vehicle-sharing systems that uses fare discounts to steer users toward alternative pick-up locations. The discounts solve an optimal control problem that trades off users leaving the service against incentive costs over a day of operation. Users' responses to incentives are modeled as a Nash equilibrium of logit models coupled through shared vehicle-availability constraints, which makes the control problem a mathematical program with nested equilibrium constraints. We develop a first-order algorithm that backpropagates through the equilibria via nonsmooth implicit differentiation and enjoys convergence guarantees. In a case study that uses Helsinki bike-sharing data, our scheme reduces the number of leaving users by up to 99% relative to no incentives, and outperforms heuristic policies while using up to 52% less incentive.

items.title: Binary Decision Process in Pre-Evacuation Behavior
items.summary: In crowd evacuation the time interval before decisive movement towards a safe place is defined as the pre-evacuation phase, and it has crucial impact on the total time required for safe egress. This process mainly refers to situation awareness and response to an external stressors, e.g., fire alarms. Due to the complexity of human cognitive process, simulation is used to study this important time interval. In this paper a binary decision process is formulated to simulate pre-evacuation time of many evacuees in a given social context. The model combines the classic opinion dynamics (the French-DeGroot model) with binary phase transition to describe how group pre-evacuation time emerges from individual interaction. The model parameters are quantitatively meaningful to human factors research within socio-psychological background, e.g., whether an individual is stubborn or open-minded, or what kind of the social topology exists among the individuals and how it matters in aggregating individuals into social groups. The modeling framework also describes collective motion of many evacuee agents in a planar space, and the resulting multi-agent system is partly similar to the Vicsek flocking model, and it is meaningful to explore complex social behavior during phase transition of a non-equilibrium process.

items.title: Readiness Barrier Functions: Forward-Invariant Control Authority for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation
items.summary: Allocators that greedily maximize a readiness metric over the actuator fiber bundle of an overactuated multirotor jump between disconnected optimal strata, demanding actuator rates no motor can deliver; effort-minimizing allocators are continuous but cannot keep wrench-rate authority above any certified level. We reconcile the two by treating authority as a forward-invariant quantity: a control barrier function on the log-determinant of the drag-aware authority co-metric, enforced at torque level by a quadratic program in the allocation null space. A single design inequality makes the certified set compact and strictly interior to the actuator box; the readiness cost of a rotor deactivation is $\ln(n/(n{-}m))$ for symmetric designs. An alignment ratio states when tracking stays exact, otherwise the wrench error is $\mathcal{O}(ρ^{-1/2})$, and a robust variant handles motor-parameter uncertainty with a closed-form floor shift independent of the airframe matrix. On a hexarotor and a fully-actuated octorotor the closed-form gap matches simulation to machine precision. Over $300$ randomized missions, greedy maximization violates the certified floor in up to $51\%$ of authority-scarce missions, while the proposed filter never leaves the certified set and, in the hardest moment reversal, commits a $79\times$ smaller wrench error. The robust variant holds the floor on all $150$ perturbed plants. A high-fidelity simulation with measured propeller and motor data shows where the floor holds under unmodeled aerodynamics, electrical limits, and delay, and where it stops applying.

items.title: Beyond Scalar Inertia: Frequency-Response-Based Assessment of Finite-Duration Inertial Support in Grid-Forming Converters
items.summary: Conventional scalar inertia characterizes only the low-frequency terminal behavior of grid-forming converters (GFMs) and cannot fully predict inertial energy delivery during short-duration frequency disturbances. This letter proposes a frequency-response-based method to assess finite-duration inertial support using complex terminal power--frequency responses, such as those provided by Network Frequency Perturbation (NFP) plots. For GFMs with nonzero steady-state droop, a duration-dependent energy-equivalent inertia is defined after subtracting the ideal static-droop contribution. An exact spectral relationship is established, expressing this metric as a duration-weighted integral of frequency-dependent inertia, without requiring knowledge of the internal controller structure and parameters. The duration dependence of the metric is further shown to encode observable oscillation frequencies and damping ratios. A coefficient-decoupling GFM control with identical scalar inertia and droop across different settings is used for verification.

items.title: Learned Network Dynamics for Model Predictive Traffic Signal Control under Incidents
items.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) of urban traffic signals relies on a model of how queues respond to signal decisions, which is hard to specify and calibrate in heterogeneous networks, particularly when incidents change capacities and turning shares. Measurements add a second limitation: the controlled lanes at the stop line are often short, so queues extending upstream of them fall outside lane-level measurements. We propose GNN-MPC, a receding-horizon controller that plans with action-conditioned network dynamics learned by graph neural networks. Phase sequences are coordinated across intersections by approximate best responses, with an acceptance test that keeps the predicted cost no higher than that of the initial plan. In microscopic simulation under non-recurrent incidents, GNN-MPC reduces travel time and increases completed trips relative to all tested controllers, on a homogeneous grid and a heterogeneous 21-intersection network. Controlled comparisons on the heterogeneous network distinguish the roles of observation and prediction. With nearly as many vehicles entering the network, GNN-MPC reduces travel time by 13% relative to MaxPressure with the same upstream measurement, and GNN-MPC without the upstream representation does not reproduce its performance. Under the same traffic measurements, planner and objective, replacing the learned dynamics with calibrated store-and-forward predictors increases travel time by 31-34%. Observing hidden demand and predicting its response to control are thus complementary requirements of network-level predictive control.

items.title: Linear Quadratic Control With Event-Based Control Actions: Performance Beyond Periodic Control
items.summary: This paper investigates linear quadratic (LQ) control for discrete-time stochastic systems to balance control performance and actuation rate. In our framework, the control input is sparse in time, and the actuation timings are determined in an event-based manner. We examine two types of problems: A sparsity-promoting regularization problem and a hard-constraint problem with a prescribed average actuation rate. Due to the combinatorial nature of these problems, finding optimal solutions is generally hard. Inspired by rollout algorithms in the context of dynamic programming, we develop a rollout-based approach to obtain tractable suboptimal policies. We show closed-loop stability and establish theoretical performance guarantees with respect to classical periodic control. Moreover, under additional conditions, we quantify the performance improvement over periodic control and prove that this improvement is strictly positive. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in balancing control performance and actuation rate.

items.title: Active Learning of Flows from Curve Observations using Gaussian Processes
items.summary: The active learning of real control systems requires informative roll-outs of controls. In this paper, we present a local optimization algorithm that finds the trajectory that most reduces uncertainty about the flow of a control system modeled by a Gaussian process. Therefore, we derive an approximation scheme for the posterior kernel of the Gaussian process after observing it on an entire continuous-time trajectory and establish a Pontryagin-type necessary condition for the optimizer. As the flow is unknown, the actual trajectory can deviate from the planned trajectory. We propose a trajectory planner that searches for the most informative control within a maximal allowed deviation horizon instead of a fixed time horizon. We show by trajectory-wise time rescaling that the underlying optimal control problem is equivalent to a fixed end time optimal control problem. Finally, we study both the fixed end time planner and the fixed maximum deviation planner in a numerical example and compare them with benchmarks.

items.title: Network Traffic Dynamics in Urban Low-Altitude Air Transport with Projected-Space Macroscopic Fundamental Diagrams
items.summary: The growth of Low-Altitude Air Transport (LAAT) systems calls for effective macroscopic modeling tools to manage dense drone traffic. The Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD) offers a promising framework for this purpose, but its conventional formulations do not directly account for the three-dimensional interactions and path deviations that characterize drone operations.
